When the stage's visit limit is reached while its last commit is still an open Red, the run MUST end at `needs_human` with a cause naming the open Red commit. Measured 2026-11-07: the check-per-file-coverage leg of the full aggregate took 3654.8 s in a fix turn's commit hook on bd-ib-tcfwol run 01M6VRQMXSRD, and 3765 s on bd-ib-akxkza, both longer than the fix node's 3600 s limit. Scenario 199 in `scenarios.md` exercises this paragraph.

**An implement, fix or review_fix turn's commits run the affected-tests gate.** A commit made by the implement stage's `commit_red` or `commit_green` node, or inside a `fix` or `review_fix` turn, MUST run, in the repository's commit hook, the affected-tests gate (`just check-changed`) on the change being committed, in place of the full check aggregate. When the change touches a file whose affected tests that gate cannot determine, such as a shared configuration file, the commit hook MUST run the full check aggregate instead. A change to the implement-work-item workflow graph, the bundled `workflow.fabro` or a repository's own fork of it, is a scoped change. Its affected tests are every test module that reads that graph file: one that names the file by its repository path or its file name `workflow.fabro`, or that imports a test-support module that names it. Selecting a test module that names a different `workflow.fabro` is permitted, because over-selection only runs more tests. The gate MUST run those test modules on the change, together with any tests its `.py` changes select. It MUST NOT report the change as having nothing to gate. When the gate cannot determine which test modules read the graph, the commit hook MUST run the full check aggregate instead. At a Red commit the gate is Red-aware: the staged test MUST fail exactly as the Red-Green commit protocol requires, and no passing test or coverage is demanded of that commit; at the Green amend and every later commit, the scoped tests and their coverage MUST pass. This is a scoped exception to the aggregate selection of the inherited pre-commit step ordering, under which any staged `.py` file routes through the full aggregate: the pre-commit steps and their order are unchanged, and outside these commits that selection is unchanged. The `janitor` stage MUST still run the full check aggregate once per visit on the run's tree before publication. This paragraph does not change the Red-Green commit protocol's own hook checks, nor the touched-test rules of "An agent stage's instructions and its publication boundary"; a commit made outside a factory turn keeps the repository's full commit hook. Measured 2026-10-26: every commit in these turns paid the full aggregate in its hook, about 24 minutes at two test workers and 12.5 at four, and repeated Green amends on bd-ib-od7v54 run 01M5V5KVG8J7 spent its whole six-hour wall budget in such passes. Measured 2026-11-07: a full aggregate in a `fix` turn's commit hook outlasted the 3600 s `fix` node limit twice in this repository (3654.8 s and 3765 s for its check-per-file-coverage leg alone). Scenario 255 in `scenarios.md` exercises this paragraph.

The `publish_draft` visit that follows a refresh-repair round is the visit
immediately after the `janitor` visit that follows a `fix` visit entered with a
refresh-repair brief; a `publish_draft` visit reached through a review-fix
round, or any other path, follows no refresh-repair round. On the visit that
follows a refresh-repair round, `publish_draft` MUST establish the run's
previously published head as the head the run's last completed
`publish_draft` pushed, read from the run's own record as the cancel record of
§"Dispatcher progress watchdog" reads it, when the run has recorded one, and
otherwise as the head named by the run's validated resume provenance; it MUST
NOT establish it from a local tracking ref. When origin has no tip for the
publish branch, or its tip is an
ancestor of the repaired head, `publish_draft` MUST push a plain fast-forward as
before. When the tip is not an ancestor of the repaired head and equals the
run's previously published head, `publish_draft` MUST republish the repaired
head with an explicit lease against the recorded remote head of this run's own
publish branch. Hooks MUST run normally during that push, and it MUST NOT use
`--no-verify`, bare force, or a rewrite of any other ref. A non-fast-forward of
the run's own published head is the expected result of a repair that rebased,
not evidence of a stale or foreign branch. When the tip is not an ancestor of
the repaired head and either differs from the run's previously published head
or that head cannot be established, `publish_draft` MUST keep failing closed
with its existing divergent-prior-run cause and MUST NOT push. A
`publish_draft` visit that follows no refresh-repair round MUST NOT rewrite the
publish branch.

**Declared record files merge without a repair round.** A repository MAY declare, in its committed `.livespec.jsonc` under `dispatcher.record_files`, the shared record files that many changes extend independently. Each entry names a repository-relative `path` and a `format`. The format is `json-array` for a file holding one JSON array of objects, and an entry of that format also names `key`, the list of fields whose values identify one object. The format is `markdown-insertions` for a Markdown file. Any entry MAY also name `generator`, a non-empty argv array run from the repository root that rewrites the file at `path` from the repository's tree. A file whose entry names a generator is a GENERATED record file. Its correct content is its generator's output over the tree it sits in, so a conflict in it is never resolved by merging its text, on any route. An absent key declares no record files. When the rebase or merge of the janitor's pre-aggregate refresh or of `pr_refresh` conflicts, and every conflicted path is a declared record file, the stage MUST first attempt an entry-wise three-way merge of each conflicted file. It compares the file at the merge base, at the default-branch side and at the run's side. For a `json-array` file, each object is identified by its `key` values. An object that one side added, changed or removed takes that side's result, and an object that both sides left alone stays as it is. The merge is resolvable only when no object was added, changed or removed differently by both sides, and when the merged array parses and holds no two objects with the same key. The merged array keeps the default-branch side's order, followed by the run's added objects in the run's order. For a `markdown-insertions` file, the merge is resolvable only when each conflicting region consists of lines that each side inserted at the same position, with no line of the merge base changed or removed by both sides. The merged region holds the default-branch side's inserted lines followed by the run's inserted lines. When every conflicted file is resolvable, the stage MUST write the merged files, MUST continue the rebase or merge to completion, and MUST then proceed exactly as after a refresh that did not conflict. A conflicted generated record file is not merged entry by entry. The stage MUST first resolve every other conflicted path by this paragraph, then MUST run the file's generator over that tree and write its output as the resolution. The file is resolvable exactly when the generator exits zero. The stage MUST record each file it resolved this way, with the generator it ran, in the run's output for that stage. The repository-declared gate runs on the refreshed head. In `pr_refresh`, a rebase whose only conflicts this paragraph resolved counts as applied without conflict for "Proof carry-forward across a refresh", and the deterministic decision of that paragraph then decides whether the verified proof covers the new head or the run re-proves. Such a merge is not a refresh-repair round and MUST NOT count toward "Refresh-repair accounting". The stage MUST record each file it merged this way, with its format and the number of objects or lines it took from each side, in the run's output for that stage. A conflict in any path that is not a declared record file, a declared file that is not resolvable, or a merged head that the gate rejects takes the refresh-repair route above unchanged, with the pre-refresh head restored. The Dispatcher's merge wait reads `dispatcher.record_files` only through the record-file arm of "Armed pull request overtaken by the default branch"; this paragraph changes no other behaviour of the merge wait. Scenario 200 in `scenarios.md` exercises this paragraph.

**A refreshed head carries its generated record files as generated.** Before the repository-declared gate runs on a head that the janitor's pre-aggregate refresh produced or that `pr_refresh` refreshed, by any route, the stage MUST run the generator of every declared generated record file over that head's tree and compare its output with the committed file. A file whose committed bytes differ from its generator's output MUST fail the stage as a failed gate target named `generated-record-file:<path>`, which takes the refresh-repair route with that target in the brief. A head that passes this check therefore carries every row its generator derives from the merged source, including rows the default branch added while the run was in flight.

**Refresh-repair accounting.** A refresh-repair round is counted once, at the
moment a stage routes to `fix` with a brief. A run MAY take at most two
refresh-repair rounds in total across the janitor's pre-aggregate refresh, `pr_refresh` and `publish_draft`; when a
third refresh would need repair, the stage MUST fail closed to `needs_human`
with the named cause `refresh-repair-exhausted` and a recovery artifact pointer
naming that stage's pre-refresh head. A refresh-repair round MUST NOT consume
`dispatcher.review_fix_cap` or any review-fix round. `pr_refresh`'s
three-refresh non-convergence bound counts each counted refresh as
"Scripted publication and proof-head integrity" defines it, once at that visit;
any other clean refresh does not count; the janitor's pre-aggregate refreshes,
repaired or not, do not count toward that bound, and the re-entry of
`janitor` after a repair does not count a second time for the refresh
that was repaired. The `fix` node's visit limit MUST accommodate the two
refresh-repair rounds in addition to the rounds its other entry paths already
allow. The visit limits of `pr_refresh`, `pr_refresh_head`, `pr`, `pr_route` and every node on the proof loop MUST accommodate the entries the `pr` to `pr_refresh` route adds beyond the three counted refreshes, so that the ratified non-convergence cause, and not an engine visit cap, ends a run that keeps meeting an advanced default branch. A refresh that applies cleanly and passes the gate is unchanged by this
paragraph or the one before it. Scenario 176 in `scenarios.md` exercises both
paragraphs.

**Proof carry-forward across a refresh.** When `pr_refresh` has refreshed the
run onto an advanced default branch cleanly — the rebase applied without
conflict, the repository-declared gate passed, the leased push succeeded, and
no refresh-repair round ran during this visit — and the head changed, the stage
MUST decide, before routing, whether the run's verified proof still covers the
new head. The decision MUST be computed by a deterministic rule from repository
and record state alone; no language-model judgement MAY take part in it. Its
inputs are: the *verified record*, the latest `verified` record on the pull
request attributable to this run (including identifiers a resume links to it);
the *verified head* and *verified base*, the head that record names and that
head's merge base with the default branch; the *previous base* and *new base*,
the default-branch commits the run was based on before and after this refresh;
the *new head*; the *incoming paths*, the output of `git diff --name-only
--no-renames <previous base> <new base>`; the *item paths*, the output of `git
diff --name-only --no-renames <verified base> <verified head>`; the
*observation scope* defined below; and the *inert classes*, which are exactly
the plan store `plan/`, the directory `<spec_root>/history/` where
`<spec_root>` is the `spec_root` value of `.livespec.jsonc`, and the directory
`<spec_root>/templates/<name>/history/` for every `<name>` directory present at
the head being examined. A path is *beneath* a class when it begins with that
class's directory prefix. The *patch identity* of a range `<base>..<head>` is
the first field printed by `git diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-renames
--full-index <base> <head> | git patch-id --stable`, and is not computable when
that prints nothing.

**The observation scope.** The rule MUST establish the observation scope
positively from the verified record's numbered reproduction steps, and MUST NOT
infer it from paths the item's prose mentions or omits. Each step MUST carry
exactly one command, which the rule splits into words by POSIX shell quoting
rules so that every word is a literal argument. A step is *outside the
direct-read grammar* when it has no command or more than one command; when,
outside single quotes, its command contains any of `|`, `;`, `&`, `<`, `>`,
`$`, a backtick, `\`, `!`, `*`, `?`, `[`, `~` or a newline; or when
double-quoted text in it contains `$`, a backtick, `\` or `!`, so that no
expansion, substitution or hidden read can occur anywhere in the command,
quoted or not. The verified record MUST state, ahead of its numbered steps, the
line `Working directory: .`, meaning every step ran from the repository root; a
verified record without that line, or naming any other working directory, makes
every step outside the grammar. `proof_capture` and `proof_verify` MUST write
that line into their record exactly when every one of its steps ran from the
repository root. A command is inside the grammar only when it matches one of
these productions exactly, where a *file operand* is a word that does not begin
with `-` and every `<count>` is a word of decimal digits: `cat` followed by one
or more file operands; `head` or `tail`, optionally followed by `-n <count>`,
then one or more file operands; `wc`, optionally followed by one of `-l`, `-w`
or `-c`, then one or more file operands; `grep` followed by options drawn only
from `-n`, `-c`, `-i`, `-F`, `-E`, `-x`, `-w`, `-v`, `-o`, `-A <count>`, `-B
<count>` and `-C <count>`, then either `-e <pattern>` or one pattern word that
does not begin with `-`, then one or more file operands; `sed -n '<script>'`
whose script consists only of line numbers, line ranges and the `p` command,
followed by one or more file operands; `diff`, optionally followed by `-u`,
then exactly two file operands; or `git show HEAD:<path>` with exactly that one
argument, whose file operand is the `<path>` component after `HEAD:`. A command
that reads no file operand, and so would read standard input, is outside the
grammar. The file operands are the step's *path operands*. Each path operand
MUST be canonicalized by interpreting it relative to the repository root,
rejecting it when it is absolute, empty or contains a `..` segment, and
collapsing `.` segments and repeated separators; at both the verified head and
the new head, every leading component of the canonical path MUST be a directory
that is not a symbolic link, and the canonical path itself MUST name a regular
file that is not a symbolic link, so the checked path is the path the command
reads. The observation scope is the set of canonical path operands across every
step. When `proof_verify` executes a working-tree read, it MUST record, for
each of that command's path operands, one *read identity* line `Read:
<canonical path> <identity>` in its record, where `<identity>` is the output of
`git hash-object --no-filters <path>` for the working-tree file it read, taken
in the same execution; a missing or unparseable read identity line makes the
decision `reproof_required` naming that path. Any step outside the grammar, and
any path operand rejected or not naming such a file, makes the decision
`reproof_required` naming that step.

**The decision.** Except as **Release bookkeeping** below provides, the decision MUST be `carried_forward` only when all of the
following hold: every step of the verified record is inside the direct-read
grammar; every incoming path is beneath an inert class, or this run has already re-proved after one changed-head `pr_refresh` and the verified record is that re-proof's own record; no incoming path is in
the observation scope or among the item paths; the patch identity of `<new
base>..<new head>` equals the patch identity of `<verified base>..<verified
head>`; and every path in the observation scope and every item path has the
same blob identity, the output of `git rev-parse <head>:<path>`, at the
verified head and at the new head, or is absent at both; and every path operand
of a working-tree read — every production except `git show` — has a *read
identity* line in the verified record whose identity equals the output of `git
hash-object --no-filters <path>` for that working-tree file at the new head;
and the *mechanical replay* reproduces every step: the stage executes each
step's command at the new head from the repository root, with standard input
closed and the environment variable `LC_ALL` set to `C.UTF-8`, and its standard
output is byte for byte identical to that step's captured proof, which MUST be
the single fenced text block the verified record gives for that step. The
mechanical replay is part of the decision, not a substitute for `proof_verify`:
it executes only commands inside the direct-read grammar, takes no
language-model judgement, and any difference in output, any failure to execute,
and any step whose captured proof is not exactly one fenced text block makes
the decision `reproof_required` naming that step. Otherwise the decision MUST
be `reproof_required`, and it MUST be `reproof_required` naming the input when
any input cannot be read or computed — the verified record absent or
unparseable, a base or head unresolvable, a path list or patch identity that
cannot be computed. A refresh that took a refresh-repair round never reaches
this decision: its repaired head re-enters `janitor`, `publish_draft` and
`proof_capture` as "Refresh repair" requires. Before routing, the stage MUST
post exactly one decision record on the pull request through the posting
primitive of §"Proof of Done record": a `carried_forward` or `reproof_required`
record naming the decision, the verified record's comment link, the verified
head, the previous published head, the new head, the incoming range `<previous
base>..<new base>` with its incoming paths, the observation scope, both patch
identities, and, for `reproof_required`, each input that decided it — each
incoming path outside every inert class or inside the observation scope or item
paths, each step outside the grammar or rejected path operand, the differing
patch identities, each path whose blob identity differs between the two heads,
each path whose read identity is missing or differs from the new head's
working-tree bytes, each step whose mechanical replay did not reproduce its
captured proof or whose captured proof is not exactly one fenced text block, or
the input that could not be read. A `carried_forward` decision whose record
cannot be posted MUST be treated as `reproof_required`, and the stage output
MUST name the failed post; a `reproof_required` decision still routes to
`proof_capture` when its record cannot be posted, and the stage output MUST
name the failed post. The verified head of a later carry-forward in the same
run is still the head of the verified record, so a chain of carry-forwards is
always measured against the diff that was actually verified. A carry-forward
consumes no review-fix round and leaves the three-refresh non-convergence bound
unchanged. Scenario 178 in `scenarios.md` exercises these three paragraphs. A run re-proves after a changed-head `pr_refresh` at most once on the second condition's account. A refresh whose incoming paths overlap the item paths or the observation scope, or whose rebase conflicts in any path that is not a declared record file, MUST still take the re-proof or refresh-repair route this section already requires. A `carried_forward` record written under the second condition MUST say that the incoming paths were not all inert and that the run's one re-proof covered them. Scenario 229 in `scenarios.md` exercises these sentences.

**Release bookkeeping.** When every incoming path is release bookkeeping, no incoming path is among the item paths, and the patch identity of `<new base>..<new head>` equals the patch identity of `<verified base>..<verified head>`, the decision MUST be `carried_forward` whatever the verified record's steps are; the direct-read grammar, observation-scope, blob-identity, read-identity and mechanical-replay conditions of "The decision" do not apply to it. An incoming path is *release bookkeeping* when it is `.release-please-manifest.json` or `CHANGELOG.md`, or when it is `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock`, `git diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --text --unified=0 <previous base> <new base> -- <path>` prints at least one hunk for it, and every line that command prints as added or removed inside a hunk has the form `version = "<text>"`, so a dependency change made beside a version bump, or a change with no inspectable hunk, is not bookkeeping. A `carried_forward` record written under this rule MUST say that every incoming path is release bookkeeping and that no proof step was graded or replayed. Scenario 246 in `scenarios.md` exercises this paragraph.

`pr` MUST query the exact pull request for the recorded branch, verify its
current head against the head named by the latest record of this run that is
either `verified` or `carried_forward`, and MUST refuse to mark the draft ready
for a head that no such record names, apply the Dispatcher- rendered title and
body, mark the draft ready and arm auto-merge with the resolved merge method
unless the item's merge hold is active. It MUST retain existing `PR_NUMBER` and
merge-hold result markers. A pull request already merged is a recorded success;
one closed without merging or carrying an unexpected head MUST fail closed.
Publication metadata MUST be passed as data, not interpolated as shell syntax.
A merge hold MUST preserve the ready pull request and leave auto-merge unarmed. When the forge rejects the head-bound auto-merge arming and a re-read reports the pull request OPEN rather than MERGED, `pr` MUST read the pull request's current head, the forge's mergeability report for it, and the authoritative default branch's current tip, read from a fetch of the authoritative branch on origin and never from a local tracking ref, before deciding what the rejection means. When the head is still the head that the latest `verified` or `carried_forward` record of this run names, and the default branch's current tip is not an ancestor of that head (the same test `pr_refresh` applies), `pr` MUST record a refresh-route marker naming this `pr` visit in the run's publication state and exit zero, and the run MUST return to `pr_refresh` through `pr_route`. That `pr_refresh` visit refreshes onto the advanced default branch (the run's first clean refresh, or, after that, a refresh entered on a forge-reported conflict); it counts toward the three-refresh non-convergence bound exactly when it is a counted refresh as defined above, and it MUST NOT consume a refresh-repair round unless the refresh itself takes the refresh-repair route. After the run has taken its one clean `pr_refresh` refresh, `pr` MUST record the refresh-route marker only when the forge's mergeability report says the pull request conflicts with the default branch. Otherwise it MUST NOT record the marker, and MUST retry the head-bound arming of the same head, re-reading the mergeability report before each retry, within a bounded implementation-defined number of attempts; when an arming succeeds the run proceeds as after any armed pull request, and when the attempts are exhausted `pr` MUST fail closed naming the forge's last rejection cause. The refreshed head then takes the decision of "Proof carry-forward across a refresh" exactly as any other changed-head refresh, so only a head named by a `verified` or `carried_forward` record can reach the next arming. When `pr` is entered again on that route it finds the pull request already out of draft and reports that it readied nothing, which is expected and is not a failure. When the head differs from the recorded head, `pr` MUST fail closed as for any unexpected head. When the default branch's tip is an ancestor of the head, or when the forge cannot report the head, the mergeability or the default branch's tip, `pr` MUST fail closed naming the forge's rejection cause or the measurement it could not take, and MUST NOT route to `pr_refresh` on an unobservable answer. Every rejected arming that does not end in `MERGED` MUST write one stage-output line naming the forge's rejection message verbatim, the pull request's state, the forge's mergeability report, the pull request's current head, whether that head equals the head of the latest `verified` or `carried_forward` record of this run, the default branch's current tip, and whether that tip is an ancestor of the head. The line MUST NOT state that the head differs from the verified head unless that comparison was taken and differed.
Resume from an earlier verified head MUST enter `pr_refresh` before `pr`,
preserving the existing exact-head and run-attribution refusals. A later head
change requires fresh proof or a `carried_forward` record for that head;
publication MUST NOT reuse a verified record from before that change except
through a `carried_forward` record that names the head being published.

**Armed pull request overtaken by the default branch.** After a run arms auto-merge, the Dispatcher's merge wait MUST read the forge's mergeability report on each poll. When two consecutive polls report the pull request OPEN and in conflict with the default branch, the wait MUST stop before the poll budget, and, unless the record-file arm below admits a resume, the dispatch outcome MUST be `blocked` at stage `merge-poll` with the named cause `base-advanced-after-arming`. Before it rests the item, the Dispatcher MUST compute the set of paths that conflict between the pull request's head and the default branch's tip, by a merge computation that changes no ref, no working tree of the primary checkout and nothing on the forge. When that set is non-empty and every path in it is a `path` declared in the committed `dispatcher.record_files` of the repository, the Dispatcher MUST resolve the item to `ready` through the same transition `resolve-blocked:<work-item-id>:ready` performs, and MUST then resume it in the same invocation through the same path `resume --item <work-item-id>` takes. The automatic resume MUST be subject to every refusal and bound of "Resume from a published pull request (`resume --item`)", including its two-resume limit, and the Dispatcher MUST attempt it at most once per invocation. The claim and the ownership lock that the invocation itself holds for the item MUST be released or carried into the resume, and MUST NOT count as a live ownership lock or a live earlier run for that resume's refusals. Before it resolves the item, the Dispatcher MUST journal one `base-advanced-record-files-resume` row naming the run id, the pull request number, its head, the default branch's tip and every conflicted path. When the resume is admitted, the invocation's outcome and exit code are those of the resumed dispatch. When the resume refuses, the item MUST rest at `blocked` with `blocked_reason: needs-human` exactly as below, with the cause `base-advanced-after-arming`, and the ledger comment and the outcome detail MUST name the refusal. When any conflicted path is not a declared record file, when the repository declares no record files, or when the conflict set cannot be computed, the item MUST rest exactly as below, and in the last case the ledger comment MUST name the measurement that failed. The automatic resume MUST NOT disarm, close or rewrite the pull request; the resumed run's `pr_refresh` disarms it before refreshing, as for a hand-driven resume. Whenever the item rests, the Dispatcher MUST rest it at `blocked` with `blocked_reason: needs-human`, through the same transition and `needs-human-blocked` journal row that a `needs_human` terminal produces, with the cause as the item's question. The item MUST NOT be left `active`, and the claim MUST NOT be released to `ready`. `blocked_reason` gains no member. The dispatch reports exit code 4 under §"Dispatcher exit codes"; no exit code is added or redefined. Before the blocked transition, the Dispatcher MUST add one ledger comment to the item that opens with the marker line `livespec-base-advanced-after-arming` and carries the run id, the factory name, the pull request number, its head and the default branch's tip. The comment MUST carry names and figures only. Every name in it MUST be identifier-shaped as §"Dispatch trace correlation" defines that term; a name that is not identifier-shaped MUST be left out, and the comment MUST state how many names were left out. The comment MUST pass the shared template-opener detector before it is written. A comment that fails the detector, or that cannot be written, MUST be journaled with its reason and MUST NOT prevent the blocked transition. The outcome detail MUST name the recovery chain: `resolve-blocked:<work-item-id>:ready`, then `resume --item <work-item-id>`. The Dispatcher MUST NOT disarm, close or rewrite the pull request itself; the resumed run's `pr_refresh` disarms it before refreshing, as "Scripted publication and proof-head integrity" requires. When the poll budget is exhausted, the Dispatcher MUST read the pull request's state once more before it records an outcome. A pull request the forge then reports MERGED MUST proceed exactly as a merge observed within the budget. A pull request the forge then reports OPEN, not in conflict, with auto-merge still armed, and with no check the forge reports as required in a terminal failure is a HANDED-OFF merge wait. Every such check MUST be passing or still running, judged after any automatic re-run the failed-check paragraph below requested. For a handed-off merge wait the Dispatcher MUST NOT rest the item at `blocked` and MUST NOT release its claim. It MUST leave the item `active` under its claim and journal one `merge-wait-handed-off` row naming the run id, the pull request number, its head, the seconds the merge wait spent, and the name of every required check still running. It MUST add one ledger comment to the item that opens with the marker line `livespec-merge-wait-handed-off` and carries the same names and figures. That comment is subject to the same identifier-shape, template-opener and journal-on-failure rules as the `livespec-base-advanced-after-arming` comment above, and a comment that fails them MUST NOT prevent the handoff. The dispatch MUST report exit code 0 under §"Dispatcher exit codes", and no exit code is added or redefined. A handed-off merge wait is completed by §"Stranded claim release". The handoff MUST end the dispatching process, so the fleet launcher that started it removes its fleet in-flight marker as §"Provisional fleet launch scripts" requires when a launch ends. A handed-off row MUST NOT be counted by the shared fleet count, by a repository's counted claims, or by the in-flight addition. A pull request the forge reports OPEN and not in conflict but with auto-merge no longer armed, or whose required checks cannot be read, MUST rest the item exactly as above, at `blocked` with `blocked_reason: needs-human`, through the same transition, journal row, ledger comment rules and recovery chain, with the named cause `merge-poll-budget-exhausted` in place of `base-advanced-after-arming` and the comment's marker line `livespec-merge-poll-budget-exhausted`. Apart from a handed-off merge wait, the item MUST NOT be left `active` under a claim whose run has ended. Scenario 220 in `scenarios.md` exercises this sentence. Scenario 184 in `scenarios.md` exercises this paragraph, including its record-file arm, the `pr` routing above, and the disarm in "Scripted publication and proof-head integrity".

**A required check that fails terminally on infrastructure is re-run once.** When the merge wait observes that a check the forge reports as required has failed terminally on the run's pull request, the Dispatcher MUST, before it records any outcome, read the step conclusions and log of every failed job of the workflow run that produced that check, and classify each failed job. The classifier MUST attribute each failed job to exactly one of `runner-teardown` (every failed step of the job is a post-run or container-teardown step, such as `Post Checkout` or `Stop containers`, or the log reports that the runner's container implementation failed, while every other step of the job succeeded), `oom-kill` (the log or the job conclusion reports the job's process or container killed for exceeding its memory limit), `job-timeout` (the forge reports the job cancelled for exceeding its maximum execution time) or `unattributed`. The classifier MUST attribute a class other than `unattributed` only from evidence it matched in that job's step conclusions or log, against a fixed pattern set committed in the plugin. A log it cannot read MUST classify as `unattributed`. A job in which pytest itself reported a test failure or error, and which matched no `oom-kill` or `job-timeout` evidence, MUST classify as `unattributed`, because the in-place test retry owns it. A process or container kill, or a job timeout, that interrupts a pytest session MUST be classified by that kill or timeout evidence. The Dispatcher MUST request a re-run only when every failed job of the workflow run that backs a required check classifies as `runner-teardown`, `oom-kill` or `job-timeout`, and no failing test that any failed job's log names before its end lies in a file the pull request changed; otherwise it MUST NOT re-run. When it re-runs, it MUST request one forge "re-run failed jobs" for that workflow run, authenticated as the factory's GitHub App identity, and MUST continue the merge wait within its existing poll budget. After requesting the re-run, the merge wait MUST disregard the check results of the attempt it re-ran and MUST judge only the results of the re-run attempt, which the forge reports under a higher run-attempt number for the same workflow run; a required check of that attempt that fails terminally is a terminal failure after the automatic re-run. When the forge rejects or errors on the re-run request, the Dispatcher MUST journal the `merge-poll-failed-jobs-rerun` row with the failure reason, MUST count that request as the one automatic re-run for the head, and MUST record the outcome below for a head it does not re-run, without waiting on the poll budget. The Dispatcher MUST request at most one automatic re-run per pull request head, counted from the journal; the count survives a Dispatcher restart, and neither a rejected re-run request nor a re-run attempt whose required checks fail resets it. For each re-run it requests, the Dispatcher MUST journal one `merge-poll-failed-jobs-rerun` row naming the run id, the pull request number, its head, the workflow run id, each failed job with its class and matched evidence, and, once the re-run attempt's required checks reach a verdict, MUST journal that outcome against the same row. For each re-run it MUST also file one work item in the governed repository's work-items store, with the same marker-line, identifier-shape and template-opener rules as the `livespec-base-advanced-after-arming` comment above, naming the workflow run, each failed job, its class and its matched evidence, so a root fix is owed for every re-run; a failed filing MUST be journaled with its reason and MUST NOT prevent the re-run. The Dispatcher MUST NOT request a second automatic re-run for the same head. When it does not re-run, when the forge rejects or errors on the re-run request, and when a required check of the re-run attempt fails terminally, the dispatch outcome MUST be exactly the one a terminal required-check failure records without this paragraph: `blocked` at stage `merge-poll`, naming the failed checks and the recovery chain `resolve-blocked:<work-item-id>:ready`, then `resume --item <work-item-id>`. A re-run MUST NOT close, disarm or rewrite the pull request, and a re-run that goes green MUST NOT close or discharge any flake work item. Scenario 308 in `scenarios.md` exercises this paragraph.

Groom-kind variants retain their existing filing-plan publication behavior:
the ACP `pr` node validates and encodes the approved cut for host-side filing
and MUST NOT push a branch or open a pull request. Its default adapter and
configuration remain supported only when the selected workflow is groom-kind.
Its success-critical ACP set remains graph-derived. The publish breaker for
implementation workflows MUST retain its sentinel and fail-closed behavior
while its diagnostic names command publication failures rather than an absent
pr adapter or a model refusal.

**`dod_gate`.** The node MUST verify, against the rendered goal, that the
Definition of Done section exists and parses per §"Effective acceptance
criteria", that every reference resolves, that every proof-mode
declaration is valid under the deliverable policy, and that the
assertions are coherent with the item's title, description and
referenced headings — a Definition of Done that a competent engineer
could not recognise as satisfied or unsatisfied from the referenced
scenario is incoherent. The node is an adjudication node: it grades the Definition of Done and changes nothing. It MUST NOT modify the sandbox working tree, create a commit, or run the repository's declared check suite, and its turn MUST leave the working tree clean and HEAD at the commit the node started on. A `dod_gate` turn that modifies the working tree or HEAD MUST end the node with a failed outcome whose failure reason names the mutation, routing through the node's existing Blocked edge to `needs_human` rather than proceeding to `implement`; no new edge, state transition or exit code is introduced. The prompt the node renders MUST state this boundary to the agent. Under the deliverable policy the node MUST
identify, for every `factory_captured` assertion, the surface its proof
needs, and MUST report as a Definition-of-Done finding an assertion
whose surface no capability in a known capability set provides, naming
the assertion, the missing capability, and the remedies in this order:
add the capability to the sandbox image and list it in the committed `dispatcher.sandbox_capabilities` array; declare the assertion
`host_captured` with a Reason when its proof needs the released build or
a host surface; declare it `human_attested` only when no agent session
can exercise it. The surface classes that no sandbox capability provides are: an external cluster or service; a credential or kubeconfig not given to the sandbox; operator-host state; and the released-build effects of a changed prompt or workflow file, including a stage prompt or workflow file under `.claude-plugin/.fabro/` that the item itself changes. The node MUST name the surface of each `factory_captured` assertion before judging it, and MUST report an assertion whose proof needs a surface of one of these classes as a Definition-of-Done finding that names that surface; for the released-build class the finding names the released-build requirement. Its refusal of a `host_captured` or `human_attested`
assertion that a sandbox capability could exercise MUST name the
capability it relies on, and its refusal of a `human_attested` assertion
that an agent session could exercise on a host MUST name the host
surface. The node MUST also report every test-existence assertion on an
item whose deliverable is not a test, a check or a gate, and every reference line that omits, for any assertion, a heading that governs it — each `## Scenario NN — <title>` heading of `scenarios.md` that states behaviour the assertion names, and each non-scenario H2 whose clauses govern that behaviour — naming each omitted heading verbatim and the remedy of adding it to the reference line (§"Effective acceptance criteria" → "Behavioural assertions" and "The Definition of Done section"). This reference-coverage finding is a semantic judgement: it MUST NOT be added to the mechanical half the host-side wall runs, and a reference line the wall accepts MAY still carry it. A reference-coverage finding is ADVISORY whenever the reference line names at least one heading that the spec-stated judgement (§"Dispatcher admission, WIP cap, and post-merge acceptance" → "The spec-stated judgement is one shared component") returns as governing one of the item's assertions. It MUST still be reported, naming each omitted heading verbatim with the remedy of adding it to the reference line, and a host taking that records its verdict on the item MUST include it in that record. But it MUST NOT fail the node, hold the item, withhold `ready` or refuse a dispatch: the node falls through to `implement`, and the host takings admit the item as they would without that finding. Only a reference line that names NO heading the judgement returns as governing any of the item's assertions is refused on reference coverage. Every taking of the Definition-of-Done judgement — the `dod_gate` node, the pre-admission judgement, the pre-dispatch judgement and any host-side preflight — MUST apply this same rule, so the four cannot disagree about whether an omission holds. The judgement can name different governing headings for one unchanged subject, so a refusal on partial omission would hold an item that no single edit reliably clears. Scenario 239 in `scenarios.md` exercises this rule. On success it falls through to `implement`. On
failure it MUST end through the structured needs-human ending whose
failure reason is the list of Definition-of-Done findings, so the run
terminates at the `needs_human` terminal and the Dispatcher rests the
item at `blocked / needs-human` with the findings as the recorded
question and `resolve-blocked:<id>:ready` as the remedy after the human
edits the section. No new state transition, exit code or claim-release
path is introduced. The mechanical half of this check (section present,
references resolve, modes parse) MUST also run in the host-side wall so a
malformed item never spends a sandbox. The semantic half MUST run in the
node on every run, and MUST also run before admission and before
dispatch per §"Effective acceptance criteria" → "Authoring at filing
time" ("Judged before admission" and "Judged again before dispatch");
neither earlier judgement removes or replaces the node. Every taking of this judgement grades the rubric and subject defined in §"Effective acceptance criteria" → "One rubric, one subject".

**`proof_capture`.** For every `factory_captured` assertion the node MUST
author the reproduction steps, execute them verbatim inside the sandbox,
capture the proof they produce (a screenshot for anything reachable
through a web interface, a terminal capture or a fenced code block of
command output for text-only behaviour), and publish the record per
§"Proof of Done record" on the draft pull request. For a behavioural
assertion (§"Effective acceptance criteria" → "Behavioural assertions")
the node MUST exercise the behaviour through the surface the assertion
names, using the delivered artifact as a user or operator would; the
output of the repository's own test suite MUST NOT be the proof of a
behavioural assertion, alone or as its only step, and MAY appear only as
supporting evidence beside a real exercise. When the surface the
assertion names cannot be reached with the sandbox's capabilities, the
node MUST NOT substitute a test run, a fixture or a double: it MUST end
through the structured needs-human ending naming the assertion and the
missing capability. Where an assertion is governed by a referenced
scenario heading, the reproduction steps SHOULD follow one of that
heading's scenarios step for step, and the record MUST name, per
assertion, the referenced heading and the scenario title the steps
exercise, or state that no scenario governs it. Every program a
reproduction step executes that is neither tracked in the repository at
the commit the record names nor an installed tool invoked by its name
MUST be written into the record itself, inline or as an asset the record
names through the proof asset store, so that each step can be replayed
from the record, that commit and the sandbox's installed tools alone; a
step MAY invoke a program the repository tracks at that commit by its
path, and an installed tool by its name, without copying it into the
record. The record MUST state the commit sha its steps ran against, which
MUST be the publish branch head at the moment of capture. A record is
CURRENT for a head under review when the tree of the commit the record
names equals the tree of that head. A commit that changes no tree, such
as an engine checkpoint commit that lands after `proof_capture` publishes,
MUST NOT make a record stale, and no rule MAY require a record to
postdate a commit that changes no tree. It MUST NOT modify the
tree; a capture that requires a code change is an implementation defect
and the node MUST end succeeded with `preferred_label=fix`, which routes
to `fix`, after publishing a record whose first-line verdict is
`not_captured` naming the assertions it could not capture and the
finding; the third `preferred_label=fix` from `proof_capture` in one run
routes to the existing `non_converged` terminal instead. A failed
outcome routes to `needs_human` exactly as every other
ACP node's does. It MUST state, in the record, which assertions are
`host_captured` or `human_attested` and therefore not captured. `review` MUST review the
latest captured record alongside the code; because `review_fix`
re-enters `janitor`, every accepted fix round re-enters `publish_draft`
and `proof_capture` before `review`, so the record `review` reads is
normally current.
`review` is read-only on the run branch. The sandbox, not the prompt alone, MUST refuse within seconds, before any repository hook starts, every command a `review` turn runs that moves or edits the run branch, such as `git rebase`, `git commit`, `git push` or `git reset`, so the run branch's head after the turn equals its head before it. It MUST likewise refuse a `review` turn's invocation of the whole declared check suite, whether `just check` or the sandbox check-suite runner, with a message telling the reviewer to run named test ids only. The `review` prompt MUST state that the reviewer grades the published diff and the latest captured record, makes no branch edits, runs no whole-suite check, and ends with its verdict label within its turn allowance, and each refusal MUST be returned to the turn as a refusal, so that a turn that attempted a refused command can still record its verdict label within that allowance.

**The `proof_capture` git launcher.** The Dispatcher MUST put a git launcher ahead of `git` on the `proof_capture` node's PATH. The launcher MUST decide every `commit` and `push` from the full command line before Git parses it, so a refused write runs no repository hook. The protected repository is the run's checkout, named by `LIVESPEC_PROOF_CAPTURE_PROTECTED_CHECKOUT`. A repository is protected when Git resolves its common git directory to the protected checkout's, which covers the checkout itself, any linked worktree of it, and any `-C`, `--git-dir` or `GIT_DIR` route to either. The launcher MUST refuse `commit` and `push` in a protected repository, and MUST refuse both when the protected checkout or the target repository cannot be resolved. A scratch repository, one whose common git directory is not the protected checkout's, MAY `commit`, and its own hooks run, because the launcher drops only the stage's private `core.hooksPath` override. A scratch repository MAY `push` only when the remote, after Git has resolved any remote name to its URL, is a local filesystem path carrying no URL scheme and no scp-style `host:path` form, and that path, with symlinks followed, resolves to a repository under the system temporary directory (`TMPDIR`, else `/tmp`) whose common git directory is not the protected checkout's. An admitted push likewise drops only that private override. The launcher MUST refuse every other `push`, including a remote carrying any URL scheme (`https://`, `ssh://`, `git://` or `file://`), an scp-style remote, a path outside the system temporary directory, a remote that does not resolve, and any `push` carrying `--receive-pack` or `--exec`. Every refusal MUST print a line beginning `LIVESPEC_PROOF_CAPTURE_READ_ONLY:` on stderr and exit non-zero. A push the launcher admits writes only into a repository under the temporary directory, so it modifies neither the run's tree nor anything published. A `factory_captured` assertion whose surface is a local git fixture with a scratch bare origin therefore remains capturable, and the launcher MUST NOT be the reason such a capture ends at needs-human. Scenario 341 in `scenarios.md` exercises this paragraph.

A blocking review finding whose subject is the latest captured record
rather than the tree is a PROOF-RECORD finding. Each of these is one: a
record that is not current for the head under review; a behavioural
assertion whose proof is test-suite output alone; a step that runs a
program the rule above requires the record to contain and that the record
does not contain; an assertion whose proof is a printed conclusion
rather than the observed output; and a newest captured Proof of Done
comment on the pull request that does not parse as a record, such as one
whose header carries an empty run id. `review` MUST treat that last case
as a blocking proof-record finding naming the comment and the field that
failed to parse, so a verdict whose only blocking finding is a non-record
capture is a recapture verdict, routes to `proof_capture` under the same
two-lap bound, and MUST NOT reach `publication-head` on a capture that
names no run. A review verdict is a RECAPTURE verdict
when it carries at least one blocking finding and every blocking finding
it carries is a proof-record finding. A recapture verdict MUST end
`review` with `preferred_label=recapture`, which MUST route to
`proof_capture` and MUST NOT route to `disposition` or `review_fix`, so
the verdict consumes no `disposition` visit, no `review_fix` visit and no
review-fix round. That holds for the first and second recapture verdicts
of a run; the third recapture verdict in one run MUST route to the
existing `non_converged` terminal without entering `proof_capture`.
Recapture verdicts are governed by that bound alone: an exhausted
review-fix budget MUST NOT pre-empt a recapture verdict, and neither the
review cap's needs-human rest nor its `merge_on_review_cap` ship edge
applies to one. A `review` visit entered after a recapture consumes no
review-fix round, and the engine visit limit of `review` MUST admit the
review-fix budget's visits plus the two recapture laps. A verdict with no
blocking finding keeps the approval route unchanged. `proof_capture`
entered on a recapture verdict MUST receive the verdict's findings by two
routes: the engine's preamble of preceding stage output, and the issuing
visit's record on the pull request — the review record for a recapture
verdict from `review`, and the `not_reproduced` record that
`proof_verify` visit published for a fidelity verdict. It MUST read that
record when the preamble carries no finding, and MUST publish a new captured record,
current for the publish head, that addresses each finding. A verdict that
carries at least one blocking finding about the tree is a fix verdict: it
routes through `disposition` and `review_fix` and is bounded by the
review-fix budget and the review cap exactly as before, and when its fix
round reaches `proof_capture` through `janitor` and `publish_draft`, that
`proof_capture` visit MUST also receive the verdict's proof-record
findings by the same two routes.

**`proof_verify`.** The node MUST run on an adapter distinct from the
implementer's, MUST replay the published reproduction steps verbatim on
the tree it receives, and MUST NOT modify the tree, the steps, or the
Definition of Done. It MUST publish its own record per §"Proof of Done
record" with the verdict `verified` when every `factory_captured`
assertion reproduced, or `not_reproduced` naming each assertion that did
not; the record header renders the verdict verbatim. For each assertion
it names as not reproduced, the record MUST classify the difference as
either FIDELITY, where the replay's observable behavioural result equals
the captured one and only the record's rendering differs (the
interleaving or ordering of output streams, whitespace, or formatting),
or BEHAVIOUR, where the behavioural result differs or cannot be compared.
A difference the node cannot positively show to be fidelity MUST be
classified behaviour. `verified` routes to `proof_grade`, which routes to
`pr_refresh` as above. A `not_reproduced` verdict whose every classified
difference is fidelity is a FIDELITY verdict: it MUST end `proof_verify`
with `preferred_label=recapture`, which MUST route to `proof_capture`
with the record's per-assertion findings as the recapture work order,
and MUST NOT route to `fix`. It counts against the same two-lap
recapture bound as a review recapture verdict, so the third recapture in
one run, from either source, MUST route to the existing `non_converged`
terminal. Any other `not_reproduced` is a BEHAVIOUR verdict. The first
and second behaviour `not_reproduced` verdicts in one run MUST route to
`fix`, and the third behaviour `not_reproduced` in one run routes to the
existing `non_converged` terminal; a fidelity verdict MUST NOT advance
that count. A behaviour `not_reproduced` proof loop re-enters `review`,
and those review visits count toward the review-fix budget like any
other. A fidelity verdict, and any `review` visit it leads back to, MUST
consume only the shared two-lap recapture allowance and MUST NOT count
toward the behaviour `not_reproduced` bound or the review-fix budget.
Where a fidelity verdict and the recapture bound both apply, the
recapture bound decides: a fidelity verdict that would be the run's
third recapture routes to `non_converged`. A `proof_grade` retry is
bounded as stated above instead. The
`review` node's ship-on-review-cap edge MUST target `proof_verify`, never
`pr`, so `merge_on_review_cap` (§"Dispatcher policy settings") skips only
the reviewer's approval and never the replay. No edge MAY route from
`proof_verify` to `pr_refresh` or `pr`; a `verified` outcome reaches `pr_refresh`
only through `proof_grade`. As a backstop to
the review finding above, a `proof_verify` visit that meets a captured
record whose proof of a behavioural assertion is test-suite output alone
MUST end through the structured needs-human ending naming that
assertion; it MUST NOT publish `not_reproduced` for it, because the
defect is in the record and not in the tree, and it MUST NOT publish
`verified`. The engine
constraints these nodes MUST honour are in `constraints.md` §"Fabro
runtime constraints".

**A verdict turn that ends without its verdict label is retried once.** The `review` and `proof_verify` nodes route on the verdict label their turn records (`preferred_label`). When such a turn ends succeeded but records none of the verdict labels its node routes on, the run MUST NOT route it to `needs_human` on that turn. It MUST instead run the same stage once more, on the same head and inputs, with a stage-scoped instruction added to that turn's prompt to end by emitting only its verdict. A retry turn that records a verdict label routes exactly as a first turn with that label does. A second consecutive turn of the same stage visit that ends succeeded without a verdict label MUST route to `needs_human`, with a cause that names the stage and states that its turn recorded no verdict label. The retry counts once per stage visit, and a stage that the run re-enters later gets its own single retry. A turn that records a verdict label, a failed turn, and a node that does not route on a verdict label, such as the command node `proof_grade`, route exactly as before. A record a `proof_verify` turn published before ending without a label stays on the pull request and is read by the existing record rules. Measured 2026-10-26 on livespec-driver-claude-5jr2xu run 01M5XA3WX7H0ZFHE4KDJ3ZVJHZ: after `review` approved, `proof_verify` ended succeeded with an implement-style report and no verdict label, and the run went to `needs_human` through the unmatched-outcome edge with no question asked. Scenario 258 in `scenarios.md` exercises this paragraph.

**Proof findings are the fix stage's work order.** When `proof_capture`
ends with `preferred_label=fix`, or `proof_verify` publishes a first or
second behaviour `not_reproduced` and so routes to `fix`, the finding — the assertion, what was observed, and
what the proof needs — MUST reach the `fix` node as its work order by
two routes: the engine's preamble of preceding stage output (no
templated node attribute and no `inputs.*` edge condition is introduced,
per `constraints.md` §"Fabro runtime constraints"), AND the stage's own
record on the pull request (`not_captured` or `not_reproduced`), so the
finding survives the run. The `fix` prompt MUST treat a proof finding as
a first-class reason for entry beside a red janitor, and MUST take as
its work order the record the entering stage graded in that visit: on
entry from `proof_verify`, the `not_reproduced` record that visit
published; on entry from `proof_capture`, that visit's `not_captured`
record. When the preamble carries no finding, it MUST read the latest
proof record on the pull request. A finding from a capture that a later
`proof_capture` visit superseded MUST NOT be presented to `fix` as its
work order. A `fix` visit entered on a proof finding MUST end either with a
tree change addressing the finding or through the structured needs-human
ending stating why the finding is wrong; it MUST NOT end succeeded with
an unchanged tree. A `fix` visit entered from a red janitor is unchanged
and receives the janitor's failure output as before. A janitor visit
that its node timeout ended before its check aggregate reported a
verdict is NOT a red janitor for that sentence: it reached no verdict,
so it has no failure output to give `fix`. Such a visit MUST NOT enter
`fix`. It MUST be followed by exactly one further janitor visit on the
same head, with no agent turn between the two visits, and that further
visit MUST NOT consume a fix-loop round. When the further visit is also
ended by its node timeout before its check aggregate reported a verdict,
the run MUST end at `needs_human` with its tree preserved, and the
recorded cause MUST state that both janitor visits were ended by the
node timeout with no check-suite verdict. A janitor visit whose check
aggregate reported a failing verdict, including one whose verdict was
recorded before a later kill, is a red janitor and still enters `fix`
exactly as that sentence states. Scenario 138 in `scenarios.md`
exercises this rule. The proof loops
stay bounded by the two finding-count bounds above — the third
`preferred_label=fix` from `proof_capture` and the third behaviour
`not_reproduced` from `proof_verify` each route to `non_converged`.
Scenario 137, Scenario 138 and Scenario 141 in `scenarios.md` exercise
the capture, replay and fix duties added to this section.

### Proof of Done record

**The record.** Each execution of `proof_capture`, `proof_verify`, each
host-leg capture or replay, and each human-attested leg MUST publish exactly
one NEW comment on the work item's pull request, whose first line is `Proof of
Done —
<captured|not_captured|verified|not_reproduced|carried_forward|reproof_required|host_recorded|host_verified|host_not_reproduced|human_attested>
— <run <run-id> | session <session-identity> | human <identity>> — <UTC
timestamp>`. The host-leg verdict words are `host_recorded`, `host_verified`
and `host_not_reproduced`, so that the proof MODE `host_captured` and a record
verdict never share a word. `not_captured` is the verdict of a `proof_capture`
execution that ended with `preferred_label=fix` (§"Definition-of-Done and
Proof-of-Done stages"); its body names the assertions it could not capture and
the finding. `carried_forward` and `reproof_required` are the decision records
of a changed-head `pr_refresh` (§"Definition-of-Done and Proof-of-Done stages"
→ "Proof carry-forward across a refresh"); their body carries the decision
inputs that paragraph names in place of per-assertion reproduction steps, and a
`carried_forward` record MUST link the `verified` record it carries. A
`carried_forward` record anchors a resume exactly as the `verified` record it
carries would, at the new head it names. A `reproof_required` record is not
proof: it MUST NOT anchor a resume, and the acceptance pass and every reader of
the latest proof record MUST skip it. The run identifier a factory record
carries MUST be one the Dispatcher can attribute to the dispatch of the item that produced the record: the
Fabro run id, or the dispatch id the Dispatcher declared to the sandbox, or,
for a resumed dispatch, an identifier the journal's `resume` record links to
it, transitively (§"Dispatcher loop invocation surface" → "Resume from a
published pull request"). A factory record (`captured`, `not_captured`,
`verified`, `not_reproduced`, `carried_forward`, `reproof_required`) MUST also
name, once, the full commit sha of the publish-branch head the stage ran on,
which for `carried_forward` and `reproof_required` is the new head; a record
naming no head cannot anchor a resume. A record comment MUST NOT be edited
after posting; a correction is a new record. The body MUST contain, per
assertion in Definition of Done order: the assertion text, its proof mode, the
governing scenario (the referenced heading and the scenario title the steps
exercise) or the statement that no scenario governs it, the numbered
reproduction steps (naming every credential by environment-variable name and
the wrapper that supplies it, never a value), and the proof — an inline image
reference for each screenshot and a fenced code block for each text capture. In
a `verified` or `not_reproduced` record, the section of each `factory_captured`
assertion MUST carry its own prose line `Reproduced: yes` or `Reproduced: no`,
outside any fenced block; a verdict line in another section, including a
record-wide summary, MUST NOT be read as that assertion's verdict. A
`captured` or `verified` record on an item with `human_attested` assertions
MUST list those assertions under a heading stating they are pending human
attestation, and one on an item with `host_captured` assertions MUST list those
assertions under a heading stating they are pending the host leg. The
human-attested record MUST be posted by the attesting human on the same pull
request in the same structure; images MAY be attached through the forge's own
upload.

**The binding.** Every record the implementation posts, each factory record
and each host record, MUST carry its own binding to the subject it proves. The
binding is written by the implementation's posting primitive, the one §"The
host leg" below names, which every stage and every host leg MUST use to
publish a record, so that no stage or session hand-formats a binding. The
binding is exactly one line, placed immediately after the record's first line
and outside any fenced block, of the form `Binds: <work-item-id> — pull
request #<number> — head <full commit sha>`. It names the work item the record
proves, the pull request the record is posted on, and the full commit sha of
the pull request head the record proves: for a factory record, the
publish-branch head the record names; for a host record, the head commit of
that pull request at its merge, which is not the default-branch commit the
merge produced. The primitive's resolution of which pull request a record is
posted on, and any refusal it makes for an item that has no merged pull
request of its own, govern host records only: a factory record is posted,
before merge, on the pull request of the run that produced it, and its binding
names that pull request. A correcting record that supersedes a factory record
MAY be posted through the primitive after merge, on the same pull request; it
carries the superseded record's run identifier on its first line and binds the
head the superseded record proves. A record that carries no binding line is a
legacy record. A human-attested record is posted by a human and is outside
this rule; the human-attested leg of the acceptance pass governs it. A
correction is a new record: a record the primitive posts MAY carry, on the
line after its binding, `Supersedes: <comment link>` naming one earlier record
on the same pull request, and only a record that itself carries a well-formed
binding to that pull request resolves the fault of the record it names. A
proof-only resume of a merged pull request (§"Dispatcher loop invocation
surface" → "A proof-only resume of a merged pull request") MAY also post new
factory records after merge on that pull request, each carrying the resumed
run's identifier and binding the pull request's head commit at merge. The
acceptance pass selects records by binding (§"Dispatcher admission, WIP cap,
and post-merge acceptance" → "The proof evidence leg"). Measured 2026-10-26:
the acceptance pass on bd-ib-tixpma, pull request 3164, resolved four run ids
as the merging runs, did not include run 0498841858ff4cb185b42d12ff26e8b4, and
reported its proof of done record NOT OBSERVED, although that run's `verified`
record had been on the pull request since 2026-10-17 and the pass of
2026-10-18 had graded it. Scenario 252 in `scenarios.md` exercises this
paragraph and the selection it governs.

**The host leg.** For an item with `host_captured` assertions, an agent
session on an operator host MUST publish a `host_recorded` record after
the change is merged and, where a release applies, released and
installed through its normal installation path. The record follows the
record structure above and MUST additionally name the BUILD IDENTITY
exercised: the release tag and the installed build identifier, or, where
no release applies, the default-branch commit exercised. A DIFFERENT
session identity MUST then replay those steps verbatim and publish
`host_verified`, or `host_not_reproduced` naming each assertion that did
not reproduce. Host records MUST be published on the pull request of the
latest merged run for the item; a host record on an earlier pull
request, or one naming a build identity that does not contain the latest
merge, is not evidence.
For an item that no factory run merged, the pull request of its latest merged
run is, throughout this specification, the pull request of the latest
`reconcile-merged` that journaled a green janitor against that pull request and
merge SHA and moved the item into `acceptance`; a refused or failed
reconciliation MUST NOT replace that pull request. The posting primitive MUST target that
pull request for such an item and MUST NOT refuse for the missing run, and when
it drives `reconcile-merged` for such an item it MUST pass that pull request as
the `--pr` selector. When the item has neither a merged run nor such a
reconciliation, the primitive MUST refuse before posting anything, naming the
item.
The implementation MUST provide one posting
primitive that renders these records, so that no session hand-formats
one. The primitive MUST post only on the pull request of the latest merged run
for the named work item, as defined above, and MUST NOT post a host record onto
any other pull request or fall back to any other merged pull request in the
repository, however that pull request was found. Its refusal when no such pull
request exists MUST state that the item has no merged pull request of its own.
A host record already posted on any other pull request is not evidence for the
item, and it is not evidence for the pull request it was posted on. The
primitive MUST compute the publishing identity itself — the
invoking agent session's id, or the forge login for a human — and MUST
NOT accept it as a caller-supplied string; it MUST refuse a
`host_verified` or `host_not_reproduced` post whose computed identity
equals that of the `host_recorded` record it replays; and, on publishing
`host_verified` or `host_not_reproduced`, it MUST drive
`reconcile-merged --item <id>` (§"Dispatcher loop invocation surface"),
which re-runs the acceptance pass. A `host_verified` record whose
identity equals its `host_recorded` record's identity, however it was
posted, is not evidence.

**The pointer.** After merge, the Dispatcher MUST write a `## Proof of Done`
section into the item's description, after the Definition of Done section and
preserving it byte-for-byte, containing only: the pull request number, the
comment link of the latest `verified` record counting for the item, its run id and timestamp, its
verdict, — when the merged head was reached through a carry-forward — the
comment link of the `carried_forward` record naming that head, — when the item
was resumed (§"Dispatcher loop invocation surface" → "Resume from a published
pull request") — the resumed run's identifier, — when the item has
`host_captured` assertions — the comment link of the latest `host_verified`
record once it exists, and — when the item has `human_attested` assertions —
the comment link of the human-attested record once it exists. The section MUST
NOT copy proof content. Every record the pointer names, and every record a
staleness check compares it with, MUST be one that counts for the item under
the proof evidence leg's bind verdicts (a factory, host or human-attested
record, as that leg defines counting). The pointer MUST be written whenever a
`verified` record counting for the item exists, independently of the
acceptance verdict: a
pass that parks the item still writes it. A pointer whose run id or comment id
does not match the latest record OF THE SAME KIND (`verified`,
`carried_forward`, `host_verified`, `human_attested`) on the pull request that
counts for the item under the proof evidence leg's bind verdicts is stale and MUST be surfaced by `needs-attention` as a hygiene fact naming the
item and the pull request; a later record of another kind does not make a
pointer stale. An item in `acceptance` that has a `verified` record counting for
it and whose description has no pointer MUST likewise be surfaced by
`needs-attention` as a hygiene fact naming the item and the pull request, and
`reconcile-merged` driven for that item MUST write the missing pointer.

**The proof asset store.** Binary proof MUST be stored through one
implementation-owned store seam. The store MUST satisfy one requirement:
a viewer authorized on the repository sees each image inline in the
record comment, and no unauthorized viewer can fetch it; a store that
fails the second half MUST NOT be selected for that repository, and the
implementing slice MUST measure the requirement on a private repository
before selecting a store. Where no API-drivable store satisfies the first
half for a repository, the record MUST carry one authenticated link per
image in place of the inline reference, the inline half is waived for
that repository, and the waiver MUST be journaled per repository naming
the store measured; the proof itself is never waived. Where it satisfies
the requirement, the first implementation MAY be the release assets of
one standing prerelease per governed repository, whose tag is the
committed `dispatcher.proof_assets_release_tag` (default `proof-assets`;
committed-configuration-only, not a console setting); the prerelease MUST
be marked prerelease so it is never the repository's latest release, MUST
NOT be deleted while any record references it, and MUST be created by
the Dispatcher before the first dispatch of a repository whose item
carries a `factory_captured` assertion — a dispatch whose target lacks it
after that attempt MUST refuse before any run exists, naming the tag.
Proof binaries MUST NOT be committed to the repository tree.

**Naming.** Every asset name MUST have the form
`<work-item-or-epic-id>__<run-id or session-identity>__<capture|verify|host-capture|host-verify>__<NN>__<slug>.<ext>`, where
`NN` is the two-digit ordinal of the proof within that stage's record and
`slug` is a short lowercase-kebab description; a reproduction step MUST
name the asset ordinal it produces, so a `verify` asset compares to the
`capture` asset of the same ordinal, and a `host-verify` asset to the
`host-capture` asset of the same ordinal. A factory record's asset
carries the run id, a host or plan record's asset carries the publishing
session identity, and a plan record's asset carries the epic id
(§"Plan Definition of Done and Proof of Done"). Because the run id or
session identity is part of the
name, no run or session MAY overwrite another's asset. The behaviour of this
section and the stages section is exercised by Scenario 132 and
Scenario 133 in `scenarios.md`; the host leg, the same-kind staleness
rule, the pointer repair and the run-identifier attribution are
exercised by Scenario 136 and Scenario 138, and the governing-scenario
entry of the record by Scenario 141.

## Factory sandbox clone release tags

A factory run's sandbox clone MUST carry the release tags its repository's
remote holds at dispatch time, so a check that reads tags inside the run
reads the same tag set a fresh clone of the remote would read. This section
governs every run the Dispatcher launches: the reserved `implement-work-item`
workflow, every registered variant, a target-local workflow resolved under
"Target-local workflow" in §"Self-contained plugin dispatch", and a run the
Dispatcher resumes.

**The prepare chain refreshes the remote's tags.** The prepare steps the
Dispatcher renders into a run MUST include a fetch from `origin` that updates
the clone's tag namespace from the remote's, with existing local tags
overwritten where the remote's tag of the same name points at a different
object. That fetch MUST run after the committed prepare chain's opening
unshallow step and no later than the Dispatcher-materialized dispatch-base
fetch of the default branch, so every later prepare step and every graph node
observes the refreshed tags. It MAY be the dispatch-base fetch itself, for
example `git fetch --quiet --tags --force origin
+refs/heads/<default_branch>:refs/remotes/origin/<default_branch>`, provided
the remote-tracking ref that fetch exists to create is still written. Tag
auto-following on the unshallow fetch, or on any fetch of a branch refspec
alone, MUST NOT be relied on to satisfy this section: it brings in only tags
that point into newly fetched history and leaves tags already present, or a
tag set seeded from elsewhere, unrefreshed.

**What the clone holds after preparation.** After the run's prepare steps
complete, all of the following MUST hold in the sandbox clone:

- every tag the remote holds whose target is reachable from the fetched
  default branch is present locally and points at the same object as the
  remote's tag of that name;
- the newest release tag the clone reports, ordered by version, equals the
  newest release tag the remote holds at dispatch time; and
- `git describe --tags` on the fetched default branch's tip names the same tag
  it names in a fresh full clone of the remote.

The fetch MAY bring in every tag the remote holds, including tags that point
outside the fetched default-branch history.

**A failed refresh fails preparation.** When the tag refresh exits non-zero,
the prepare chain MUST fail, as a failure of the dispatch-base fetch does. It
MUST NOT continue on the tag set the clone already had, because a tag-reading
check would then grade the change under test against a stale tag set and
report its own staleness as the change's defect.

**Tag-reading checks are not made to tolerate stale tags.** A repository's
check that reads release tags MUST NOT be weakened to tolerate a clone whose
tags lag the remote; the remedy for a stale tag set is this section's
refresh. Measured 2026-11-02 on factory run 01M6E7FFPF99
(livespec-dev-tooling-t4rx4t): the sandbox clone of livespec-dev-tooling
carried release tags ending at v1.99.0 while the remote's default branch was
at v1.153.2, and the repository's versioning lockstep test failed in the
refresh merge's suite-green leg on that stale tag set. The Dispatcher's launch
overlay unshallowed the single-branch clone and fetched only the
default-branch refspec, so the clone's tag namespace was never refreshed.
Scenario 298 in `scenarios.md` exercises this section.

## Work-item state semantics

What each of the seven lifecycle states MEANS, in plain English. These
definitions are ratified semantics: every transition contract in this
specification (§"Dispatcher admission, WIP cap, and post-merge
acceptance", §"The four maintainer touchpoints", the scenarios) is
subordinate to them. Design record: repo `thewoolleyman/livespec`,
`plan/archive/work-item-state-machine/research/03-decision-log.md`
(decisions 26 and 32), with the maintainer's verbatim reasoning in
`plan/archive/work-item-state-machine/conversation/transcript.md`.

- `backlog` — captured but not yet groomed: the item needs
  decomposition or grooming before it can be worked.
- `pending-approval` — prepared (groomed) but not yet authorized to
  start — the lane that shows the maintainer exactly what waits on
  their GO.
- `ready` — authorized to start (a human approved it, or the item's
  `admission_policy: auto` delegation did), pulled into work when a
  WIP slot frees. An item awaiting a human's permission MUST NOT be
  in `ready`.
- `active` — admitted into a WIP slot and being worked — or parked
  rework-pending: routed back from `acceptance` by a rework entry and
  awaiting its fix-forward re-dispatch (§"Rework-pending re-dispatch").
- `acceptance` — merged, live, and observable, awaiting post-ship
  confirmation per its effective `acceptance_policy`.
- `blocked` — cannot proceed without something outside the factory
  (`blocked_reason: needs-human` or `infra-external`). This is a
  TRANSIENT lifecycle state — the item rests in `blocked` because
  something outside the factory is *currently* preventing progress, and
  it clears when that external thing resolves. It is a DIFFERENT axis
  from `factory_safety` (§"Work-item beads-issue mapping"), an INTRINSIC
  capture-time classification of the work ITSELF: a non-null
  `factory_safety` item is permanently host-only regardless of external
  state — `ready`/dispatchable-in-principle but routed to a host actor
  rather than an agent sandbox — and it never "clears".
- `done` — accepted and closed.

**`approve` IS the `pending-approval → ready` transition** ("manual: a
human; auto: automatic"). **Gradeable acceptance criteria
(AI-dispositive items):** an item whose EFFECTIVE `acceptance_policy` is
`ai-only` or `ai-then-human` and whose effective acceptance criteria
(§"Effective acceptance criteria") parse to zero gradeable assertions
MUST NOT enter `ready`: the human `approve` valve MUST refuse it and an
`auto` admission policy MUST withhold it, in both cases surfacing the
parse result, the item id, and the remedy (author criteria via groom or
