Like every mechanical finding it MUST be displayed by `filing_display`, MUST be recorded on the item as a `definition-of-done finding (mechanical):` ledger comment, and MUST withhold `ready`, even when the item's effective `admission_policy` is `auto`; the `approve` rule for an auto-admission item held by intake, which re-runs the intake Definition-of-Done check against the item's current text, applies to it unchanged. Where the repository carries no committed `tests/heading-coverage-debt.json`, the same bullet MUST NOT produce this finding. Bullets outside the `## Definition of Done` section, and the legacy acceptance-criteria field, MUST NOT be read for it. The rule is lexical by design: a bullet that names the token only to exclude it still produces the finding, and its remedy is the same edit, stating the requirement without the token. Scenario 339 in `scenarios.md` exercises this kind. A test-existence or
scenario-reference finding the wall recognises is ADVISORY: it MUST be
displayed and MUST NOT withhold `ready`, because only the gate can judge
it. The rendered goal is assembled from the dispatched item's own fields
and ledger comments, and the sandbox has no ledger access. So a
description, Definition of Done or comment that names another work-item as
holding this item's evidence directs the implementer to text it cannot
read. The wall MUST report such a reference as an ADVISORY finding naming
the referenced work-item, with the remedy of copying the evidence onto this
item before dispatch. An item the wall does not flag MUST NOT be reported
as clear of such references. Scenario 218 in `scenarios.md` exercises this
sentence. When the committed Dispatcher policy setting
`dispatcher.goal_size_warning_bytes`, a positive integer with no default, is
set, an item whose rendered goal exceeds it MUST carry an ADVISORY finding
naming the item and the rendered goal's size in bytes. The rendered goal
here means title, description, criteria, notes, lessons and every ledger
comment. The finding MUST be shown by the filing displays and by the
Dispatcher's stderr and dispatch journal when it renders that goal, and
MUST be among the `needs-attention` hygiene facts for a `ready` item. It
MUST NOT refuse or delay a dispatch. When the key is unset, the finding
MUST NOT be evaluated, and an invalid value MUST be reported as a
configuration finding. Scenario 219 in `scenarios.md` exercises these
sentences. Either kind MUST be recorded on the filed item as a ledger comment,
so it is repaired where it was made. For a child of a plan, which plan
assertions the child carries is recorded ONLY in the epic's carrier-map
event (§"Plan Definition of Done and Proof of Done" → "The carrier
map"); the child's description MAY repeat it as prose before the
Definition of Done heading and MUST NOT state it inside the section,
where it is a finding under "Unevidenceable assertions"
(§"Post-merge acceptance (`acceptance → done`)"). `needs-attention`
SHOULD surface, as hygiene facts, each `ready` item carrying an advisory
Definition-of-Done finding, so that it is repaired before a sandbox is
spent on it. The implement prompt MUST state the kept-current rule
below. Scenario 140 in `scenarios.md` exercises this clause.

**The spec-stated judgement is one shared component.** The Dispatcher MUST obtain two verdicts from the `livespec_runtime.spec_stated` module of the livespec-runtime release this plugin vendors, and from nowhere else: for a behaviour statement, whether the ratified specification states it — `stated`, naming each governing H2 heading verbatim; `partial` or `unstated`, naming the existing heading whose generalization would state it, or none — and for a work-item, whether it is a `feature`, a `bug`, a `chore` or `non_functional`, the stored type being evidence rather than the answer. The module defines the prompt, the inputs and the verdict schema and invokes no model itself; the Dispatcher supplies the model runner through the module's injected callable, so the judgement is defined once for every orchestrator. The Definition-of-Done judgement named in the "Judged before admission" and "Judged again before dispatch" paragraphs below, the `dod_gate` node, and the filing-time reference advisory MUST take the governing-heading verdict for each assertion from this component and MUST name the heading it returns as the remedy for a reference that does not govern the assertion; coherence, proof-mode feasibility, rider coherence and every existing refusal remedy remain graded exactly as before, because this component answers only the two questions above. A verdict MUST be reused only while its input and the spec identity it was taken against (§"Effective acceptance criteria" → "One rubric, one subject") are both unchanged since it was taken. For a governing-heading verdict taken for an assertion, the input is the assertion's text together with every ledger comment the subject's goal carries, so a rider appended to the item invalidates the governing-heading verdicts of all its assertions. For a work-item classification, the input is the subject's goal. The spec-change tier decision of "An autonomy tier is assigned" — the item's classification taken together with the verdict on its asked-for behaviour — has as its input the asked-for behaviour statement, and its spec identity is the clause provenance defined below for a governing-heading verdict: the set of clauses the judgement placed before its model in full, together with every clause the verdict names, each with its heading and body. The asked-for behaviour statement is the item's title, description and acceptance criteria rendered as one statement, EXCEPT that the description's `## Definition of Done` section MUST be rendered without its proof-mode partition: the rendering MUST omit every `### Host-captured` and `### Human-attested` sub-heading together with its `Reason:` line, and MUST render the section's assertion bullets in one canonical order that does not depend on their position or proof mode. Proof mode states how an assertion is proved, not what the item asks for. A Definition of Done edit confined to that partition (moving a bullet word for word between the default `factory_captured` bullets and a `### Host-captured` or `### Human-attested` sub-heading, adding, removing or rewording a `Reason:` line, or reordering bullets) therefore MUST NOT change the spec-change tier decision's input, and a recorded tier decision MUST be reused across it on the same terms as any unchanged input. A change to any bullet's text, to the title, to the `References:` line, or to description text outside the section's bullets changes the input and MUST cause the tier decision to be taken again. This narrowing applies to the spec-change tier decision only; a governing-heading verdict keeps its own input, the assertion's text together with the goal's ledger comments. Every spec-change tier record appended at filing, at groom or on a dispatch path MUST carry that clause provenance. A tier decision MUST be reused across a new revision under `<spec-root>/history/` exactly when a governing-heading verdict would be: the asked-for behaviour statement is unchanged, the selection repeated against the new revision returns the same clauses, and every clause the verdict names is unchanged in heading and body. Classifying an item "again on every dispatch path" is satisfied by that reuse and does not require a new model judgement. A recorded tier decision that does not carry the clauses it was judged against is invalidated by every new revision. For a governing-heading verdict, the spec identity is narrower; this narrowing applies to the governing-heading component and to the spec-change tier decision above, and the enclosing Definition-of-Done judgement keeps the spec identity of "One rubric, one subject". The identity is the set of clauses the judgement placed before its model in full, together with every clause the verdict names, each with its heading and body. The selection of those clauses MUST be a deterministic function of the item's subject and the specification text, and before reusing a verdict after a new revision the Dispatcher MUST repeat that selection against the new revision. It MUST reuse the verdict only when the newly selected clauses, and every clause the verdict names, are exactly those the verdict was judged against, with unchanged headings and bodies. A revision that adds, removes or changes any of those clauses, or that changes which clauses are selected, therefore invalidates the verdict. A revision that leaves them all unchanged does not, even when it adds, removes or changes clauses elsewhere, including headings the prompt listed without their bodies. A change to the item's Definition of Done changes a governing-heading verdict's input and invalidates it, as a rider does; for the spec-change tier decision, a change confined to the proof-mode partition is not a change to its input. A recorded verdict that does not carry the clauses it was judged against is invalidated by every new revision. The judgement that decides whether to release a held spec-change-tier item MUST NOT reuse a verdict taken before the latest revision; it always runs against the ratified specification. Scenario 206 in `scenarios.md` exercises this paragraph together with the autonomy-tier bullet below. A human attestation recorded by the `release-spec-tier` valve (§"The four maintainer touchpoints", touchpoint 1) is the one exception to this paragraph's verdict source, selection and reuse rules, on the terms that touchpoint states.

**Host judgements take the resolved `dod_gate` chain.** The pre-admission and pre-dispatch takings of the Definition-of-Done judgement, every governing-heading verdict and work-item classification the Dispatcher takes from the spec-stated judgement on the host, the drift run's spec-stated judgement, and the out-of-band reflector's judgement of shipped work's telemetry MUST each take their model judgement from the `dod_gate` node's candidate chain as a dispatch of the governed repository resolves it under §"ACP node adapter configuration" (repository layer over workflow layer, with no per-dispatch override). They try the candidates in chain order as FALLBACKS: the first candidate that returns a verdict decides the judgement, and the remaining candidates are not run. A candidate the host cannot launch, because its resolved adapter carries no agent identity the host can run or its agent is not available, or one that returns no verdict (a timeout or an unparseable reply), passes the judgement to the next candidate. In the pre-admission and pre-dispatch takings of the Definition-of-Done judgement, which take their verdict from the first candidate that returns one, the Dispatcher MUST bound the total model input of each candidate it runs; a repository preflight's independently graded chain is not ended mid-run by this bound, but a preflight candidate whose requests together report input at or above it has returned no verdict, with the input bound as its cause. A candidate's input is the input tokens its output reports for its model requests, uncached, cache-written and cache-read alike, whether reported per request or as an aggregate covering several requests; each request is counted once however many times its report is repeated, and never both in its own report and in an aggregate that covers it. The Dispatcher MUST check the running total at every usage report the candidate's output makes available while it runs, and again on its final usage before it accepts the candidate's verdict. When the total reaches or exceeds 100,000 tokens, the Dispatcher MUST end the candidate, that is, cancel its active turn, terminate its remaining processes, never resume its session, and discard any verdict it returned, and MUST treat it as having returned no verdict, so the judgement passes to the next candidate. The Dispatcher MUST enable and consume every usage reporting the candidate supports, per-request, aggregate and streaming alike. A candidate whose reporting so enabled supplies no input usage at all cannot be bounded and runs unbounded, and its usage is recorded as unreported; that exception never applies because the Dispatcher omitted to enable or consume reporting the candidate supports. The record of a pre-admission or pre-dispatch taking whose chain returned a verdict MUST name the total input tokens its deciding candidate's requests reported, marked complete when the reports cover every request, partial when they cover only some, and unreported when there are none. The record of a taking whose chain returned no verdict names no deciding candidate and lists each candidate the bound ended, and for each such candidate the total input tokens its requests reported, marked complete, partial or unreported as for a deciding candidate, and the bound that ended it. The same holds for the pre-admission taking's did-not-run record and for the pre-dispatch taking's. A taking that reuses a recorded verdict runs no candidate, so neither the bound nor the field applies to it. Measured 2026-10-26, one host taking launched as `claude -p` made three requests that each re-sent a context of about 128,000 tokens, so one grading consumed about 380,000 input tokens. When no candidate returns a verdict, the judgement did not run, and the taking follows its ratified did-not-run route. For the out-of-band reflector, a reply that parses as its structured findings is a verdict even when it carries no findings, and a reply that does not parse as findings is no verdict. Its did-not-run route is this: its pass MUST record that its judgement did not run and why, and MUST file no work item and propose no lesson from that pass. A host judgement MUST NOT carry a hard-coded model default and MUST NOT take its model from any other source. In particular, the out-of-band reflector MUST NOT launch an agent process of its own outside the candidate chain, such as a headless `claude -p`, and no variable of the host's environment, `LIVESPEC_REFLECTOR_MODEL` included, selects its model; a model the resolved candidate's committed adapter configuration carries is not such a selection. The Honeycomb telemetry access the reflector needs is named on the reflector's own invocation, as the next paragraph permits. Measured 2026-10-26, the reflector launched `claude -p` directly on the Anthropic model `LIVESPEC_REFLECTOR_MODEL` named, with `claude-opus-4-8` as its hard-coded default, and no work item then routed it through the chain. A repository preflight that runs its own chain of candidate judges is not governed by this paragraph; it keeps the independently graded chain the TAKING paragraph below defines. Scenario 239 in `scenarios.md` exercises this paragraph, and Scenario 251 exercises its sentences on the out-of-band reflector.

**A host judgement launches outside the interactive agent configuration.** Each host judgement the preceding paragraph names MUST launch its candidate agent without the interactive agent configuration of the governed repository or of the host's operator. No hook, plugin, MCP server or instruction file from the project-level or user-level configuration of the candidate's agent loads into the judgement's agent session, beyond what the judgement itself names on its own invocation. This holds whichever agent the resolved candidate runs. The judgement's subject, rubric and governing text reach the agent only through the judgement's own prompt and the tool allowance the judgement grants. The reason is cost, measured on 2026-10-25 on the gmktec factory host. Two or three host judgements per dispatch each launched `claude -p` with the governed repository as its working directory, so each one ran that repository's session-start hooks: twelve plugin marketplace and install calls, a credential wrapper and an MCP server. A guard hook also ran on every tool call. Together they made up most of the 4.7 to 6.8 CPU-minutes that a dispatch spent before its Fabro run started.

**One rubric, one subject.** The Definition-of-Done judgement is taken by the `dod_gate` node, before admission, before dispatch, and by any host-side preflight a repository runs before launching a dispatch. Every taking MUST grade by ONE rubric: the `dod_gate` node's prompt file, read from the plugin build that will execute the dispatch. A taking MUST NOT add, remove or restate a check. A taking other than the node MAY append only an ending contract stating the verdict form it must return. Any other guidance about how to grade a check, including any statement about where the capability set comes from, MUST be written into the rubric itself, so that the node grades by it too.

Every taking MUST grade one SUBJECT, made of four components.

- The GOAL: the item's rendered goal exactly as the Dispatcher renders it for the node — title, description, effective criteria, notes, lessons and every CARRIED rider, as §"Dispatch-brief lessons injection" → "A goal carries a bounded rider set" defines it, and so excludes the Definition-of-Done JUDGEMENT RECORDS: each comment whose first line begins with `livespec-dod-judgement`, whichever taking or surface wrote it (verdict, did-not-run and disagreement records alike), the filing-time FINDING COMMENTS: each comment whose first line begins with `definition-of-done finding (advisory):` or `definition-of-done finding (mechanical):`, the prefixes filing writes before each advisory and each mechanical finding, and the SPEC-CHANGE TIER RECORDS: each comment whose first line is `livespec-spec-change-tier`, whichever stage wrote it. Those records are receipts, not brief: each reports a judgement taken against one specification version, and a later revision can supersede it. The Dispatcher MUST omit them from the node's rendered goal as well, and recording any of them MUST NOT change any subject digest. A rendered goal MUST NOT carry any carried rider's text more than once, whichever section of the goal carries it, and the subject digest MUST be computed over the subject as this paragraph defines it, unchanged by how the node receives the subject. A ledger comment added after filing that is none of these records is a rider, and the rendered goal's operator-rider section carries it while it is CARRIED. A comment that is not carried MUST NOT change any subject digest, so a verdict recorded on identical carried riders remains reusable. Omitting a record from the subject and the goal MUST NOT remove it from the item's ledger. Every taking MUST decide whether a References heading resolves by matching it against the H2 headings of the specification tree it grades against, and MUST NOT treat an earlier finding comment or spec-change tier record as evidence about the item's References headings or as operator brief. This omission concerns the judgement's subject and the rendered goal only: it leaves unchanged the reuse of a recorded tier decision, `classify-tier`'s report of an existing record, the carrying forward of a linked proposed-change topic, and the spec-change-tier hold, each of which reads the tier records as before. Within the GOAL, the effective criteria returned by the shared primitive MUST render as a block in which each assertion is its own `- ` bullet, in source order. When the source is `description-definition-of-done`, the block MUST preserve each `### Host-captured` and `### Human-attested` sub-heading and its `Reason:` line from that section in their original positions relative to the assertions, so that every assertion's proof mode is visible by position; an assertion above every proof-mode sub-heading MUST remain above all of them. For the legacy `criteria-field` and `description-exit-criteria` sources, the block MUST render the resolved assertions without importing proof-mode sub-headings or `Reason:` lines from other description sections.
- The HEADINGS: the verbatim body of each heading the reference line names.
- The SPEC IDENTITY: the CLAUSE PROVENANCE of the governing-heading verdicts the taking uses for the subject's assertions (§"Dispatcher admission, WIP cap, and post-merge acceptance" → "The spec-stated judgement is one shared component"), kept per assertion: for each assertion, the clauses its verdict was judged against and, separately, every clause that verdict names, each with its heading and body. A ratified revision that changes any of those clauses, or that changes which clauses any assertion's selection returns or its verdict names, therefore changes the SPEC IDENTITY, and a revision that leaves them all unchanged leaves the SPEC IDENTITY unchanged; the other subject components change the subject digest exactly as before. When any of the subject's assertions has a governing-heading verdict that did not run or carries no clause provenance, and for the judgement that decides whether to release a held spec-change-tier item, the SPEC IDENTITY is instead the WHOLE-TREE DIGEST: a digest of the bytes of every file under the governed spec root at the resolved commit, excluding `proposed_changes/` and `history/`. A host taking therefore establishes each assertion's governing-heading verdict before it computes the subject digest: it reuses each recorded verdict that verdict's own reuse rule allows, which runs no model, and takes the others. A surface that only compares a subject digest and is not a taking, such as drain candidate enumeration or a `needs-attention` hygiene fact, MUST NOT take a governing-heading verdict: it uses only recorded verdicts that their reuse rule allows, and when any assertion has none, the digest it compares is treated as differing from every record. The pre-dispatch taking MUST record the SPEC IDENTITY it used, with its form and its clause provenance, in the dispatch journal, and in its judgement record when it appends one, and MUST supply them to the run, whether it reused a record or appended one. The `dod_gate` node MUST compute its subject digest from that supplied identity rather than from verdicts of its own, so that the node's outcome and the matching host record compare on one digest, and the node still runs. When the run was supplied no SPEC IDENTITY, because the pre-dispatch judgement did not run, the node uses the WHOLE-TREE DIGEST at the resolved commit.
- The GRADING SET: the committed `dispatcher.sandbox_capabilities` array at that commit, as sorted names, or the literal `unpublished`.

The RESOLVED COMMIT is the default-branch commit the dispatch seeds the sandbox from. The Dispatcher MUST resolve it once per dispatch, MUST take the pre-dispatch judgement against it, and MUST seed the sandbox from that same commit. A host taking before dispatch resolves the default branch's current tip. Every recorded verdict MUST carry the SUBJECT DIGEST and the RUBRIC DIGEST. The rubric digest is a SHA-256 over the rubric file's bytes. The subject digest is a SHA-256 over the four components in the order above, each encoded as UTF-8 and preceded by its byte length in ASCII decimal and one newline. Within the components: the HEADINGS are the bodies in reference-line order, each preceded by its heading line; the SPEC IDENTITY is the ASCII prefix `clauses:` followed by the CLAUSE PROVENANCE digest, or `tree:` followed by the WHOLE-TREE DIGEST; the CLAUSE PROVENANCE digest is a SHA-256 over the subject's assertions in Definition of Done order, each contributing its assertion text, then its selected clauses and then its verdict-named clauses as two separately length-prefixed lists, each list sorted by spec file path and then heading line, and each clause contributing its file path relative to the spec root, a NUL byte, its heading line, a NUL byte, its body's byte length in ASCII decimal, a NUL byte and its body; the WHOLE-TREE DIGEST is a SHA-256 over the included files sorted by their path relative to the spec root, each contributing its path, a NUL byte, its byte length in ASCII decimal, a NUL byte and its bytes; the GRADING SET is the sorted names joined by newlines.

A TAKING is one invocation of the judgement: one repository preflight run, one pre-admission judgement, one pre-dispatch judgement, or one run's `dod_gate` node. The first three are HOST TAKINGS. A repository preflight that runs a chain of candidate judges is ONE taking. When every candidate returns a verdict, its outcome is a pass only when every candidate passes, and otherwise a refusal carrying the refusing candidates' findings. When any candidate cannot return a verdict (no eligible model, a timeout, an unparseable reply, or the input bound ending it), the taking did NOT run: it returns no verdict, the preflight exits with its cannot-run code `2`, and the record it appends is a did-not-run record naming that candidate and the cause. When the cause is the input bound, the record MUST also state the subject's size in characters and the number of carried riders the subject held. A did-not-run outcome is never a refusal. The pre-admission and pre-dispatch takings keep their ratified did-not-run routes unchanged. Every taking that runs a judge MUST cause one judgement record to be appended to the item. For a host taking, the taking appends it. For the node, the Dispatcher appends it when it reads the run's `dod_gate` outcome, whether that is a pass or a refusal. Each record names the taking (and the run, for the node), the subject digest, the rubric digest, the outcome with any findings, and, for a chain, each candidate with its outcome. Records are ordered by their ledger creation time, ties broken by comment id. A CACHE-ELIGIBLE record is a host taking's completed verdict record, a pass or a refusal. Did-not-run records, node records and disagreement records are never cache-eligible. Before running the Definition-of-Done judge, and after establishing the governing-heading verdicts its SPEC IDENTITY needs, a host taking MUST look for the earliest cache-eligible record whose subject digest and rubric digest both equal its own. When one exists, the taking MUST return that record's outcome as its verdict, MUST name the record as reused, MUST NOT run any judge or candidate, and MUST NOT append a record. Node records MUST NOT answer a host lookup, and no record ever answers the node, which runs on every run. Whenever two records on an item carry identical subject and rubric digests and opposite outcomes, whichever takings wrote them, or one record's candidates returned opposite outcomes, the Dispatcher MUST append one `dod-judgement-disagreement` row to the dispatch journal and one judgement record of that kind on the item. Each MUST name both digests, the two takings or candidates, each outcome's timestamp, the run where the node is one of them, and each refusal's findings. The Dispatcher MUST record each distinct disagreement exactly once. An item refused by the node MUST rest exactly as any `dod_gate` refusal rests it. Scenario 239 in `scenarios.md` exercises this paragraph.

**Judged before admission.** Before intake routes an implement-kind
item to `ready` — from `backlog` or `pending-approval`, whether through
intake, the approve valve, or groom — the Dispatcher MUST run the same
Definition-of-Done judgement the `dod_gate` node applies (its prompt,
against the item's effective criteria, the referenced specification
headings and the resolved sandbox capabilities). When that judgement runs a Claude model on the host, it MUST authenticate with the Claude subscription credential the Dispatcher selects for a dispatch it would launch at that moment, which is the pool slot the Dispatcher's admission would choose for a dispatch at that moment under the "Admission filters candidates by projected Claude session headroom" paragraph, and, when no pool slot qualifies or no numbered slot is injected, the unnumbered credential. It MUST NOT read the account-selection process's selection to choose the credential. When it falls back to the unnumbered credential, it MUST say so on stderr, naming the reason. The same rule governs the pre-dispatch judgement of the paragraph that follows. When that judgement
would end a run through the structured needs-human ending, the item
MUST NOT be routed to `ready`: it rests where a mechanical finding
would hold it, and the verdict, with each remedy, MUST be appended to
the item as a ledger comment. When that judgement admits the item, intake MUST route it exactly as it would without the judgement. A cache-eligible record on identical digests answers this judgement without running any judge, as "One rubric, one subject" requires of every host taking, and the verdict comment this paragraph requires is then not appended again. When
the judgement cannot be run (no eligible model, a timeout, an
unparseable verdict, or the input bound ending every candidate), intake
MUST record on the item that the
pre-admission judgement did not run and why, and MUST route the item as
it would without the judgement; the in-run `dod_gate` node remains the
backstop, so an unrun judgement never admits anything the gate would
not have seen. A wall finding the judgement did not grade stays
ADVISORY as above. `needs-attention` MUST list, as hygiene facts, each
item held by the pre-admission judgement with its verdict's first
remedy; the ready-item advisory hygiene fact above still applies to
items the judgement admitted or could not judge.
To find each held item's recorded verdict, that listing MUST read the ledger a
bounded number of times per snapshot, independent of how many items are
heldable, for example from markers already on the loaded records or from one
snapshot-wide read, and MUST NOT issue a ledger read per heldable item; the
facts it lists, held items with their recorded remedy and no fact for an item
with no recorded verdict, are unchanged by that read shape. Scenario 174 in
`scenarios.md` exercises this paragraph.

**Judged again before dispatch.** Admission is not the only route to
`ready`: an item also reaches it through `resolve-blocked:<id>:ready`
after a needs-human ending, and its Definition of Done MAY be edited
after it was admitted. So before the Dispatcher claims an implement-kind
item for a dispatch — in the pre-dispatch wall, on the single-item and
the drain paths alike, whatever route brought the item to `ready` — it
MUST run the same Definition-of-Done judgement the "Judged before
admission" paragraph names, against the item's effective criteria as
they stand at dispatch time. When that judgement would end a run through
the structured needs-human ending, the Dispatcher MUST refuse the
dispatch before any claim is taken and before any factory run is
created, MUST name in the refusal the finding text the judgement
produced, and MUST append that verdict, with each remedy, to the item as
a ledger comment; the item MUST NOT be moved out of `ready` by the
refusal. When the judgement admits the item, the dispatch MUST proceed
exactly as it would without the judgement. When the judgement cannot be
run (no eligible model, a timeout, an unparseable verdict, or the input
bound ending every candidate), the Dispatcher MUST record on the item that the pre-dispatch judgement did
not run and why, and MUST proceed as it would without the judgement; the
in-run `dod_gate` node remains the backstop. The Dispatcher MUST reuse the earliest cache-eligible record among those whose subject digest and rubric digest both equal the digests of the subject and rubric this dispatch would grade ("One rubric, one subject"), and MUST NOT run the judgement again or append another comment for a
reused verdict; a reused refusing verdict refuses the dispatch without a
new comment. A refused item MUST be excluded from drain candidate enumeration until the subject digest or the rubric digest it would now be graded by differs from the refusing verdict's,
and `needs-attention` MUST list it as a hygiene fact naming the
verdict's first remedy, exactly as the pre-admission paragraph does for
held items. The did-not-run record MUST likewise be written at most once
per distinct cause until the judgement next runs. A refusal on the
hand-picked `dispatch --item` path MUST exit with the dedicated exit
code `5` of "The pre-dispatch wall" paragraph. Scenario 174 in
`scenarios.md` exercises this paragraph.

**Every host taking is journaled with its input size.** Each host taking of the Definition-of-Done judgement (repository preflight, pre-admission and pre-dispatch) MUST append one dispatch-journal row naming its stage, the candidate that decided it or, when it did not run, each candidate the bound ended, and the total input tokens each named candidate's requests reported, with the same complete, partial or unreported marking. The row lets the share of takings that reach the bound be counted from the journal alone, without reading the item's ledger.

**An item whose judgement the input bound ended is listed as unpreflightable.** When the most recent host taking of an item's Definition-of-Done judgement did not run because the input bound ended every candidate, `needs-attention` MUST list the item as a hygiene fact naming it as unpreflightable, with the subject's size in characters and the number of carried riders the subject held. Every host taking's did-not-run record whose cause is the input bound MUST state both numbers, and the fact MUST take them from the most recent such record. A taking in which only some candidates were ended by the bound is not unpreflightable. The fact MUST clear once a later host taking of that item returns a verdict, reused or fresh, or does not run for a cause other than the input bound. Listing the fact MUST NOT change the item's lifecycle state, and MUST NOT be treated as a refusal.

**Kept current.** The Definition of Done is the statement the proof
stages capture against and the acceptance pass grades against, read from
the dispatch-time snapshot. A factory run MUST NOT deliver behaviour that
differs from the Definition of Done it was dispatched with: when the
implementer determines the section is wrong or incomplete, the run MUST
end through the structured needs-human ending carrying the proposed
amendment as its failure reason, the item rests at `blocked / needs-human`
exactly as any needs-human outcome does, and the human edits the ledger
and releases it through `resolve-blocked`. This is the ONE rest state for
a wrong Definition of Done, whichever stage notices it. The sandbox has no
ledger write path (`constraints.md` §"Factory sandbox credential
constraints"); every ledger write these clauses describe is performed by
the Dispatcher on the host from what the run emits.

**Per-assertion proof mode.** Every gradeable Definition of Done
assertion carries exactly one proof mode from the closed enumeration
`factory_captured` | `host_captured` | `human_attested`. Values MUST be these
self-describing names on every surface that renders, journals or
configures them; a numbered or tiered label MUST NOT be used.
`factory_captured` means the factory's `proof_capture` stage captures
visible proof of the assertion inside the sandbox and the `proof_verify`
stage reproduces it before the run may publish for merge.
`host_captured` means the assertion's proof requires the released,
normally installed artifact or a surface of an operator host that no
sandbox image can carry, and that an agent session can nonetheless
exercise without a human; an agent session captures it on an operator
host and a different session replays it (§"Proof of Done record" → "The
host leg"). `host_captured` is a property of the assertion, independent
of `factory_safety`: a host-routed item's assertions keep their declared
modes, but no factory run executes a host-routed item, so a
`factory_captured` assertion on one cannot be evidenced and is governed by
"The deliverable policy" below.
`human_attested` means no agent session — in a sandbox or on an operator
host — can exercise the assertion's proof (for example a physical
device, or a console that admits only an interactive human login), so a
human captures it against the same written
steps and records it on the pull request. The enumeration MAY gain values
by ratification; a value not in the enumeration MUST be reported as a
Definition-of-Done finding. An assertion's mode is `factory_captured`
unless it appears under a `### Host-captured` sub-heading
(`host_captured`) or a `### Human-attested` sub-heading
(`human_attested`) inside the
Definition of Done section. Each sub-heading MUST carry, before its first
bullet, a line `Reason: <text>`: under `### Host-captured` it names the
host surface or the released-build requirement; under
`### Human-attested` it names why no agent session can exercise the
proof (for example a physical device, or an external administrative
console that admits only an interactive human login). A `### Host-captured` or `### Human-attested`
sub-heading with no non-empty `Reason:` line MUST be reported as a
Definition-of-Done finding by the host-side wall, and the item MUST NOT
enter `ready` until repaired. The mode is declared by the filer at capture
or groom time and validated by the gate; an implementer MUST NOT change
an assertion's mode, and a run that needs the mode changed ends through
the structured needs-human ending with that amendment as its reason.

**The deliverable policy.** The modes are ordered `factory_captured`,
then `host_captured`, then `human_attested`, and an assertion MUST carry
the first mode in that order that can prove it. An assertion whose
subject a published sandbox capability can exercise
(§"Definition-of-Done and Proof-of-Done stages" → "Sandbox
capabilities") — behaviour of the governed repository's own
application, plugin, command-line surface, API, web interface, or test
suite — MUST NOT be declared `host_captured` or `human_attested`; the gate MUST refuse such a
declaration naming the assertion and the sandbox capability that makes it
factory-capturable. An assertion an agent session could exercise on an
operator host MUST NOT be declared `human_attested`; the gate MUST
refuse such a declaration naming the assertion and the host surface that
makes it host-capturable. A `human_attested` declaration is legitimate only for
an assertion whose proof no sandbox capability and no agent session on
an operator host can exercise. In the other direction, a
`factory_captured` assertion whose proof needs a surface no published
capability provides is a finding of the gate, with its remedies
(§"Definition-of-Done and Proof-of-Done stages" → `dod_gate`). Where the
capability set is unknown, the refusals of a weaker mode in this
paragraph still apply on the gate's judgement of the deliverable, and
only the missing-capability finding is withheld. A proof that requires a write-scoped or production credential is
NOT a reason to declare `human_attested`: such an item carries
`factory_safety: needs-host-secrets` and is host-routed, where its proof
is still captured mechanically. More generally, an item whose
`factory_safety` is non-null is host-routed
(§"Admission valve (`ready → active`)") and no factory run executes it, so
no sandbox capability can prove any of its assertions. For such an item the first mode that can prove
an assertion is `host_captured`, or `human_attested` where no agent session
on an operator host can exercise it, and the sandbox-capability refusal
above MUST NOT be applied to it. A `factory_captured` assertion on such an
item MUST be reported by the host-side wall as an ADVISORY
Definition-of-Done finding naming the assertion, the item's
`factory_safety` reason and the remedy of moving the assertion under a
`### Host-captured` sub-heading with a `Reason:` line. The finding MUST NOT
withhold `ready`. The binding of a `factory_captured` record to the merging
dispatch's run identifier is unchanged. Scenario 217 in `scenarios.md`
exercises these sentences.

**Derived routing, never stored.** No field, label or metadata key MAY
store an item-level proof mode. The item-level consequence is computed by
the shared variant-aware acceptance-eligibility decision below from the
assertions: when every gradeable assertion is `factory_captured`, the item
MAY close under an `ai-only` policy on a PASSING post-merge pass whose
criteria leg is the `verified` record (§"Post-merge acceptance
(`acceptance → done`)" → "The proof evidence leg"); when any gradeable
assertion is `human_attested`, the item MUST park in `acceptance` for the
human-attested leg after merge, an effective `acceptance_policy` of
`ai-only` MUST be refused for it by the host-side wall with a message
naming the human-attested assertions and the two remedies (declare
`ai-then-human` or `human-only`, or make the assertion
factory-capturable), and this ONE decision MUST be consumed by every
dispatch entry path — direct `dispatch --item`, hand-picked, drained and
autonomous-loop — so the same item receives the same verdict from each.
When any gradeable assertion is `host_captured`, the item MUST rest in
`acceptance` after merge until a `host_verified` record lists that
assertion as reproduced, under EVERY effective `acceptance_policy`
(§"Post-merge acceptance (`acceptance → done`)" → "The host-captured
leg"). An `ai-only` policy is NOT refused for such an item, because the
host leg is agent-performable: under `ai-only` the item closes on the
acceptance pass that first observes the `host_verified` record with the
factory leg passing and no other leg pending.
Scenario 131 and Scenario 133 in `scenarios.md` exercise this clause;
Scenario 136 exercises its `host_captured` half, and Scenario 139 the
capability checks of "The deliverable policy".

Gradeability is defined at the ASSERTION level: an effective-criteria
set is empty when it contains zero gradeable assertions. A physical-line
parse that counts wrapped continuation fragments as assertions is a
known-defective approximation of this definition (`bd-ib-tfpdya`; the
shipped parser already joins indented continuations and drops
header-only lines — non-indented wraps survive); the walls MUST NOT be
implemented against a parse that counts non-assertable fragments as
gradeable. The completion criterion for that gate is mechanical: the
walls MAY land once (a) a formatting-independence test exists proving
the same criteria text reflowed to different column widths yields the
same gradeable-assertion count, and (b) the discriminating control holds
— a genuinely unmet real criterion still fails while a wrapped fragment
no longer does.

**The shared variant-aware acceptance-eligibility decision.** Exactly ONE
public decision combines the effective-criteria result above with the effective
workflow variant resolved by the same recorded precedence as dispatch. A
groom-kind variant is eligible because its purpose is to produce gradeable
slices. Every other item whose effective `acceptance_policy` is `ai-only` or
`ai-then-human` is ineligible when the effective criteria contain zero
gradeable assertions; `human-only` is eligible with respect to the
gradeable-assertion COUNT because the human, not the AI pass, owns its
grading; every item whose effective workflow variant is implement-kind,
`human-only` included, is ineligible while its Definition of Done section
is absent or carries no valid reference line; a groom-kind variant is
exempt from the section requirement entirely. The decision also derives the item-level
proof routing of "Derived routing, never stored" above. The pre-dispatch wall,
the Dispatcher drain, `next`, the existing `needs-attention` implementation
item composed from `next`, the idle-factory fact, and the
unrunnable-acceptance fact MUST consume this one decision. They MUST NOT
independently parse criteria, approximate workflow resolution, or disagree
about whether the same item is dispatchable.

**The pre-dispatch wall.** The Dispatcher MUST refuse to dispatch an
AI-dispositive item whose effective acceptance criteria parse to zero
gradeable assertions, and ANY implement-kind item whose description
carries no Definition of Done section or whose section carries no valid
reference line or a malformed proof-mode declaration — before any factory
run is created, for both the drain and the hand-picked `dispatch --item`
path; the same section checks MUST refuse the `approve` transition of
§"Work-item state semantics". The refusal MUST name the work-item id,
state that the effective acceptance criteria are empty or ungradeable or
name the missing or malformed element of the section, and exit with the
dedicated documented exit code `5`
(§"Dispatcher exit codes"), distinct from the precondition exit `3`.
The same exit code `5` MUST be used when the pre-dispatch
Definition-of-Done judgement of "Judged again before dispatch" refuses a
hand-picked dispatch.
An explicit hand-picked dispatch remains protected by this refusal even when
candidate enumerations filtered the item earlier. Already-filed items that
predate the wall are not backfilled or exempted: an affected physical `ready`
row stays in place, is excluded from every dispatch-candidate enumeration, and
is surfaced by the `hygiene:unrunnable-acceptance:<work-item-id>` fact until
repaired. The capture, groom, and approve surfaces display the parse so each
item can be repaired when it is next touched. The section-presence,
reference and proof-mode checks are the mechanical form of the intake
checklist's autonomously-verifiable gate; the intake gate count is
unchanged.

**Advise at capture and groom.** The capture and groom front-ends MUST
display the effective-criteria parse result (the gradeable-assertion
count, and the resolved source) whenever they create or redraft an item,
and MUST NOT refuse on an empty parse — filing remains consent-gated and
criteria MAY legitimately arrive at groom time.

**Change-implying criteria and the empty-diff refusal.** Every gradeable
effective acceptance criterion MUST be treated as CHANGE-IMPLYING by
default: an AI-dispositive item with a non-empty gradeable effective
criteria set is presumed to require file changes, so the empty-merged-diff
refusal (§"Post-merge acceptance (`acceptance → done`)" → "The evidence rule" → "Empty merged
diff is ungradeable, not delivered") applies to it. The ONLY exemption is
an item explicitly declared CHANGE-OPTIONAL — a `change-optional`
(no-change-expected) marker on the item, distinct from its
`acceptance_policy` — for which an empty merged diff MUST route to the
item's normal grading path rather than to the empty-diff refusal. An item
MUST NOT be silently exempted: the change-optional property MUST be a
declared property of the item, and the acceptance pass MUST record in its
journal both the change-implying/change-optional classification it used
and, when the refusal fires, the empty-diff evidence leg. Absence of a
declared change-optional marker resolves to change-implying; a malformed
or unknown marker value resolves to change-implying (fail-closed toward
refusing an empty diff, never toward accepting one).

### Dispatcher exit codes

`0` — success / all dispatched green. `1` — non-skipped findings present,
any terminal failed dispatch, or any dispatched item parked in
`acceptance` on a NEEDS_ATTENTION verdict (§"Post-merge acceptance
(`acceptance → done`)" → "A parking verdict is recorded"). `2` — usage error. `3` — precondition
error (missing repo / workflow / item not ready), including the master-CI
deferral of a still-running default-branch run, which is journaled
`deferred` rather than `failed` (the "Master-CI pipeline resolution" rule). `4` — dispatch
completed with the work-item routed to the ledger's human gate
(`blocked / needs-human`) and no terminal failures; the run itself has
terminated (§"A factory run never awaits a human").
`5` — permanent pre-dispatch refusal: the effective acceptance criteria are
empty or ungradeable, or the Definition of Done section is absent or
carries no valid reference line (§"Effective acceptance criteria"), or
the pre-dispatch Definition-of-Done judgement refused a hand-picked
dispatch (§"Effective acceptance criteria" → "Authoring at filing time"
→ "Judged again before dispatch"), or the pre-dispatch wall refused a
spec-change-tier item held for its linked proposal's ratification
(§"Grooming and slice-size calibration" → "The four maintainer
touchpoints", touchpoint 1), or the factory-safety routing predicate routed a
hand-picked dispatch's work item to the host (a non-null `factory_safety`, or a
declared edit under `.github/workflows/` that no
`workflow-scope-override:citation-only` label overrides), or the goal-template
preflight refused a hand-picked dispatch (`--item`) at stage
`goal-minijinja-preflight` because an item field carries a goal-template
opening delimiter (§"Dispatcher policy settings" → "A goal-template opener is neutralized in a comment and refused in a field").
`skipped`-severity findings never flip the exit code.

Every exit-`5` refusal MUST write exactly one line to stderr that begins with
`REFUSED: `, names the work-item id, and states the refusal and its remedy.
The structured outcome MUST still carry the refusal's own status (for example
`host-only-refused`). A refusal that a later retry of the same invocation could
clear MUST NOT use exit code `5`. A drain that skips a host-only item without a
hand-picked `--item` is not a refusal and MUST NOT change its own exit code on
that account. Scenario 315 in `scenarios.md` exercises this rule. For a
goal-template preflight refusal, the `REFUSED: ` line MUST name each offending
field and the 0-based character offset of its first delimiter, its remedy MUST
name the field to edit, and the line MUST NOT quote the delimiter, so a
launcher that copies it into a ledger comment adds no opener. The exit-`5`
cause applies to a hand-picked dispatch only; this rule does not change how a
drain that meets the refusal computes its own exit code. Scenario 321 in
`scenarios.md` exercises that case.

### Post-merge acceptance (`acceptance → done`)

Acceptance is **post-merge / in-production** (observability + reversibility).
The deterministic `just check` stays the HARD **pre-merge** floor (the
in-sandbox janitor gate, which already executes the suite); acceptance
verifies *fit + real behavior* against the **shipped** artifact:

- **`complete` (`active → acceptance`)** MUST **merge-on-green**: the
  Fabro impl run merges via `gh pr merge` with the resolved
  `dispatcher.merge_mode` method (default `rebase`) and `--auto`; entering
  `acceptance` means the change is **merged + live + observable** (OTel →
  Honeycomb; the OOB reflector reads `GROUP BY work.item.id`). The item
  transitions to the observable `acceptance` state instead of straight to
  `done`.
- **`accept` (`acceptance → done`)** is a **post-ship confirmation**
  against tests + telemetry, governed by the item's effective
  `acceptance_policy` — the item's own `acceptance_policy` label when it
  carries one, otherwise the global `dispatcher.acceptance_mode` default
  (§"Dispatcher policy settings"). The **AI acceptance pass** is a
  **read-and-judge of the merged diff and the Proof of Done record against
  the item's acceptance criteria, plus a telemetry watch, yielding a PASS,
  FAIL, NEEDS_ATTENTION, or NO_CHANGE_NEEDED verdict** — never a rubber
  stamp:
  - `ai-only` — a PASSING AI pass with no pending leg confirms and
    accepts the item to `done` autonomously.
  - `human-only` — a human accepts from the console (via the
    `drive` `accept:<id>` valve action). The AI pass still runs, but it is
    ADVISORY.
  - `ai-then-human` (the default) — on a PASSING AI pass the AI's findings
    are surfaced and the item **parks in `acceptance` on the ledger**
    (cheap, durable) until a human gives final acceptance from the
    console (the same `accept:<id>` valve action).

  There MUST be no "release with zero verification" — every acceptance
  carries at least one AI pass.

  **The evidence rule.** A verdict MUST NOT be manufactured from absent
  evidence. The pass judges three evidence legs — the merged diff, the
  effective acceptance criteria (§"Effective acceptance criteria"), and
  the run/telemetry outcome — and:

  - **PASS** requires every leg OBSERVED and passing: an observed green
    outcome, a gradeable merged diff, and a non-empty effective-criteria
    check set with every check passing. For an item with `host_captured`
    or `human_attested` assertions, PASS requires every
    `factory_captured` assertion passing and every `host_captured`
    assertion either passing from a `host_verified` record or pending,
    and lists the pending host-captured assertions and the
    human-attested assertions as pending; a PASS with any pending leg
    (host or human) MUST NOT accept the item to `done` under any policy,
    `ai-only` included. The human-attested
    leg is graded by the `accept` valve, never by the AI pass.
  - **FAIL** requires OBSERVED failing evidence: an observed failing
    outcome, or at least one effective criterion judged failing against
    observed evidence. A FAIL is dispositive rework input (the FAIL
    route below).
  - **NEEDS_ATTENTION** is the verdict when the pass CANNOT OBSERVE what
    a judgment needs: the merged diff is unobservable or ungradeable,
    the effective criteria parse to zero gradeable assertions, or the
    run/telemetry leg is unobservable (distinct from observed-failing).
    Absence of evidence is never failure evidence and never passing
    evidence.
  - **NO_CHANGE_NEEDED** requires OBSERVED evidence that the item's
    change is no longer applicable — already present on the default
    branch, or superseded — and, under a to-`done` policy, closes the
    item with resolution `no-longer-applicable` (the shipped, tested
    auto-close branch). It is a disposition verdict, not a judgment that
    work was done well; it MUST NOT be reached from absent evidence.
    (The verdict is currently UNREACHABLE through the acceptance pass —
    the pass emits only the other three — and this contract gives it
    ratified semantics rather than leaving an undocumented dead branch;
    wiring a reachable producer is implementation work.)

  **Empty merged diff is ungradeable, not delivered.** A merged diff that
  changes zero files — zero hunks under the merged ref — is, for a work
  item whose effective acceptance criteria are change-implying
  (§"Effective acceptance criteria" → "Change-implying criteria and the
  empty-diff refusal"), an UNGRADEABLE merged-diff leg, NOT an observed
  gradeable diff: an empty diff carries no evidence that any
  change-implying criterion is met. The acceptance verdict for such an
  item MUST be NEEDS_ATTENTION, with the merged-diff leg named as the
  absent-evidence leg, and MUST NOT be PASS — grading an empty diff PASS
  is exactly a verdict manufactured from absent evidence, which the
  evidence rule forbids. An empty diff alone MUST NOT be read as
  NO_CHANGE_NEEDED either: "nothing changed in this merge" is not the
  OBSERVED "already present on the default branch, or superseded" that
  NO_CHANGE_NEEDED requires. The only exemption is a work item declared
  change-optional (§"Effective acceptance criteria" → "Change-implying
  criteria and the empty-diff refusal"), for which an empty merged diff
  routes to the item's normal grading path rather than to this refusal.

  **The proof evidence leg.** For every effective assertion whose proof mode
  is `factory_captured` (§"Effective acceptance criteria" → "Per-assertion
  proof mode"), the acceptance pass MUST take its criteria-leg evidence from
  the Proof of Done records on the pull request whose merge it grades,
  selected by each record's binding (§"Proof of Done record" → "The binding").
  It MUST NOT select a record by inferring which runs merged that pull
  request. The pass MUST read every Proof of Done record on that pull request
  and give each one exactly one bind verdict, taking the first rule below that
  applies:

  - `human-attested`: it is a human-attested record, which the human-attested
    leg below governs.
  - `superseded`: a later record on the pull request carries a well-formed
    binding to this pull request and a `Supersedes:` line naming it. It is not
    evidence, and it is never a refusal.
  - `bound`: its binding is well-formed and names this work item and this pull
    request.
  - `bound-elsewhere`: its binding is well-formed and names another work item
    or another pull request. It is not evidence for this item.
  - `legacy-host`: it is a host record that carries no binding. The
    host-captured leg judges it by the host-leg rules of §"Proof of Done record"
    → "The host leg", unchanged.
  - `legacy-matched`: it is a factory record that carries no binding, and its
    run identifier is one the Dispatcher attributes to a dispatch of this item.
    The pass MUST match it against EVERY dispatch of the item that the item's
    dispatch records name, never against a subset resolved as the merging run.
    For each dispatch it MUST accept the Fabro run id, the dispatch id the
    Dispatcher declared to that dispatch's sandbox, and every identifier the
    journal's `resume` records link to that dispatch, transitively (§"Dispatcher
    loop invocation surface" → "Resume from a published pull request").
  - `unbindable`: any other record, that is, one whose binding line is
    malformed or incomplete, one that carries more than one binding line, or a
    factory record without a binding whose run identifier matches no dispatch of
    this item.

  A record COUNTS for this item when it is a factory record whose verdict is
  `bound` or `legacy-matched`, a host record whose verdict is `bound` or
  `legacy-host`, or a human-attested record; a `reproof_required` record that
  counts is still never evidence, as §"Proof of Done record" → "The record"
  requires. A counted record proves the head its binding names, or, for a
  legacy record, the head the record names. A counted `proof_verify` record
  (verdict `verified` or `not_reproduced`) APPLIES to the merge when the head
  it proves is the pull request's head commit at merge, or when a counted
  `carried_forward` record names that merged head and links that
  `proof_verify` record. A legacy record that names no head applies as it did
  before this paragraph was ratified. A counted `proof_verify` record that
  does not apply is reported as stale-head and is not evidence. Each assertion
  is judged on its own section of the newest applicable counted `proof_verify`
  record, whatever that record's record-wide verdict: passing when the section
  carries `Reproduced: yes`, and failing when it carries `Reproduced: no`.
  When that record has no section for the assertion, or its section carries no
  `Reproduced:` line, the assertion is NEEDS_ATTENTION naming that record and
  the missing evidence, and the pass MUST NOT fall back to an older record.
  When no applicable counted `proof_verify` record exists, the record is
  ABSENT, and the assertion is UNOBSERVED, yielding NEEDS_ATTENTION per the
  evidence rule. The host-captured leg MUST take as evidence only host records
  whose verdict is `bound` or `legacy-host`, and keeps the host-leg rules on
  which pull request, build identity and session identity count. When any
  record on the pull request is `unbindable`, the pass MUST NOT grade any of
  the item's `factory_captured` or `host_captured` assertions and MUST NOT
  report any of them UNOBSERVED. Its verdict is NEEDS_ATTENTION for the reason
  that a proof record is unbindable, which is a reported state distinct from
  an ABSENT record; the rework counter is unchanged. The parking record MUST
  name each `unbindable` record by its comment link, state its fault, and name
  the action that clears it: posting, through the posting primitive, a
  correcting record that supersedes it. `needs-attention` MUST surface the
  refusal as an attention fact naming the item, the pull request and each such
  record. The parking record of every pass that parks the item, and the pass's
  journal record, MUST list every Proof of Done record found on the pull
  request with its kind, its run or session identifier, its comment link, its
  bind verdict, the fault of each `unbindable` record and each stale-head
  report, so that a reader sees why each record did or did not count. The pass
  MUST NOT apply merged-diff vocabulary
  matching to an assertion that carries a proof mode; vocabulary matching
  remains only for items resolved from a legacy criteria source, which
  after v114 are only items already in flight; the implementing slice
  SHOULD record the date after which that legacy leg can be retired. The
  merged-diff leg and
  the run/telemetry leg keep their existing semantics. The journal record
  of the pass MUST name, per assertion, the evidence leg it used and the
  record comment it read.

  **The human-attested leg.** An item with at least one `human_attested`
  assertion MUST rest in `acceptance` after its factory-captured
  assertions pass, regardless of policy, until a human-attested record
  exists on its pull request. The `accept:<id>` valve MUST refuse such an
  item while that record is absent, naming the assertions awaiting
  attestation and the record format; `needs-attention` MUST surface the
  pending leg as an attention item carrying the pull request link. `done`
  for such an item means both records observed. Under `human-only` the AI
  pass remains advisory and never disposes, as below.

  **The host-captured leg.** The acceptance pass MUST judge a
  `host_captured` assertion passing only from a `host_verified` record,
  on the pull request of the latest merged run for the item, that lists
  the assertion as reproduced and names a build identity containing the
  merged change. The pass MUST verify that containment itself: the named
  release tag MUST contain the merge commit on the default branch (the
  merge commit is the tag's commit or an ancestor of it); where no
  release applies the record names the default-branch commit exercised
  and the pass verifies the same ancestry. The installed build
  identifier is recorded, not verified. A record that fails the
  containment check, sits on an earlier pull request, or whose replaying
  identity equals its capturing identity is not evidence, and the pass
  MUST report why. A `host_not_reproduced` record that is evidence is a
  FAIL for the assertions it names and is rework input by the FAIL route
  below. With no host record that is evidence the assertion is PENDING:
  the pass lists it as pending the host leg, the item rests in
  `acceptance` under every policy, and no `acceptance_rework_cap`
  attempt is consumed. The `accept:<id>` valve MUST refuse an item with
  a `host_captured` assertion while no `host_verified` record lists it
  as reproduced, naming the assertions and the record format.
  `needs-attention` MUST surface a pending host leg as an attention item
  naming the item, the pull request and the assertions. The pass is
  re-run by `reconcile-merged --item <id>` (§"Dispatcher loop invocation
  surface"), which the host-record posting primitive drives on
  publishing `host_verified` or `host_not_reproduced`; `reconcile-merged`
  driven by hand is the same route. `done` for such an item means the
  `verified` and `host_verified` records both observed.

  **A parking verdict is recorded.** Whenever a pass leaves the item in
  `acceptance`, under any policy — NEEDS_ATTENTION, a PASS with a
  pending host or human leg, a PASS under `ai-then-human` or
  `human-only`, or an advisory FAIL under `human-only` — the Dispatcher
  MUST record on the item, as a ledger comment, the verdict, each
  evidence leg with what was observed or what could not be observed,
  each pending leg, and the action that would move the item. It MUST
  record one comment per DISTINCT (verdict, pending-leg set, proof-record
  inventory), where the inventory is the list of Proof of Done records with
  their bind verdicts, faults and stale-head reports that the proof evidence
  leg requires: a re-run whose verdict, pending-leg set and inventory are
  unchanged appends nothing. The
  dispatch result for such an item MUST report `stage: acceptance` and
  `verdict: <verdict>`, with `status: green` for a PASS that parked or
  has a pending leg and `status: needs-attention` for NEEDS_ATTENTION;
  an advisory FAIL under `human-only` reports `status: green` with
  `verdict: FAIL`, because the pass completed and disposed of nothing.
  The exit code is `0` for `status: green` and `1` for `status:
  needs-attention` (§"Dispatcher exit codes"); no new exit code is
  introduced. `stage: done` MUST be reported only for an item the pass
  closed.

  **Unevidenceable assertions.** An assertion that is not
  `factory_captured` with a record, not `host_captured` with a
  `host_verified` or `host_not_reproduced` record or a pending host leg,
  and not `human_attested` with a record is
  unevidenced, not failed: the pass MUST yield NEEDS_ATTENTION naming it,
  MUST NOT consume an `acceptance_rework_cap` attempt for it, and MUST NOT
  pass it silently. An assertion about another work item, a specification
  scenario, or a plan file is out of scope for this item's evidence and
  MUST be reported as a Definition-of-Done finding by the host-side wall
  and the gate rather than graded. Scenario 132 and Scenario 133 in
  `scenarios.md` exercise these legs; Scenario 136 exercises the
  host-captured leg, and Scenario 138 the parking record, the dispatch
  result and the run-identifier attribution.
- **A FAILING AI acceptance pass under an AI-dispositive policy.** For an item
  whose effective `acceptance_policy` is `ai-only` or `ai-then-human`, a FAIL
  routes the item back to `active` for **fix-forward rework automatically — no
  human is consulted for a fail** — mirroring `reject (rework)`, but
  AI-initiated. The under-cap FAIL disposition MUST stamp the ledger-held
  `rework:pending` label on the item in the same disposition, and the
  dispatch process then ends; EXECUTING the rework is owned by
  §"Rework-pending re-dispatch". "Automatically" in this clause means no
  human is consulted for the ROUTING decision — it does not mean the
  disposing process performs the rework itself. Repeated failure on one item is bounded by
  `dispatcher.acceptance_rework_cap` (§"Dispatcher policy settings"): an item
  that exceeds the cap **escalates to `blocked` / `blocked_reason:
  needs-human`** rather than reworking again. The human `reject` valve is
  retained for human-judgment rejects.
- **A FAILING AI acceptance pass under `human-only`.** Under `human-only` the
  AI acceptance pass is **ADVISORY — it INFORMS, it never DECIDES**. On a FAIL
  it MUST NOT auto-rework the item and MUST NOT dispose of the item in any
  way: the failure is surfaced as an advisory **finding**, and the item
  **stays PARKED in `acceptance`** for the human, who accepts, or uses the
  existing `reject (rework)` / `reject (re-groom)` valve if they concur. An
  auto-rework IS the AI deciding, which is precisely what `human-only`
  reserves to the human; auto-reworking here would let the machine repeatedly
  bounce an item the human explicitly claimed, stripping their
  accept-vs-reject call. The pass still RUNS — it is what satisfies the "no
  release with zero verification" floor for this policy — because `human-only`
  means "no AI DECIDES this", NOT "no AI READS this". (Maintainer-declared
  2026-07-14.)
- **`reject` from `acceptance`** carries a corrective side-effect because
  the change is already live: `reject (rework) → active` is
  **fix-forward** (patch on top of the live change) and MUST stamp the same
  `rework:pending` label, so the human rework path is selectable by the
  identical machinery — the two rework entries MUST NOT diverge in
  selectability (the valve's durable journal record carries the
  provenance; the label is a presence marker); `reject (re-groom) →
  backlog` is **revert the merged change + re-decompose**.

### The NEEDS_ATTENTION verdict

Under EVERY effective `acceptance_policy` — `ai-only`, `ai-then-human`,
and `human-only` alike — a NEEDS_ATTENTION verdict MUST park the item in
`acceptance` for a human and MUST NOT dispose of it: it MUST NOT accept
the item to `done`, MUST NOT route it to rework, MUST NOT stamp the
`rework:pending` marker, MUST NOT move it to `blocked`, and MUST NOT
consume `dispatcher.acceptance_rework_cap`. A cannot-judge verdict is a
truly-unresolvable decision in the sense of §"Every needs-human
escalation still reaches a human": no policy setting MAY auto-dispose
it, including `ai-only` — the delegation `ai-only` grants is the
authority to act ON evidence, not the authority to act without it.

The parking MUST be journaled with the verdict and the absent evidence
leg(s), MUST be surfaced (the existing parked-in-acceptance surfacing),
and the parked item is an orchestrator-owned human wait for the
attention surface — composed through the EXISTING composition classes (a
parked acceptance awaiting the human `accept`/`reject` valves); this
clause introduces no new attention kind. The human disposes of the
parked item with the existing `accept:<work-item-id>` and
`reject:<work-item-id>:rework|regroom` valve actions.

The pass itself still satisfies the "no release with zero verification"
floor: a NEEDS_ATTENTION verdict is a completed AI pass whose finding is
that the evidence was unobservable — it is not a skipped pass.

There is exactly ONE merge model (ship-on-green); the risk dial sits at **the `approve` gate + reversibility**, not a pre-merge acceptance hold. The AI
acceptance pass (the telemetry-reading reflector + a diff/criteria judge
against the merged ref) is an orchestrator-internal realization; it
defaults to read-and-judge + watch telemetry and is upgraded to a
sandboxed exploratory-execution pass only if a bug class is shown to slip
through.

### Consent boundary

These `admit` / `complete` / `accept` / `reject` writes are machine-path
dispositions of already-filed items and are EXEMPT from the
per-operation consent discipline by design (see §"Machine-path exemption
— the Dispatcher"). The Dispatcher MUST NOT create net-new work-items on
its own initiative.

The admission-valve, WIP-cap, and post-merge-acceptance behaviors are
exercised by `scenarios.md` (the WIP-capped top-ranked admission, the manual rest-at-`pending-approval`, the complete-merges-on-green, and the
accept-per-policy scenarios).


## Dispatch pre-launch step attribution and concurrency

A dispatch's pre-launch chain is every step one Dispatcher process runs for a work-item from the moment the process starts until it submits `fabro run` for that item, or until it refuses, defers or abandons the dispatch without submitting. It includes admission, the Definition-of-Done judgement, the ACP checks, the dispatch-claim stamp, recovery routing and the source-checkout preflight. Time spent in this chain is time a launched dispatch holds a launch slot while no run exists on any factory, so the chain MUST be fully attributed, MUST NOT serialize work that does not need to be serialized, and MUST NOT recompute a fact that cannot change within one loop pass.

**Attribution.** For every pre-launch step it runs, the Dispatcher MUST journal one record when the step starts and one when it ends. Each record names the step, the work-item (or, for a step that serves a whole loop pass, the pass), the instant, and on the end record the elapsed seconds and the step's outcome. Process start-up, configuration and ledger reads that precede the first item-scoped step are steps under this rule and are journaled the same way. Between the Dispatcher process's start and its `fabro run` submission for an item, no interval longer than five seconds MAY go uncovered by a journaled step.

**Concurrency.** Pre-launch steps whose inputs do not depend on another pre-launch step's result MUST be started without waiting for one another, and the dispatch MUST NOT wait on a step whose result it does not need. Every ordering between two steps that another section of this contract requires is unchanged, and nothing is submitted to a factory before every step whose refusal would withhold the dispatch has completed. A step that fails or refuses MUST still journal its end record, and the dispatch MUST apply that step's existing refusal rule exactly as it would had the steps run one after another.

**Once per loop pass.** A loop pass is one iteration of `dispatcher.py loop` over the items it selects; a single-item dispatch is a loop pass of one item. A fact whose answer is the same for every item one loop pass dispatches MUST be computed at most once in that loop pass and reused by every dispatch in it. Such facts include the default branch's master-CI state, the sandbox container sweep, the GitHub App reach probe and the ACP session-headroom baseline. A per-pass fact MUST NOT be carried into the next loop pass. This rule does not relax §"Bounded Fabro event reads" → "Pre-launch reads": the dispatch journal and each run's `fabro inspect` are still read at most once per dispatch pass, and a dispatch pass still makes its own first read of each.

**Source-checkout ancestry.** When the source-checkout preflight looks for a remote-tracking ref that contains the dispatch's head, it MUST test the default branch's remote-tracking ref first, and it MUST NOT start one process per remote-tracking ref to answer the question.

## Dispatcher successful terminal evidence

The Dispatcher MUST distinguish successful workflow completion from an engine's
failure to persist its terminal run event. A worker-exit conclusion that reports
exit status zero before emitting a terminal event MUST NOT by itself turn a
completed successful workflow into a failed implementation. Reconciliation of
this conflict MUST use the latest available structured checkpoint for the current
run and matching forge publication evidence; free-form assistant prose, a process
exit code alone, or a successful earlier attempt MUST NOT establish completion.

The checkpoint MUST identify the current run, establish that its configured
successful terminal route has completed all required preceding stages, and carry
successful outcomes for those stages. A checkpoint at the final successful stage
whose next node is the configured successful exit qualifies; requiring a separate
completed exit-node entry MUST NOT exclude that engine representation. A merely
intermediate checkpoint, a failed required stage, cancellation, non-convergence,
or a needs-human route MUST NOT qualify. Publication MUST be observed on the
expected repository and publish branch at the checkpoint's successful published
head; a stale or unrelated pull request, a closed unmerged pull request, a head
mismatch, or unavailable evidence MUST NOT establish successful completion.

When both evidence legs qualify, the Dispatcher MUST continue its ordinary
pull-request and merge reconciliation and report the matching pull request and
its observed publication or merge state. This classification MUST NOT bypass
merge holds, required checks, proof verification, post-merge janitor, acceptance,
or any other ordinary disposition guard. A pending merge remains pending and a
later reconciliation failure retains its normal non-green outcome. Without both
evidence legs, the conflict MUST retain the ordinary non-green disposition.

The dispatch journal MUST identify the run, the structured completion and
publication evidence used, and the conflicting engine conclusion separately from
the successful-workflow classification. It MUST retain the conflict actually
observed through supported engine surfaces, without fabricating server-log
access, timestamps or events. This rule changes Dispatcher evidence reconciliation
only; it makes no claim to repair the engine's run store.

## Dispatcher policy settings

The Dispatcher's routine dispositions are governed by orchestrator-wide
`dispatcher.*` policy settings in the consumer project's `.livespec.jsonc`
(siblings of the existing `dispatcher.wip_cap` and `dispatcher.fabro_bin`
keys). Each setting is a **global default**; a **per-item ledger label
overrides the global default for that one work-item** — the per-item label
WINS over the global, and an item that carries no such label inherits the
global. Admission is the one exception to that precedence: when the
repository commits `dispatcher.auto_approve_ready`, the committed value
decides every item's effective `admission_policy` and a stored per-item
`admission_policy` label does not override it (§"The five policy settings").
The settings are **independent**: no setting implies another, and
there is no master switch. This section composes — never contradicts —
§"Admission valve (`ready → active`)", §"Post-merge acceptance (`acceptance →
done`)", §"Dispatcher grooming behavior", and §"Store-write consent
discipline".

The rationale is granular, orthogonal operator control: the operator can
delegate routine admission while keeping human acceptance (or the reverse),
each setting carrying its own risk, and every safety floor below holds under
every setting independently. Design record: repo `thewoolleyman/livespec`,
`plan/archive/autonomous-mode/handoff.md`, the "SESSION UPDATE — 2026-07-14 (cont. 12)" section
(THE RE-LOCKED DESIGN), together with its "CORRECTION / ADDENDUM" section, which
records the maintainer's ruling that every setting is per-item overridable
EXCEPT `wip_cap`, whose rationale is that a concurrency ceiling is not a
per-item property. Admission departs from that record deliberately: the
maintainer's later ruling of 2026-08-21, "the config file setting should
always be respected", makes a committed `dispatcher.auto_approve_ready` win
over every per-item admission label, because a stale `admission:manual` label
otherwise holds an item at `pending-approval` in a repository whose committed
configuration says to auto-approve; a deliberate per-item hold is expressed as
status `blocked` with its reason recorded on the item, never as an admission
label. `dispatcher.require_invoker` (§"Journal invoker
attribution") is a committed attribution-integrity dial, not a policy
setting of this section: it has no per-item override and is deliberately
not API-configurable.

### Quantitative plan-progress limits

`dispatcher.plan_progress_window_seconds`,
`dispatcher.plan_progress_handoff_threshold`, and
`dispatcher.redispatch_no_progress_limit` MUST be positive committed
integers (not booleans) when their corresponding detector/admission path
runs. These quantitative limits have no inferred numeric default and no
per-item policy label override. Missing or invalid values MUST produce the
configuration finding/refusal specified in the Planning Lane and
across-dispatch progress clauses. Existing within-run caps remain intact.

### The five policy settings

Each is a global default with a per-item label override (for
`dispatcher.auto_approve_ready`, only while the setting is not committed), and
each defaults to its SAFE value:

- **`dispatcher.auto_approve_ready`** (boolean, default **`false`**) — the
  repository setting for an item's effective `admission_policy`: `true` ⇒
  `auto` (auto-approve `pending-approval → ready` without a human); `false` ⇒
  `manual` (rest at `pending-approval` for the human's explicit `approve`).
  Precedence: when this repository's `.livespec.jsonc` commits
  `dispatcher.auto_approve_ready`, the committed value decides the item's
  effective `admission_policy` and a stored per-item `admission_policy` label
  MUST NOT override it. When the key is not committed, the stored per-item
  label governs, and an item carrying no label inherits the shipped default
  (`false` ⇒ `manual`). An admission label is not a hold mechanism: a
  deliberate per-item hold MUST be expressed as status `blocked` with its
  reason recorded on the item. The Dispatcher
