non-empty `LIVESPEC_FABRO_FACTORY`), and an entry of
`dispatcher.overflow_factories`.

Neither changes the factory selection order: an explicit
`--factory` is taken first, then `LIVESPEC_FABRO_FACTORY` when it is set and
non-empty; then, for a resume only, the item's recorded factory; then factory
overflow selection (§"Factory overflow selection") when
`dispatcher.overflow_factories` is non-empty, and otherwise the resolved default factory: the named `dispatcher.default_factory`, or the
registry's fleet default when it is `fleet`. A *resume* here is a dispatch whose route is
`resume`: an invocation of §"Resume from a published pull request
(`resume --item`)", or a `dispatch` or `loop` pass whose recovery routing
(§"Factory-configurable ACP fallback priority" → "Recovery from the failed
run's preserved work") routes the item `resume`. It is the one route that
continues the run lineage the item's recorded factory belongs to. Every other
dispatch is a FRESH dispatch, whatever entry point carries it: a
`dispatch --item`, a `drive` action `impl:<id>` or a loop drain whose item
recovery routing routes `seeded` or `fresh`, an item not released for
recovery, and an item reopened for rework. The classification is per item and
per pass, so one loop wave may carry a resume beside fresh dispatches. A fresh
dispatch MUST NOT read the item's recorded factory as a pin. When no explicit
selection is made it MUST proceed as an unpinned dispatch, so changing
`dispatcher.default_factory` re-routes the next fresh dispatch of every item
onto the new default factory, or through factory overflow selection when it is
configured. The admission claim stamp MUST apply the same order, using the
route recovery routing assigned before the admission valve, so a fresh
dispatch is stamped with the factory it will reach and a resume with the
factory selected by that same order. Every dispatch MUST still write the item's dispatch-factory
record, and every surface that locates an item's live or earlier run through
that record or through the run's own recorded target MUST keep reading it
unchanged: the reconcile survey, a liveness read, the claim stamp's run
target, adapter launch evidence, the acceptance pass, and a resume's read of
its earlier run. A recorded factory name that `dispatcher.factories` no longer declares keeps
its existing treatment for a resume: when no explicit selection is made it is
ignored and the resume proceeds as an unpinned one, so renaming a factory
re-routes the later resumes of every item that recorded the old name onto the
default factory, or through factory overflow selection when it is configured.
A recorded factory name the dispatch reached through `fleet` is the exception: on
a resume it MUST continue to resolve, by that recorded name, as a registry-backed
entry even when the repository does not declare it and even after the
registry's fleet default moves to another factory. A resume carrying such a pin
MUST go to the recorded factory, MUST NOT be silently re-routed to the current
fleet default, and MUST be refused before any claim, naming the factory and the
registry path, when the registry no longer resolves that name. An explicit
selection still takes precedence over it exactly as over any recorded factory. A
fresh dispatch of an item whose recorded factory was reached through `fleet`
resolves the current resolved default factory, or factory overflow selection
when it is configured, and its fleet-derived record pins nothing. A `dispatcher.default_factory`, other than the reserved value `fleet`, that names no
declared entry keeps its existing treatment as well; this clause does not govern it.

A factory name SHOULD name the Fabro server instance it addresses and SHOULD
stay the same for that instance's whole life. A fleet member repository SHOULD
set `dispatcher.default_factory` to `fleet` and SHOULD NOT commit `bin`,
`secret_channel` or `environment` for a registry-backed factory, so that moving
the fleet's default from one instance to another, or changing how that instance
is spoken to, is a change to the provisioning inventory alone. A repository that
names a factory in `dispatcher.default_factory` opts out of that move by design.

### Factory overflow selection

`dispatcher.overflow_factories` is an OPTIONAL committed array of factory
names. Each entry MUST name an entry of `dispatcher.factories`, MUST NOT
repeat, and MUST NOT name the resolved default factory: `dispatcher.default_factory`, or the
registry's fleet default when it is `fleet`. An entry that violates
this MUST be refused before any item is claimed, with a configuration finding
naming the offending value. The key is committed-only: it is NOT declared
API-configurable. When it is absent or empty, selection is exactly the order
of §"Factory addresses resolved from a host registry", and nothing in this
section applies.

Overflow selection applies ONLY to a dispatch that has no explicit `--factory`
and no non-empty `LIVESPEC_FABRO_FACTORY`, and that is either a fresh dispatch
or a resume carrying neither a recorded factory that `dispatcher.factories` still
declares nor a preserved fleet-derived recorded factory, whether or not the
repository declares that name (§"Factory addresses resolved from a host
registry"). A resume carrying a preserved fleet-derived recorded factory is
pinned, takes no overflow ranking, and goes to its recorded factory. For an overflow-eligible dispatch the
candidates are the resolved default factory followed by each entry of
`dispatcher.overflow_factories`, in that order. For each candidate the
Dispatcher MUST read, from that candidate's own Fabro server at selection
time, its non-terminal run count and its own `max_concurrent_runs`. A
candidate has a FREE slot when its count is below its `max_concurrent_runs`.
A candidate whose read fails, times out, is unparseable, or reports a
`max_concurrent_runs` below 1 MUST count as having no free slot.

The Dispatcher MUST place the dispatch on the candidate with a free slot whose
count divided by its `max_concurrent_runs` is smallest; ties go to the earlier
candidate. When no candidate has a free slot, the dispatch MUST be placed on
the resolved default factory. Selection MUST NOT refuse, defer, hold, delay or
count a dispatch on capacity grounds: a dispatch whose chosen factory has no
free slot proceeds to submission on it, where that factory's scheduler queues
it as §"Host concurrency belongs to the Fabro scheduler" sanctions. Selection
does not relax any other requirement: the chosen factory, including a default
factory reached by fallback, is resolved and admitted exactly as an explicitly
selected one, except that the committed-declaration requirement binds only an
actual explicit selection and not an overflow winner, so a registry-backed
default the registry cannot resolve is refused under §"Factory addresses resolved from a host registry".

The chosen factory MUST be recorded as the item's dispatch-factory record
exactly as an explicit choice is, so that a later resume, reconcile or acceptance pass of the same dispatch follows it; a later
fresh dispatch of the item does not. A registry-backed candidate
MUST be resolved through the host registry before its server is read. A
candidate the registry cannot resolve counts as having no free slot for
selection; this does not relax the registry refusal for a dispatch that names
that factory explicitly.

The Dispatcher MUST journal each overflow selection as one record. The record
carries every candidate considered, in order, with the non-terminal run count
and `max_concurrent_runs` its server reported or the reason its read failed.
It also carries the chosen factory and the reason for the choice, which is
`least-utilized-free-slot` or `no-candidate-free-default`. A dispatch to which
overflow selection did not apply journals no such record.

## Built-in ACP node defaults

The factory's ACP nodes run a model the Dispatcher CHOOSES from configuration,
never one the sandbox happens to resolve. This section is the wire contract for
the defaults every node inherits when a repository configures nothing, and for
the Codex-specific rendering rules that outlive the retired per-class shorthand.
A reader MUST be able to predict the literal adapter string a dispatch will
carry from this section together with §"Agent and model catalogs" and §"ACP node
adapter configuration", and check its clear command/args plus the digest of the
complete rendered bytes against the redacted `run_turn.command` record the
factory emits. Raw env values MUST NOT ride that trace.

**Defaults are per node and structured.** The workflow's own declared inputs
(`acp_adapter`, `review_adapter`, `disposition_adapter`,
`dod_gate_adapter`, `proof_capture_adapter`, `proof_verify_adapter`, and
groom-kind-only `pr_adapter`) MUST
express the built-in defaults as structured entries in the grammar of §"ACP node
adapter configuration", never as class-shaped tiers:

| node | built-in default entry |
|---|---|
| `implement`, `fix`, `review_fix`, `proof_capture` | `{"agent": "claude-acp", "model": "claude-opus-5", "effort": "high"}` |
| `pr` (groom-kind only) | `{"agent": "claude-acp", "model": "claude-haiku-4-5", "effort": "high"}` |
| `review`, `disposition` | the entries the workflow declares for its review and disposition inputs |
| `dod_gate`, `proof_verify` | the entry the workflow declares for its review input |

The implementer nodes carry design judgement and default to the strongest
available model. Rendered through the `claude-acp` catalog's environment
mechanism, their defaults MUST render literally:

    ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-opus-5 CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=high npx -y @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp

For an implementation workflow, `pr` MUST be a command stage and MUST NOT
launch an ACP adapter. Its retired `pr_adapter` input MUST NOT be rendered or
consumed. Repository and per-dispatch `pr` overrides resolve according to the
workflow-kind rule in §"ACP node adapter configuration"; a `node_timeouts.pr` override remains
valid for the command stage. The retired `dispatcher.codex_models` setting
continues to refuse, with a diagnostic explaining that its `pr` class has no
ACP replacement for implementation workflows. A groom-kind workflow retains
`pr_adapter` and the existing Claude Haiku 4.5 structured default for its ACP
filing-plan `pr` node, including explicit repository overrides. Through the
environment catalog mechanism its literal rendering MUST remain:

    ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-haiku-4-5 CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=high npx -y @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp

Other node defaults and their rendering remain unchanged.

Model and effort ride the selected catalog mechanism; changing that mechanism
is a committed default change under the verification rule below. The Dispatcher
MUST NOT append a context-window suffix such as `[1m]` to a default model name.

The Dispatcher SHOULD treat the first dispatch after a change to any built-in
default — the entry itself or the catalog rendering behind it — as a
verification run: the run transcript's resolved model MUST be checked against
the pinned model and the result recorded on the work-item that changed the
default, because earlier `claude-agent-acp` versions ignored `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`
and silently ran a smaller model.

**`dispatcher.codex_models` is retired.** A repository routes a node to Codex by
writing a structured entry whose `agent` is `codex-acp` for THAT node; no
class-shaped shorthand exists. A `.livespec.jsonc` that sets
`dispatcher.codex_models` MUST refuse before claim, and the refusal MUST print
the equivalent `dispatcher.acp_nodes` entries — `{"agent": "codex-acp",
"model": <model>, "effort": <reasoning_effort>}` under each node the retired
class covered (`implement`, `fix` and `review_fix` for `implementer`); the
retired `pr` class directs removal because publication is scripted. Measured at ratification, no fleet
repository set the key.

**Every Codex candidate is pinned.** A candidate whose `agent` is `codex-acp`,
primary or fallback, MUST carry both `model` and `effort`, and the Dispatcher
MUST refuse before claim one that does not. The reason is specific rather than
stylistic: the sandbox image bakes a `codex-acp` build whose models-manager
cannot decode the current model catalog, so an unpinned adapter falls back to a
baked static list. Its effective model is then the residue of a decode failure,
and it drifts silently whenever either the catalog or the baked adapter changes.
The one deliberate exception is the explicit un-pinned opt-out: a MANUAL-form
candidate whose `command` is the baked path below and whose `CODEX_CONFIG`
carries no `model` key. It MUST render byte-identically to the un-pinned base
string spelled out below. There is no structured spelling of the opt-out, so an
operator who disables the pin does so visibly, in the escape-hatch form.

**There is no environment override.** The pins MUST NOT be overridable by an
AD-HOC SHELL environment variable read from the orchestrator host's ambient
environment. They are a steady-state cost policy read once per dispatch
on the orchestrator host; such a seam would let an ad-hoc shell re-tier
the whole factory with nothing in the committed record to show for it.

This rule does NOT constrain an adapter's OWN DECLARED `env` map. That map is
committed configuration, resolved through the three layers of §"ACP node adapter
configuration", rendered into the recorded adapter string with each VALUE
preserved byte-for-byte through shell tokenization. The dispatch journal stores
the env KEY, supplying layer, and digest of the exact rendered bytes but MUST
NOT store the value — so it leaves a verifiable committed record
an ambient seam would destroy. The distinction is load-bearing rather than
pedantic: the pins below ride the adapter's declared environment, and reading
this rule as a ban on environment assignments generally would forbid the very
channel this section specifies.

**The rendered form, literally.** The adapter command is the successor
`codex-acp` package invoked AT ITS BAKED PATH:

    /opt/livespec/codex-acp/bin/codex-acp

Its settings ride the command as leading `KEY=value` ENVIRONMENT assignments in
sorted key order, exactly as §"ACP node adapter configuration" requires of every
node's `env` map. Two assignments are defined here. `CODEX_CONFIG` MUST carry a
JSON object merged into the adapter's session configuration; `INITIAL_AGENT_MODE`
MUST carry `agent-full-access` for a write-capable node, and
`read-only` for a node that performs no writes. The `codex-acp` entry of the
agent catalog (§"Agent and model catalogs") MUST render exactly this form. The settings MUST ride the
environment rather than an ACP node attribute because Fabro REJECTS `model` and
`reasoning_effort` as node attributes, so neither a node attribute nor a model
stylesheet is available here. Because the rendered adapter string is
SHELL-TOKENIZED before execution, the `CODEX_CONFIG` value MUST be shell-quoted:
an unquoted JSON object does not survive that tokenization — every quote
character is stripped and the adapter fails to parse its own configuration. The
quoting is part of the byte-identity referent below, so an implementation
rendering bare JSON is NOT byte-identical to the base string.

**The UN-PINNED BASE STRING, spelled out.** The posture keys are ALWAYS present:
an adapter carrying no pin still declares its sandbox and approval posture, just
as the retired `-c` form carried `sandbox_mode` and `approval_policy` on every
rendered string. The un-pinned base string for a write-capable node is therefore,
literally:

    CODEX_CONFIG='{"approval_policy":"never","sandbox_mode":"danger-full-access"}' INITIAL_AGENT_MODE=agent-full-access /opt/livespec/codex-acp/bin/codex-acp

and for a node that performs no writes it is that string with
`INITIAL_AGENT_MODE=read-only`. This is the ONE referent of "the un-pinned base
string" everywhere in this section. Spelling it out is load-bearing rather than
decorative: the opt-out below is defined as byte-identity against it, and the
posture keys live inside `CODEX_CONFIG` rather than on the command, so a reader
cannot reconstruct the un-pinned string from the bare path alone.

**A PINNED adapter is the un-pinned base string with `model` and
`model_reasoning_effort` ADDED inside `CODEX_CONFIG`**, the object's keys
remaining in sorted order. Pinning adds keys to that object and changes nothing
else: it never alters `INITIAL_AGENT_MODE`, never reorders the environment
assignments, and never appends an argument. This is the environment mapping
the `codex-acp` catalog entry declares for a structured candidate's `model`
and `effort`.

**The adapter is identified by its baked path, never by package name.** The
invocation MUST NOT be resolved through `npx` by package name. The baked path
preserves every property the previous `npx --no-install` form was chosen for —
it is version-free, it performs no npm registry round-trip so it runs under
`--network none`, and the baked image remains the single source of truth for the
adapter version — and it adds the one property that form lacked: an unambiguous
IDENTITY. `npx` resolves a package's bin through the SHARED global bin link, so
where two `codex-acp` packages are installed, invoking either package NAME runs
whichever package owns that link. A renderer using the name can therefore emit a
string naming one package while executing another, which defeats this section's
opening claim that a reader can predict the literal adapter string and verify its
command/args plus digest against `run_turn.command`. Relying on package-name resolution to distinguish the
successor from the predecessor is FORBIDDEN.

**Reachable models are bounded by the baked adapter.** The set of models this
adapter can actually reach is a property OF THE BAKED ADAPTER VERSION, not of
this specification: the adapter vendors a Codex generation, and a model the
vendored generation does not know is refused by the backend rather than silently
substituted. A pin naming an unreachable model fails that candidate. When the
failure carries an exact eligible diagnostic, the Dispatcher records a
candidate-scoped hold and re-dispatches the item to the next eligible candidate
of an explicitly configured chain under §"Factory-configurable ACP fallback
priority"; without a further candidate the item waits under that section rather
than failing every dispatch, and without an eligible diagnostic the failure
keeps its existing route.

Therefore the reachable model set MUST be RE-MEASURED from the sandbox against the
real projected credential whenever the baked `codex-acp` version changes, and any
recorded reachable-model table MUST NAME the adapter version it was measured against. A
table attributed to a version the image no longer bakes MUST NOT be carried here:
it reads as current, and a pin chosen from it fails at dispatch time with nothing
in the table to explain why. The concrete post-succession table is produced by
ledger item `bd-ib-nr3pon` and is not asserted by this section; the model
catalog's `openai` entries carry it once measured. The Claude default adapter is fetched by `npx -y` rather
than baked into the sandbox image, exactly as the review adapter is, and
authenticates with the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` the Dispatcher already projects
for the review node.

## ACP node adapter configuration

Every ACP node of the `implement-work-item` workflow — `dod_gate`,
`implement`, `fix`, `review_fix`, `proof_capture`, `review`, `disposition`,
`proof_verify` — runs an adapter the Dispatcher
RESOLVES FROM CONFIGURATION, never from a code-level provider choice.
Switching any node to any model behind any provider protocol, open-weight and
local models included, MUST be a configuration change with no code change.

**Publication adapter by selected workflow kind.** A repository-level
`dispatcher.acp_nodes.pr` entry applies only to a groom-kind workflow's ACP
filing-plan node. For an implementation workflow it MUST be ignored and
journaled as not-applied, naming the entry and the selected workflow kind;
it MUST NOT create a candidate chain or require provider credentials. An
explicit per-dispatch `--acp-node pr=...` override on an implementation workflow
MUST refuse before claim with a removal remedy, because it requests an adapter
for a command stage. Both repository and per-dispatch overrides apply normally
for a groom-kind ACP `pr`. In a mixed-workflow loop this refusal is evaluated per item before claim.
This scoped rule is the sole exception to the
absent-ACP-node layer refusal below.


**The per-node value.** A node's adapter configuration, and every entry of its
`fallbacks` array under §"Factory-configurable ACP fallback priority", is
EXACTLY ONE of two forms. The Dispatcher MUST refuse before claim an entry that
mixes the two or matches neither, naming the entry and the offending field.

*The structured form* is the default spelling. It carries `agent` (string; an
agent id in the committed agent catalog of §"Agent and model catalogs"), `model`
(string; a model reference the catalog resolves for that agent — a bare model id,
or a `provider/model` reference when the agent is multi-provider), and optional
`effort` (string; one of the effort levels the catalog declares for that agent).
It MAY also carry `display_name`, `candidate_key`, `availability_key`,
`availability_signatures` as an OVERRIDE of the value the catalogs derive, and
`pricing` as the fallback table applied only when the catalogs name no price for
the candidate's identity. The Dispatcher MUST render a structured entry into the manual form below
before any layer merge, journal, digest or run input, so every downstream rule
of this section and of §"Factory-configurable ACP fallback priority" applies to
the rendered candidate unchanged. Rendering MUST be deterministic: the same
catalog snapshot and the same entry MUST render byte-identical adapter bytes.

*The manual form* is the escape hatch for any agent or wiring the catalogs do
not cover, including agents no registry lists, and it MUST remain accepted
everywhere the structured form is. It is a table with three fields: `command`
(string; the ACP adapter command, e.g.
`npx -y @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` or
`/opt/livespec/codex-acp/bin/codex-acp`), `env` (table of string to
string; environment assignments prefixed onto the command as leading
`KEY=value` pairs, the mechanism Fabro already parses), and `args` (array of
strings; appended to the command verbatim, e.g. `-c model_provider=<name>`). In
the manual form model and reasoning effort are NOT fields of their own: they
ride in `env` for adapters that read them from the environment
(`ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` on the Claude adapter,
`CODEX_CONFIG` on the Codex adapter), and MAY ride in `args` for an adapter
whose own interface takes them on the command line. A provider behind an
Anthropic-Messages or OpenAI-compatible endpoint is expressed the same way —
`env` carries `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`
on the Claude adapter, `args` carries `-c model_provider=<name>` and its
provider definition on the Codex adapter — so the manual form is
provider-agnostic by construction. Nothing in the manual form is derived:
identity is never inferred from command text. The rendered adapter string MUST
be exactly: the `env` pairs in sorted key order, then `command`, then `args` in
order, single-space separated. Each `env` VALUE MUST be shell-quoted such that
POSIX shell tokenization of the rendered string recovers that value
BYTE-FOR-BYTE. This is stated as a round-trip property rather than as a literal
quote-wrap because the values are operator-supplied and unvalidated: a naive
wrap in single quotes is defeated by a value containing an apostrophe, which
closes the quote early and yields an unparseable command string rather than a
wrong-but-parseable one.

**Three resolution layers, most specific wins.** Each node's value MUST
resolve through, in ascending precedence: (1) the WORKFLOW DEFAULTS — the
declared inputs and their defaults in the workflow's own `workflow.toml`
(`acp_adapter`, `review_adapter`, `disposition_adapter`, and groom-kind-only
`pr_adapter` today),
so a vendored workflow carries its own defaults and the built-in fleet
defaults of §"Built-in ACP node defaults" are expressed there; (2) the
PER-REPOSITORY LAYER — the `dispatcher.acp_nodes` table in the dispatch
TARGET's `.livespec.jsonc`, keyed by node name, read from the target
repository exactly as the tiers are; (3) the PER-DISPATCH LAYER — an explicit
`--acp-node <node>=<value>` argument on `dispatcher.py dispatch`,
`dispatcher.py loop` and the `drive` operation's `impl:<id>` action, whose
value MAY be either form — a legacy adapter string (the manual form) or a JSON
object in the structured form — under the same refusal rules before claim.
Resolution is per node and per FIELD: a more specific layer that sets
`command` or `args` REPLACES that field; `env` MERGES with the more specific
layer's keys winning, EXCEPT that when a more specific layer sets a `command`
that differs from the `command` the less specific layers resolve to, the less
specific layers' `env` is DISCARDED and only that layer's `env` applies. The
comparison is of the rendered `command` field alone, so it holds for both
forms without inferring identity from command text: a structured entry for
the same agent renders the same `command` and keeps merging, while routing a
node to a different adapter drops every inherited model, effort and endpoint
key of the adapter it replaced. A layer that changes `command` for the same
adapter (a different install path or package pin, say) MUST therefore restate
any `env` it needs. Scenario 233 in `scenarios.md` exercises this rule. A layer that names a node not present in the workflow
MUST refuse the dispatch before any run exists, naming the node.

**`dispatcher.codex_models` is retired.** No shorthand expands into this layer.
A `.livespec.jsonc` that sets `dispatcher.codex_models` MUST refuse before claim
with the equivalent `dispatcher.acp_nodes` structured entries printed, per
§"Built-in ACP node defaults".

**The per-dispatch layer is a recorded argument, never an environment
variable.** The no-environment-override rule of §"Built-in ACP node defaults"
holds for every layer: an ad-hoc shell MUST NOT be able to re-tier the factory
with nothing in the committed record or the journal. The per-dispatch value
MUST be journaled on the dispatch record as its redacted structural
representation plus digest, not as raw env values. This argument is an OPERATOR
argument: the console's factory-drain launcher of §"Control surface and audit"
passes NO per-run argument, and this section does not change that.

**The supplying layer is visible in the run record.** For every node the
Dispatcher MUST journal, on the dispatch record, the adapter's command/args,
each env KEY and its supplying layer, and a deterministic digest of the exact
rendered adapter bytes. It MUST NOT journal raw env values. This redacted
structural form lets a reader distinguish workflow default, repository override,
and per-dispatch override without re-deriving it while preserving the secret
floor of §"Factory-configurable ACP fallback priority".

**Keys are committed-configuration-only.** `dispatcher.acp_nodes`,
`dispatcher.agent_catalog` and `dispatcher.model_catalog` belong to the
committed-configuration-only class of §"Control surface and audit" (the class
`dispatcher.codex_models` occupied before its retirement); they are outside the
API-configurable key set and do not trigger the console Settings lockstep.

**Commit-time resolution check.** The repository's `just check` aggregate MUST run a target named `check-acp-preflight-config`. That target MUST evaluate the repository's committed `.livespec.jsonc` through the same ACP node resolution the Dispatcher applies before claim: the three resolution layers, the structured and manual candidate forms, and §"Agent and model catalogs". It MUST NOT use a second, independently written validator. The target MUST exit non-zero and print the refusal text, including the offending node and field, whenever that resolution returns a configuration refusal. Configuration refusals are the refusals this section and §"Agent and model catalogs" define for an entry that mixes forms, names an agent absent from the agent catalog, names a model the model catalog does not declare for that agent, or otherwise cannot be rendered. The target MUST NOT fail on an availability condition: an unexpired availability hold, an outstanding availability confirmation or a session-headroom wait is not a configuration defect. To keep its verdict deterministic, the target MUST read no dispatch journal, MUST NOT probe a credential, MUST NOT apply a session-headroom policy and MUST NOT query a factory. It MUST therefore reach the same verdict on a host with no network access. Because the target is part of `just check`, it runs wherever `just check` runs, locally, in pre-push and in CI, so a committed configuration whose candidate chain cannot resolve is refused before it can reach a dispatch.

**Per-node context declaration.** A node's value, in either form, MAY carry one optional field, `loads`: a table of four arrays of strings — `instruction_files` (paths relative to the governed repository root, for example `AGENTS.md`), `skills`, `plugins` and `mcp_servers` (names as the node's agent identifies them). `loads` resolves through the same three layers as every other field, and a more specific layer that sets it REPLACES it whole; its arrays never merge across layers. When some layer sets `loads` for a node, the Dispatcher MUST launch that node's agent so that its session loads EXACTLY the declared set: every declared item, and no instruction file, skill, plugin or MCP tool — from the governed repository or from the sandbox user's agent configuration — that the declaration omits. A declared instruction file MUST reach the session whichever file name the node's agent reads it under, so declaring `AGENTS.md` covers a `CLAUDE.md` symlink to it. A node whose `loads` arrays are all empty loads none of the four kinds. When no layer sets `loads` for a node, that node loads what its agent loads by default. Harness settings the Dispatcher itself writes into the sandbox are not context under this rule and MUST still apply. A declared item the Dispatcher cannot deliver to that node's agent MUST refuse the dispatch before claim, naming the node and the item. The Dispatcher MUST journal each node's resolved `loads`, and the layer that supplied it, on the dispatch record beside the adapter record above. The bundled `implement-work-item` workflow's defaults MUST set `loads` on every one of its ACP nodes: `implement`, `fix` and `review_fix` declare the governed repository's instruction file, and every other ACP node declares all four arrays empty. Scenario 275 in `scenarios.md` exercises this rule.

**Verification.** A negative control per layer MUST exist: for each of the
three layers, a test that sets a value at that layer and a conflicting value
at every less specific layer, and asserts the more specific value renders.
Proving that an arbitrary adapter with an `env` map and a provider definition
renders and takes precedence MUST be done hermetically — a stub endpoint or
the fake backend — and MUST NOT require network reachability of any real
provider from the factory.

Implemented by ledger item `bd-ib-tsna`; `bd-ib-un226z` (per-node provider
assignment) is superseded by this section.

## Agent and model catalogs

The structured candidate form of §"ACP node adapter configuration" resolves
through two committed, versioned catalogs the plugin ships. Both are SNAPSHOTS:
the Dispatcher MUST NOT fetch a registry, a provider, or a catalog service at
dispatch time, so a dispatch depends only on committed bytes.

**The agent catalog.** Entries are keyed by Agent Client Protocol registry agent
id (`claude-acp`, `codex-acp`, `opencode`, `grok-build`, `glm-acp-agent`, and
the rest of the registry's population). Each entry MUST carry: the launch
distribution rendered from the registry's `npx`, `uvx` or per-platform `binary`
distribution at a pinned agent version, in the manual-form shape (`command`,
`args`, `env`); the agent's display name; its account domain, an opaque
`availability_key` naming the allowance the agent draws on; the mechanism by
which the agent takes `model` and `effort`, EXACTLY ONE of `protocol` (ACP
session config options, §"Factory-configurable ACP fallback priority" →
"In-protocol model and effort selection") or an explicit per-agent environment
or argument mapping; whether the agent is multi-provider, in which case `model`
MUST be a `provider/model` reference; and the effort levels it declares. The
catalog MUST record the registry snapshot digest and the date it was seeded
from. A repository MAY add or override agent entries under
`dispatcher.agent_catalog` in its `.livespec.jsonc` under the same closed
grammar; an unknown key refuses before claim. At this ratification the
`claude-acp` entry declares the environment mapping (`ANTHROPIC_MODEL`,
`CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL`) and the `codex-acp` entry declares the baked path
and `CODEX_CONFIG` mapping of §"Built-in ACP node defaults", so every rendered
byte those sections ratify is preserved.

**The model catalog.** Entries are keyed by `provider/model` and carry the
canonical model id, aliases, the four USD-per-million prices in the `pricing`
shape of §"Factory-configurable ACP fallback priority", and measured
availability signatures in that section's signature grammar, including a
`protocol.message` form for every provider-limit diagnostic it carries. It MUST
be seeded from upstream Fabro's model catalog where that catalog carries the
model and extended for models it does not, including the ratified Codex
ChatGPT-account diagnostic. A repository MAY add or override entries under
`dispatcher.model_catalog`. A structured entry MAY carry a per-candidate `pricing` table. The model catalog entry the candidate's identity names is consulted first; the per-candidate table applies only when that identity resolves to no catalog entry, which is the manual-form case and the case of a repository-added model the shipped catalog does not declare. A per-candidate table never overrides a catalog price for an identity the catalog declares. When a repository wants a different price for a catalogued model it changes the catalog through `dispatcher.model_catalog`, never through a per-candidate table. A per-candidate `availability_signatures` override on a structured entry wins over the catalog value, and the all-or-none pricing rule applies to catalog entry and override alike.

**Resolution and derivation.** For a structured candidate the Dispatcher MUST
resolve `agent` in the agent catalog, then `model` in the model catalog for that
agent's provider (or for the provider a `provider/model` reference names), and
MUST refuse before claim when either lookup fails or when `effort` is not one of
the agent's declared levels. The resolved entries supply the rendered adapter,
the derived identity, the pricing and the signatures. Derived identity, when not
overridden, is: `display_name` = the agent's display name followed by the
model's display name; `candidate_key` = the canonical `<agent>/<provider>/<model>`
triple; `availability_key` = the agent entry's account domain. Two structured
entries naming the same agent and model therefore share identity across nodes
by construction, which is the cross-node reuse §"Factory-configurable ACP
fallback priority" already permits. Built-in identity attaches to a structured
candidate by catalog resolution, never by byte-equality of the rendered command;
byte-equality remains the rule for the manual form. The cost path MUST price a
structured candidate through the model catalog first and a per-candidate
override second, and the exact-identity rule (one trailing `-YYYYMMDD` suffix
stripped, no broader prefix match) applies to the catalog key.

## Factory-configurable ACP fallback priority

An ACP node MAY carry an ordered, provider-generic candidate chain so an
observed allowance outage or exact model removal does not make one configured
adapter a single point of failure. The Dispatcher, not the Fabro engine,
consumes the chain: at every dispatch and every re-dispatch it MUST render, for
each ACP node, exactly ONE candidate as that node's literal adapter — the
candidate "Per-node selection" below chooses — and the engine runs that one
adapter with no knowledge of the other candidates. Ordered fallback therefore
happens BETWEEN runs, through "Provider-limit release and re-dispatch" below,
never inside one node visit. This is an additive configuration feature:
when no fallback metadata is present, or `fallbacks` is an empty array, adapter
resolution and rendered command bytes MUST remain byte-identical to §"ACP node
adapter configuration". In particular, an unconfigured `review_fix` node retains its workflow
default, and an explicit structured `review_fix` entry remains candidate zero.
For implementation workflows the command stages `pr_refresh` and `pr` have
no candidate chains. The groom-kind ACP `pr` keeps ordinary candidate-chain
semantics and its admission-required membership remains graph-derived; its
filing-plan-only work issues no remote Git effect.

**Resolve the primary before attaching the chain.** The Dispatcher MUST first
resolve candidate zero through the existing workflow-default, explicit
repository entry, and per-dispatch layers in their current order, rendering a
structured entry through the catalogs of §"Agent and model catalogs" at the
layer that set it. Only then may repository identity metadata and `fallbacks` be
attached. A fallback-only `acp_nodes` table MUST NOT shadow a more specific
primary or restore the workflow default. Built-in identity attaches to a
structured primary by catalog resolution and to a manual-form primary only while
its rendered bytes match a built-in; a fallback-enabled manual-form arbitrary
primary MUST carry explicit identity and MUST NOT retain the replaced built-in's
identity.

An identity-less arbitrary single-adapter override with no fallback metadata
retains the v107 containment path and cannot mint or consume current typed
holds. It is conservatively covered by every unexpired legacy provider record
and continues to mint legacy records through v107 cause-text attribution;
declaring explicit identity is the only route out of that blanket. Identity MUST
NOT be inferred from command text.

Every explicitly identified candidate, and every candidate in a fallback-enabled
chain, carries non-empty, non-secret `display_name`, `candidate_key`, and opaque
`availability_key`. Display text is never a machine key. The pair
`(availability_key, candidate_key)` identifies one candidate entitlement and MAY
be repeated across nodes when that identity is truly shared; different accounts
or routers MUST use different keys. For a structured-form candidate those three
fields derive from the catalogs as §"Agent and model catalogs" specifies unless
overridden. A MANUAL-form fallback entry additionally carries a complete
`command`; omitted `args` and declared adapter `env` mean empty values; a
structured-form entry carries none of these and renders them from the catalogs.
No entry of either form MAY inherit another candidate's command, args, declared
env, model, identity, signatures, or pricing. Container-level credentials remain shared by
the existing Worker credential projection; this clause promises no candidate-
level secret isolation.

For a fallback-enabled node, `command`, `args`, and `env` are public committed
data and MUST contain no literal credential, token, or secret reference.
Candidate credentials MUST arrive only through §"Worker credential projection";
the projected key is supplied through the uncommitted overlay directly to the
child process and omitted from the rendered adapter string, run input, run
record, and trace. A new provider credential channel requires its own ratified
change. A no-fallback legacy node retains v107's arbitrary-adapter env behavior
and Scenario 88 unchanged. Execution still receives the exact
resolved adapter bytes, but the existing journal rule is narrowed for secrets:
journals, traces, events, diagnostics, and refusals MUST store a redacted
structural form containing command/args, env key names and supplying layers plus
a deterministic digest, never raw env values or the full candidate chain.

The legacy string-valued `--acp-node NODE=ADAPTER` remains valid for a node with
no new-grammar metadata. It MUST refuse before claim on a new-grammar-enabled node,
because it carries no stable candidate/domain identity; it MUST NOT become hold-
exempt, retain stale metadata, or infer identity from command text. A future
structured chain override requires separate ratification. Because the
Dispatcher renders exactly one literal adapter per node, a new-grammar-enabled
dispatch requires NO Fabro engine capability for fallback. The Dispatcher MUST
NOT refuse a dispatch because the resolved factory server does not advertise a
fallback-chain capability; the only engine capability gate that remains is the
`config_options` gate of "In-protocol model and effort selection" below, which
applies only to a dispatch whose selected candidates use it. Unknown, duplicate-key, incomplete,
wrong-typed, or conflicting fallback configuration refuses before claim or run.

"New-grammar-enabled" means identity, signature, pricing, the structured form
(`agent`), or a non-empty fallback
field is present; `fallbacks: []` alone remains the byte-identical no-op. The
enabling repository MUST commit `dispatcher.minimum_release` at or above the
first plugin release that implements Dispatcher-level fallback; this existing operator floor makes older
Dispatchers refuse rather than silently ignore the feature. From that release
onward every unknown `acp_nodes` key refuses before claim. Any remaining engine
capability (the `config_options` gate) is read from the dispatch's resolved
factory server, never a local binary. The
existing `acp_nodes`-wins rule applies only to the primary fields actually set
(`command`/`env`/`args` in the manual form, `agent`/`model`/`effort` in the
structured form); identity-only and fallback-only fields attach after the
primary renders.

**The candidate grammar is closed.** A candidate object is EXACTLY ONE of the
two forms of §"ACP node adapter configuration", and its key set is closed to the
keys of that form. The STRUCTURED form admits `agent`, `model`, `effort`, and the
override keys `display_name`, `candidate_key`, `availability_key`,
`availability_signatures` and `pricing`. The MANUAL form admits `command`, `args`,
`env`, `display_name`, `candidate_key`, `availability_key`,
`availability_signatures` and `pricing`. A node's value in either form also admits the
optional `loads` field of the "Per-node context declaration" paragraph of
§"ACP node adapter configuration". Any other key, and any object that
carries `agent` together with `command`, `args` or `env`, MUST refuse before
claim. `config_options` is NOT a configuration key: it is a field of the node
adapter the Dispatcher renders for a selected candidate (see "In-protocol model
and effort selection" below) and MUST refuse if it appears in committed
configuration. A
structured candidate with overrides, and a manual candidate, look like this:

```jsonc
{
  "agent": "codex-acp",
  "model": "gpt-5.5",
  "effort": "high",
  "availability_key": "chatgpt-team-account"   // override of the catalog account domain
}
```

```jsonc
{
  "display_name": "operator text",
  "candidate_key": "stable-candidate",
  "availability_key": "default-domain",
  "command": "adapter",
  "args": ["literal", "non-secret"],
  "env": {"NAME": "non-secret value"},
  "pricing": {
    "model": "exact-emitted-model",
    "input_usd_per_million": 0.0,
    "output_usd_per_million": 0.0,
    "cache_write_usd_per_million": 0.0,
    "cache_read_usd_per_million": 0.0
  },
  "availability_signatures": [
    {
      "source": "protocol.machine_code",
      "machine_code": "exact.nonempty.code",
      "cause": "model_unsupported",
      "scope": "candidate"
    },
    {
      "source": "protocol.message",
      "all_literals": ["usage limit", "requested model"],
      "exit_code": 1,
      "cause": "quota",
      "scope": "availability-domain",
      "hold_key": "optional-domain-override"
    }
  ]
}
```

`source` is exactly `protocol.machine_code`, `protocol.message`,
`process.terminal_diagnostic`, or `turn.final_output`. `cause` is exactly `quota`, `rate_limit`,
`provider_capacity`, `provider_server_unavailable`, `model_unavailable`,
`model_not_found`, `model_unsupported`, or `model_not_entitled`. `scope` is
exactly `availability-domain` or `candidate`. A machine-code source requires one
non-empty exact `machine_code` and forbids `all_literals`; the
`protocol.message` and `process.terminal_diagnostic` sources require a
non-empty array of non-empty `all_literals` and forbid `machine_code`. A
`turn.final_output` signature requires one non-empty `final_text`, the complete
measured refusal text the provider delivers, and forbids `all_literals`,
`machine_code` and `exit_code`; it MUST declare `scope: candidate`. No other
source accepts `final_text`.
An optional `exit_code` is an integer from 1 through 125 and only refines the
required discriminator; it is never sufficient by itself. Domain scope MAY
carry a non-empty opaque `hold_key`, defaulting to `availability_key`. Candidate
scope forbids `hold_key` and keys exactly on
`(availability_key, candidate_key)`. Duplicate identities within one node chain
and statically identical conflicting signatures MUST refuse the complete
configuration; cross-node identity reuse is intentional. A candidate belongs to
its `availability_key` domain plus every override `hold_key` declared by its
domain signatures. If distinct signatures nevertheless match one runtime
diagnostic with different cause/scope/key dispositions, the failure is
non-eligible and surfaced as ambiguous, and it creates no hold; runtime first-
match choice is forbidden.

Literal-based text matching is a conjunction after Unicode case-folding and
whitespace normalization, never a regular expression. The Dispatcher applies signatures to
the failing node's recorded failure as read from the run's resolved factory:
a `protocol.machine_code` signature matches only where the engine preserved the
provider's structured payload; a `protocol.message` signature matches the
provider's message text, including the engine form that preserves ONLY the
failure message text and no structured payload; a `process.terminal_diagnostic`
signature matches the separately captured adapter startup/termination
diagnostic. Structured fields MUST be parsed as fields, independent of JSON
whitespace and key order, never matched as a byte substring. When the run ended
at the workflow's `needs_human` terminal and the terminal message no longer
carries the provider's sentence, the Dispatcher MUST read the failing node's own
recorded attempt outcome before classifying, and MUST NOT classify from the
needs-human script's own output. Matching never reads an arbitrary exec-output
tail, prompt, tool/test/review output, or run log, and it reads agent response
text ONLY through a `turn.final_output` signature. A `turn.final_output`
signature applies only to an agent node attempt that the engine recorded as
succeeded, and it is not a conjunction of literals. Both the recorded turn
output and the signature's `final_text` are normalized by Unicode case-folding,
collapsing every maximal run of whitespace to one space, and removing leading
and trailing whitespace. The signature matches only when the normalized output
ENDS WITH the normalized `final_text` at a sentence boundary: the output either
equals that text, or the character immediately before the text is `.`, `!` or
`?`, or the text is preceded by exactly one space whose preceding character is
`.`, `!` or `?`. Nothing else satisfies it. (The measured output that motivated
this form reads `I'll make no changes.Selected model is at capacity. Please try
a different model.`, with no space after the preceding terminator.) Refusal words that
appear anywhere other than that tail do not match, so a turn that discusses a
refusal and then continues is not a refusal; and an output that ends with the
refusal text marked as a quotation, by a closing quotation mark after the text
or by a lead-in such as a colon immediately before it, does not match. An output
whose final sentences reproduce the refusal text unmarked is textually
indistinguishable from the refusal itself and DOES match; that
misclassification is accepted, because a match only mints a candidate hold and
journals a warning, and it releases the item only under the unrecovered-cause
condition of "A provider refusal booked as a successful turn is a failed
attempt" below. The Dispatcher MUST read that
recorded output from the run's resolved factory, exactly as it reads a failure
for the other sources. Structured
machine codes take precedence. Authentication,
command-not-found, cancellation, node deadline or stall expiry, generic HTTP
400/404, remote-compaction 404, malformed command/configuration, signal exit,
unattributed sandbox/DNS/transport failure, code/test/review/tool failure, and
non-convergence are non-eligible before configured matching: they mint no hold,
are not released for re-dispatch, and keep their original identity and their
existing route, except that an adapter launch failure is released without a
hold under "Adapter launch release and re-dispatch" below. A mere pre-turn
failure is not provider evidence.

Provider and entitlement attribution MUST come from the recorded executed
candidate identity of the failing node attempt. A shared message literal MUST
NOT infer a different provider or account: a sentence that more than one
provider emits is attributed to the candidate that actually ran.

Built-in Claude and Codex candidates MUST carry exact, measured mappings for
stable diagnostics exposed by the pinned adapters, including the recorded
ChatGPT-account diagnostic that names the requested model as unsupported. The
generic HTTP 400 remains non-eligible; the exact model-naming discriminator is
candidate-scoped. Every provider-limit mapping MUST exist as a
`protocol.message` signature, and additionally as a `protocol.machine_code`
signature where the adapter emits a structured token, so that detection survives
an engine that keeps only message text. A `turn.final_output` form is the one
exception: it describes a refusal the adapter delivers as turn text on an attempt
the engine recorded as succeeded, so there is no recorded failure for a
`protocol.message` form to match, and none is required. The measured minimum set at this
ratification, each `cause: quota` and `scope: availability-domain`, is: for
`claude-acp`, the session-limit form (literals `hit your session limit`), the
generic limit form (literals `hit your limit` and `resets`), the usage-limit form
(literals `hit your usage limit`), and the organisation spend-limit form
(literals `org` and `spend limit`); for `codex-acp`, the structured usage-limit
field in BOTH its camelCase spelling (`codexErrorInfo` carrying
`usageLimitExceeded`) and its snake_case spelling (`codex_error_info` carrying
`usage_limit_exceeded`), and the message forms (literals `hit your usage limit`;
literals `usage limit exceeded`). Both measured Codex spellings MUST be
recognized. The measured minimum set additionally carries one form that is
neither `cause: quota` nor domain-scoped: for `codex-acp`, the capacity form,
source `turn.final_output`, `cause: provider_capacity`, `scope: candidate`,
`final_text` `Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.`
The capacity form is candidate-scoped to `codex-acp`: a `claude-acp` attempt
whose output ends with the same words MUST NOT match it. A Claude `rate_limit` kind alone does not establish quota
exhaustion; its measured message discriminator is required. A non-dispositive
structured kind MUST NOT suppress that discriminator. Every listed measured
form MUST be exercised against its recorded executed candidate, including
message-only payloads and both structured Codex spellings. A newly measured
provider-limit form is added to this set by a committed change to the built-in
signatures or the model catalog, never by loosening a literal into a broader
match. Every Codex primary or fallback continues to obey the v107 pin, posture,
baked-path, and empty-model opt-out rules. Consequently the v107 reachability
statement is narrowed: an unreachable pin is a failure of that candidate; when
its exact typed cause is eligible it mints a candidate hold and the item is
released for re-dispatch to the next eligible candidate, and otherwise it keeps
its existing route. Verification-run guidance applies to every new or changed
candidate.

**Preflight consumes versioned observed holds.** A current record carries at
least `scope`, opaque `hold_key`, optional `candidate_key`, stable
`observation_id`, occurrence time, bounded expiry, and explicit
`schema_version: 1`. Unknown versions MUST be preserved and surfaced as
unobservable, never interpreted as v1, rewritten, or allowed to mint a hold. A domain record skips
every candidate covered by its selected hold key; a candidate record skips only
the exact identity pair. Legacy provider-only records remain readable,
clearable by the legacy valve, and effective until retirement against built-in
candidates whose compatibility alias names that provider plus identity-less
legacy candidates, which every live legacy record covers. Explicitly identified
candidates MUST NOT be broadened to unrelated identities. Typed candidate evidence takes
precedence over legacy cause-text attribution when a chain executed.

A hold MUST come from an actual candidate attempt: a typed eligible failure
classified from a failed node of a terminal run, whichever terminal the run
reached, or a refused availability confirmation turn (see "Availability is
re-confirmed after expiry" below), which runs the candidate's own adapter and
is therefore an actual attempt. Expiry is computed from occurrence time and
never from ingestion. No hold may come from credentials, catalogs, the
admission-time credential-usability probe, predicted health, price, model
strength, or provider reset claims. The Dispatcher MUST retain configured order
after filtering.

**A provider refusal booked as a successful turn is a failed attempt.** An
agent node attempt that the engine recorded as succeeded, but whose turn
matches a `turn.final_output` signature of its executed candidate, MUST be
treated by the Dispatcher as a FAILED attempt of that candidate with the
matched cause and scope, for every purpose of this section. It mints the
candidate hold that the signature declares, with expiry computed from the
attempt's completion instant. It journals the model-fallback warning exactly
as a failed attempt does. It MUST NOT count as a successful completion under
"A record is falsifiable only by later matching execution", under the
warning-retirement rule, or as a successfully completed availability
confirmation turn. Such an attempt is the failing node attempt for
"Provider-limit release and re-dispatch" ONLY when it is the unrecovered failure
responsible for the run's terminal disposition, as that paragraph requires: the
run reached a terminal other than its successful exit through the reclassified
attempt's own outcome, or through retries of the same node every one of which
was also reclassified, and no later attempt of any node, agent or non-agent,
failed on its own. In that case the Dispatcher MUST perform the release,
including returning the item to `ready` with no `blocked_reason`, and MUST NOT
rest the item at `blocked / needs-human`. When a later failure determined the
terminal instead, that later failure keeps its own classification and route,
including a non-eligible failure's route, and the reclassified attempt does not
release the item. A run that reaches its successful exit keeps its outcome.
The run's overall outcome, successful or not, never retires the reclassified
attempt's hold or warning; their existing retirement rules still apply. The release
record MUST name the matched signature's source as `turn.final_output`.

**Holds are per provider domain and discoverable host-wide from factory-native
run records.** A domain hold keyed on a provider allowance's `availability_key`
is the per-provider hold; a candidate hold keys on the exact identity pair.
Availability evidence MUST be discoverable host-wide from the factory's native
run records, without an optional per-repository peer list. Each recorded attempt
MUST identify its resolved factory, repository, run, node attempt, candidate
entitlement, occurrence time, and typed availability outcome. Hold observations
and their retirement evidence MUST remain reconstructible after any
repository-local dispatch journal is removed. Dispatch journals MAY record audit
references but MUST NOT be the sole authority for holds. The participating
factory instances are every factory declared under `dispatcher.factories`, every
implicitly declared factory, and every recorded-target factory (§"Factory
addresses resolved from a host registry"); each Dispatcher MUST read
availability evidence from every participating factory. A participating factory
whose evidence cannot be read, including a recorded-target factory the registry
no longer resolves, has the existing unavailable-evidence treatment: losing a
factory's address does not retire a hold recorded there, and its holds retire
only through the confirmations and operator clearances this section defines, so an
observation made by any repository's run on a participating factory is visible
to every repository that dispatches to it. Observations, successful availability
confirmations, and operator clearances MUST each be recorded as a factory-native
record on the participating factory whose evidence they create or retire — a
confirmation by the factory run that confirmed it, and an operator clearance by
a minimal factory-native record whose recorded outcome carries the clearance's
exact identity, actor, time, and reason — so retirement is reconstructible from
the same source as observation. Reading other repositories' recorded attempts
for this purpose is availability evidence, not counted-claim bookkeeping, and
the tenant-scope clause of §"Host concurrency belongs to the Fabro scheduler"
does not govern it. No separate hold sidecar file, cache, or store MAY hold or
mirror this evidence.

An unreadable or incomplete evidence source is unavailable, not an empty hold
set. The Dispatcher MUST surface that condition and retry observation on a
bounded cadence. It MAY continue with candidates whose availability evidence is
independently complete; it MUST NOT treat an unobserved candidate as confirmed
unheld. This condition MUST NOT create a needs-human decision. A hold, current
or legacy, MUST NOT refuse, delay, or re-route a dispatch whose resolved
candidates are all outside its coverage; in particular no gate MAY refuse every
dispatch because some provider holds a record.

**Per-node selection.** For each node, the Dispatcher MUST choose the first candidate in configured order that has no covering live hold, has satisfied any outstanding post-expiry availability confirmation, has not been skipped by the admission-time credential-usability probe for this evaluation, and has not been skipped by the admission session-headroom filter for this evaluation. Such a candidate is *eligible*. Selection is made once per dispatch from one
consistent read of the availability evidence and is journaled per node with a
stable selection identity, the selected candidate index and identity, the
full-chain digest, the primary-generation fingerprint, and the holds that
skipped earlier candidates; that record contains no command, env value,
credential, prompt, raw error, or unredacted diagnostic. When headroom skips an earlier candidate, the selection record MUST identify that candidate, reference its headroom assessment, governing floor and governing horizon, and state whether the skip was a floor skip or a projection skip; it MUST NOT represent that skip as an observed hold.

The workflow MUST expose the ACP nodes that dominate every green terminal path.
Those are the success-critical nodes; for the reserved
workflow they are `dod_gate`, `implement`, `proof_capture`, `review`,
`proof_verify`, each of which dominates every green terminal path;
for a registered variant the success-critical set is the ACP nodes
dominating that variant's own green terminal paths. The admission-required set
is wider: every ACP node potentially reachable in the submitted graph is
admission-required, success-critical or not. Before submission, every ACP node
potentially reachable in the submitted graph MUST have an eligible candidate. A
node proven unreachable in that graph imposes no candidate requirement. If any
potentially reachable node has no eligible candidate, the item MUST remain
ready without a claim or blocked reason, and the Dispatcher MUST schedule
another admission evaluation. It MUST NOT render or start a candidate covered
by a live hold, including for conditional repair or adjudication nodes. The
same predicate governs rework admission, where the parked item stays parked
without a claim. The scheduled evaluation falls at the earliest expiry among
the holds that empty a chain, and otherwise after
`dispatcher.credential_reprobe_interval_seconds`; no human valve is the remedy
for that wait. An unsupported or ambiguous workflow graph MUST refuse
fallback-enabled dispatch instead of guessing. Idle-factory and wait attention
consume this identical verdict.

The admission-time credential probe creates no observed record. For a fallback-
enabled chain, a provider-limit/rate-limit probe refusal is an ephemeral
candidate-local skip for that one admission evaluation; the Dispatcher
continues in order and MUST NOT hold the loop while every admission-required
chain is viable. If all candidates are locally unusable, admission may refuse
for the empty chain but no durable hold is minted. The re-probe wait applies to
a legacy single candidate and a genuinely exhausted fallback chain, never a
primary-only probe refusal with a viable fallback. This admission-time probe is
distinct from the availability confirmation turn below and confirms nothing
about availability.

Bounded expiry, later matching execution, and operator clearance are the only
hold-retirement routes; a successful availability confirmation satisfies an
expired observation's outstanding confirmation and does not shorten a live one.
A node attempt that starts after a domain observation
and succeeds against the same hold key retires only that older domain record; a
later success by the exact candidate identity retires only its older candidate
record. A re-dispatched run that succeeds on a fallback candidate MUST NOT clear
the held primary, even when the whole run succeeds. An exact scope/key clearance
valve MUST be attributed, reason-required, append-only, and refuse a
nonexistent live target; the legacy provider valve addresses legacy records
only. Operator clearance MUST make the affected wait eligible for immediate
reevaluation.

**Provider-limit release and re-dispatch.** When a run terminates — through
any terminal, the workflow's `needs_human` terminal included — and the failing
node's recorded failure classifies under this section's signatures as an
eligible cause, the Dispatcher MUST, in this order and without a human:
(1) record the hold that failure observed, scoped and keyed as the matching
signature declares; (2) journal one `provider-limit-release` record naming the
work-item, run id, factory, failing node attempt, matched cause, scope and hold
key, the candidate identity that failed, and the preserved-work reference the
release observed (the published head or preservation ref) or its confirmed
absence; the recovery route itself is decided by recovery routing at the item's
next dispatch;
(3) release the item's dispatch claim and return it to `ready`, NOT to
`blocked` and with no `blocked_reason`; and (4) leave the item to the ordinary
admission valve, which re-dispatches it with every node selected afresh as
"Per-node selection" specifies. When every admission-required node still has an
eligible candidate the re-dispatch is admitted on the next pass; otherwise the
item waits as the admission paragraph above specifies. A provider-limit release
MUST NOT consume any budget of §"The three rework caps", MUST NOT count as an
item-attributable terminal under §"Across-dispatch required-result progress",
and MUST NOT be surfaced as a needs-human decision. Only a failure the
Dispatcher cannot classify as eligible keeps its existing route, including the
`blocked / needs-human` rest of §"A factory run never awaits a human".

`provider-limit-release` covers the eligible availability causes defined by the
signature grammar, including candidate-scoped model removal. The typed
provider-usage-limit flag of §"Provider-limit permanence and root-cause
surfacing" remains specific to usage or spend ceilings and MUST NOT be set
merely because another eligible availability cause triggers release. A typed
provider-limit failure from an identity-less legacy adapter MUST record the
existing legacy provider observation and release the item to ready without
inventing a candidate identity. Its conservative legacy coverage remains
unchanged.

Each release operation of this section -- a provider-limit release, or an adapter launch
release below -- MUST be idempotent and replayable by reconciliation,
keyed by resolved factory, run, and failing node attempt. Reconciliation MUST
complete any interrupted hold, release, cost-observation, and ledger-transition
writes without refreshing the original hold expiry, duplicating cost, or
releasing a newer dispatch claim. The failure selected for release MUST be the
unrecovered failure responsible for the run's terminal disposition. An earlier
failed attempt that later succeeded MUST NOT release a successful run or
override a subsequent unrelated failure. Unreadable failure evidence MUST be
surfaced as unavailable and retried automatically; it MUST NOT be treated as a
measured non-match or converted into a needs-human decision.

**Adapter launch release and re-dispatch.** An *adapter launch failure* is a failing ACP node attempt whose recorded failure states that the ACP adapter process exited before the ACP protocol completed, for which complete factory-native evidence for that exact node visit, engine attempt, and executed candidate establishes that the prompt boundary was not crossed, and whose recorded termination is an ordinary process exit rather than a signal termination. The Dispatcher MUST first apply the existing non-eligible guards and availability-signature classification to the same attempt's recorded evidence. An eligible availability failure MUST take Provider-limit release and re-dispatch and MUST NOT be classified as an adapter launch failure. An adapter launch failure MUST carry no provider evidence in the recorded protocol machine code, protocol message, or separately captured process terminal diagnostic. Authentication, command-not-found, cancellation, node deadline or stall expiry, generic HTTP 400/404, remote-compaction 404, malformed command/configuration, signal exit, unattributed sandbox/DNS/transport failure, code/test/review/tool failure, and non-convergence retain their existing routes and MUST NOT be reclassified as adapter launch failures. The generic ACP process-exit failure identity alone is not provider evidence, and an adapter launch failure itself is not provider evidence: it mints no hold, retires none, sets no provider-usage-limit flag, and attributes nothing to a provider or account.

Adapter launch evidence MUST be read from the factory recorded for the run and scoped to the unrecovered attempt responsible for its terminal disposition. The prompt boundary is conservatively considered crossed when that attempt has an `agent.acp.started` event; this event precedes prompt submission, so its presence excludes launch release even when no later activity was observed. Absence of that event establishes the boundary was not crossed only when the engine's event-emission and durability guarantees cover that execution path and the attempt's event stream is verified complete through termination. Any recorded agent activity also excludes launch release. Neither zero inference, an empty tool ledger, the generic process-exit message, nor an internal activity-derived `turn_started` value alone establishes eligibility. Missing, incomplete, unreadable, or unscopable evidence is unavailable, not negative evidence: the Dispatcher MUST surface it and retry observation automatically without releasing the item or manufacturing a needs-human decision.

When a run terminates -- through any terminal, the workflow's `needs_human` terminal included -- and its unrecovered failing node attempt is an adapter launch failure, and the item's preceding dispatch did not itself end in an adapter launch failure, the Dispatcher MUST, in this order and without a human: (1) journal one `adapter-launch-release` record naming the work-item, run id, factory, failing node attempt, executed candidate identity, the recorded exit code or its explicit absence, the preceding dispatch's run id or the explicit statement that the item has none, and the preserved-work reference the release observed (the published head or preservation ref) or its confirmed absence; the recovery route itself is decided by recovery routing at the item's next dispatch; (2) write one ledger comment on the item naming the run id, factory, failing node and the recorded exit code or its explicit absence; (3) release the item's dispatch claim and return it to `ready`, NOT to `blocked` and with no `blocked_reason`; and (4) leave the item to the ordinary admission valve, which re-dispatches it with every node selected afresh as "Per-node selection" specifies. The *preceding dispatch* is the immediately preceding submitted run for the same item in durable dispatch order, relative to the run being classified, across every factory: a refused admission is not a dispatch, a node retry is not a new dispatch, and an item's first dispatch has none. The predecessor identity is persisted with the release decision and reused by any replay; unavailable predecessor history is unavailable evidence, never proof of no predecessor. The bound is therefore one release per consecutive sequence of adapter launch failures: any intervening dispatch that did not end in an adapter launch failure resets it. An adapter launch release MUST NOT consume any budget of §"The three rework caps", MUST neither increment nor reset the item count of §"Across-dispatch required-result progress", and MUST NOT be surfaced as a needs-human decision. When the item's preceding dispatch also ended in an adapter launch failure, the current failure keeps its existing route, including the `blocked / needs-human` rest of §"A factory run never awaits a human"; that terminal is not item-attributable and neither increments nor resets the across-dispatch item count, and its needs-human cause record MUST name both runs and state that a repeated adapter launch failure is not released automatically. The release MUST be idempotent per run under the release operation above: completing or replaying it after a newer dispatch has claimed the item MUST NOT release that newer claim, journal a second record, or write a second ledger comment.

**Recovery from the failed run's preserved work.** An item is *released for
recovery* when its latest journaled dispatch ended in a first-stall release
(§"Dispatcher progress watchdog"), a `provider-limit-release` record, an
`adapter-launch-release` record, or a `stale-assignee-clear` record for that
dispatch's run; an item is also released for recovery while it is a stale
assignee whose run stamp names a run (§"Stranded claim release" → "Stale
assignee clearance"). An item is also released for recovery when its latest journaled dispatch ended at the workflow's `needs_human` terminal or at a `non_converged` terminal, the item has since returned to `ready` by any path (a human valve, a groom, or a return from `backlog`), and no newer dispatch has been submitted for it. An item whose latest journaled dispatch ended at the `non_converged` terminal because the run's recapture bound was reached — the third recapture verdict in one run, which §"Self-contained plugin dispatch" → "Definition-of-Done and Proof-of-Done stages" routes to `non_converged`, recognised by the cause line that terminal records carrying the marker `LIVESPEC_RECAPTURE_EXHAUSTED` — is released for recovery by the preceding sentence. Recovery routing MUST route such an item `held`. It MUST NOT route it `fresh`, and it MUST NOT route it `resume` or `seeded` automatically, even when every resume precondition passes. A proof that exhausted its recapture bound is not re-captured until a person or an owning seat supplies a proof rider and resumes the item explicitly through §"Resume from a published pull request (`resume --item`)". The `recovery-held` record of such an item MUST name the refusal `recapture-exhausted`, and its detail MUST read `recapture-exhausted: implementation preserved on <preserved> ; resume --item <work-item-id> at proof_capture with a proof rider`. `<preserved>` names pull request `#<number>` at head `<sha>` when the item's pull request is open; otherwise it names the needs-human ref and commit preserved at that run's ending; otherwise it reads `no preserved work observed`. This hold is a non-fallback refusal: no fallback-permitting refusal can turn it into a `seeded` or `fresh` route. It is graded after the pre-claim refusal of §"Across-dispatch required-result progress", exactly as every released candidate is, and like every release here it consumes no budget of §"The three rework caps". An explicit `resume --item` of such an item is governed by that command's own preconditions, including its two-resume chain bound, and this hold MUST NOT add a precondition to that command. Scenarios 342 and 343 in `scenarios.md` exercise this hold. An item is also released for recovery when its latest journaled dispatch ended by any route other than a merge of its pull request, the item carries a `livespec-preserved-tree` ledger comment under §"Dispatcher admission, WIP cap, and post-merge acceptance" → "A run's ending names its latest preserved capture on the item" that names that dispatch's run and either names a work-in-progress ref of that run or states that the run's preservation could not be determined, the item is at `ready` by any path (the Dispatcher's own return after a cancel, a human valve, a groom, or a return from `backlog`), and no newer dispatch has been submitted for it. *Any route* includes a factory restart cancel of a run that was not janitor-green, a cancel made outside the Dispatcher, and a whole-run wall-budget cancel once a person has returned the item to `ready`. This release MUST NOT move an item out of `blocked`: an item that the wall budget rests for a person is released only after that person returns it to `ready`. Deciding this release MUST read the ledger comment only, so it takes no remote measurement. Every sentence that follows in this paragraph, from "For such an item" through "... the needs-human or non-convergence cause recorded on the item.", MUST apply to an item this release covers exactly as it applies to an item the preceding sentence releases: the pre-claim refusal is graded first, the release consumes no budget of §"The three rework caps", routing measures the preserved work on origin before it seeds, a measurement that cannot be taken is the `held` outcome and never `fresh`, and a needs-human ref or preservation ref published at the same run's ending is preferred over the run's latest preserved capture. The goal brief of a `seeded` dispatch of such an item SHOULD name the ending it recovers from. For such an item, the pre-claim refusal of §"Across-dispatch required-result progress" MUST be graded BEFORE recovery routing: an item that refusal refuses MUST NOT be routed, MUST NOT be offered to the admission valve in that pass, and keeps that section's refusal and remedy. This ordering is what bounds the release, because the release consumes no budget of §"The three rework caps". An item the refusal does not refuse MUST be graded by recovery routing exactly as every other released candidate is: `resume` at the anchored node when every precondition of §"Resume from a published pull request (`resume --item`)" passes, `seeded` from its preserved work when every applicable resume refusal is fallback-permitting and preserved work is verified, `fresh` only when preserved work is confirmed absent or a current fresh ruling governs the item, and `held` when a non-fallback refusal applies or a measurement routing needs cannot be taken. Its preserved work MUST be taken in the preference order this clause states below, so the pushed ref a needs-human ending preserves under §"A factory run never awaits a human", and the preservation ref of a failed engine checkpoint, are preferred over the observed published head. That preference is bounded by run age. A needs-human ref, or a failed-checkpoint preservation ref (a `refs/livespec/preserved-publish/` ref that a `livespec-preserved-tree` ledger comment names), outranks the observed published head only when the run it belongs to is the run that published that head or a later run of the item, and it MUST NOT be preferred over a head published by a later run. Runs are ordered by the order in which the item's dispatches were journaled. A needs-human ref belongs to the run its ref name names, or to the run it carries under the paragraph "A needs-human tree is recognised by the run it carries" below. A failed-checkpoint preservation ref belongs to the run its `livespec-preserved-tree` ledger comment names. The observed published head belongs to the run whose publication record or journal record names that head. A preserved-publish ref written by §"Stale publish-branch reclaim before a re-dispatch" stands for the published head it preserves and is ranked as that head, not as a competing ref. A needs-human ref or failed-checkpoint preservation ref whose tip commit's tree is identical to the observed published head's tree holds no work that head lacks, so it is likewise not a competing ref: routing MUST NOT require its run, or the head's run, to be established on its account, and MUST route the item as it would if that ref were absent. The tree comparison MUST be read from the same per-pass identification that supplies the tip trees for "A needs-human tree is recognised by the run it carries"; a comparison that cannot be taken is the existing unobservable-measurement hold, and MUST NOT be read as identity. When the item holds both an observed published head and a needs-human ref or failed-checkpoint preservation ref, and the run of the head or of that ref cannot be established, routing MUST route the item `held`, and the `recovery-held` record MUST name the measurement `publishing-run-unobservable`. An item holding no such competing ref is routed as this clause otherwise states, whether or not its head's run can be established. Scenario 323 in `scenarios.md` exercises this run-age bound.
