    and the always-run pre-push `dispatcher.py ledger-normalize --gate`
    mode.
- `title` — beads `title`. Identity.
- `description` — beads `description`. Identity. Its first heading is the
  Definition of Done section (§"Effective acceptance criteria"), and the
  host-written `## Proof of Done` section (§"Proof of Done record")
  follows it.
- `rank` — beads `metadata.rank` (a structured value carried in the
  metadata JSON column, like `audit`). `rank` is the **sole ordering
  authority** — a strictly-required, non-null fractional/lexicographic
  `str`. Rank sorts ASCENDING: the lexicographically earliest key is
  the most urgent, and "top-ranked" throughout this spec means exactly
  that earliest key. A legacy beads issue whose `metadata` lacks `rank`
  reads back through the shared bottom-sentinel
  (`livespec_runtime.work_items.rank.BOTTOM_SENTINEL`) the store adapter
  substitutes, so it sorts strictly after every real key WITHOUT making
  the domain type nullable.
- `priority` — **REMOVED as a logical field** (`rank` is the sole order;
  two order sources would be two conflicting truths). A legacy beads
  issue keeps its native `priority` column harmlessly; the materialized
  work-item no longer reads it. The one-time L2 backfill seeds `rank`
  from the legacy `priority → captured_at → id` order.
- `assignee` — beads `assignee` (first-class field). Identity when
  present; absent when null. Reused in place as the claimed-by/owner
  field (beads has no native `owner`); the Dispatcher sets it on `admit`.
  **REQUIRED once `status == active`** (the `active ⟹ assignee`
  invariant).
- `admission_policy` — beads label `admission:<auto|manual>`;
  `acceptance_policy` — beads label `acceptance:<ai-only|human-only|ai-then-human>`;
  `rework_pending` — beads label `rework:pending` (a boolean logical field
  carried on the materialized work-item: present ⟺ the label is present;
  stamped and cleared only per §"Rework-pending re-dispatch", so the
  selection, accounting, and discrimination clauses there read a
  first-class field rather than a raw label);
  `blocked_reason` — beads label `blocked-reason:<needs-human|infra-external>`
  (the STORED reasons only; the third reason `dependency` is DERIVED and
  NEVER stored — it surfaces only as a rendered lane reason). An absent
  policy/reason label reads back `None` (inherit / the system safe
  default — the blessed optional-on-read pattern).
- `factory_safety` — beads label
  `factory-safety:<needs-host-secrets|mutates-host-machinery|needs-privileged-host|needs-host-only-input>`.
  An absent label reads back `None`, meaning FACTORY-SAFE — the fleet is
  factory-safe BY DEFAULT and only an explicit reason opts out. The four
  reasons name work that genuinely cannot run in a sandbox executing
  agent-written code: `needs-host-secrets` (verification requires real
  secrets that must never enter such a sandbox), `mutates-host-machinery`
  (changes the live host substrate the factory itself runs on — systemd
  timers, credential wrappers, the plugin cache, and Fabro servers — or
  changes external merge-gate machinery under `.github/workflows/`), and
  `needs-privileged-host` (privileged provisioning — a Dolt server, a
  1Password environment, a per-tenant Fabro server), and
  `needs-host-only-input` (the item's authoritative input — a file, verdict
  or state it must read — exists only on the host and cannot be committed to
  the repository or fetched into the sandbox; an input that CAN be committed
  is not this reason, and committing it is the remedy; an input that is
  itself a secret is `needs-host-secrets`, which takes precedence). The
  sharp line for the first three: writing CODE for any of these (including
  the Dispatcher's own code) is factory-safe; APPLYING host or external
  factory-gate state is host-only.
  Editing `.github/workflows/` remains host-routed even while ordinary CI
  runs on GitHub-hosted capacity, because those files are the factory's own
  executable merge gates and an agent must not rewrite its own examiner.
- `awaits_scope_override` — boolean read from the presence of the beads label
  `awaits-scope-override`. It is `true` only after a dispatch attempt is
  refused by the declared-workflow-edit arm while `factory_safety` is null,
  meaning `set-workflow-scope-override:<id>:citation-only` is the applicable
  remedy. It is distinct from `factory_safety`: a non-null `factory_safety`
  item is never awaiting this override because predicate ordering guarantees
  the override cannot admit it. The Dispatcher MUST set the label on that
  specific refusal and MUST clear it when the override is applied or when the
  item's current text no longer triggers the declared-workflow-edit arm, so
  consumers may treat the signal as current state rather than history.
- `origin` (`gap-tied` / `freeform`) — beads label `origin:<value>`.
- `gap_id` — beads label `gap-id:<id>`. Present iff `origin == gap-tied`;
  REQUIRED non-empty when present, absent when `origin == freeform`. The
  gap-id ↔ label exactly-once invariant is honored as exactly one
  `gap-id:` label per gap-tied issue.
- `status`/`assignee`/etc. unchanged on read — materialization parses
  the `bd` JSON (`status` mapped back through the `done`↔`closed`
  adapter; `rank` read from `metadata.rank` with the bottom-sentinel
  fallback).
- `depends_on` — beads `blocks` dependency edges. For each blocker, a
  `bd dep add <this-issue> <blocker> --type blocks` edge exists; the
  reader populates `depends_on` from these edges.
- `superseded_by` — beads `supersedes` dependency edge (`bd dep add
  <superseding> <this> --type supersedes`) when both items live in one tenant; when the superseding item lives in another tenant, which no dependency edge can reach, the item's `metadata.superseded_by` key holding the superseding item's id. Present iff non-null.
- epic linkage — beads native `parent-child` (`bd create … --parent
  <epic>` / `bd update <child> --parent <epic>`), or a `tracks` dependency
  edge from the record to the epic. An epic is a `type: epic` issue whose
  members are its beads children. Every surface that reports a record's
  parent or enumerates an epic's children, including the plan
  child-enumeration union, the `context` envelope's children, the
  `list-work-items --json` projection's `parent`, the plan-progress
  attribution of §"Attention without confusing activity with results" and
  the epic-close check of the merge-evidence exemption, MUST
  honour both edge types, so that no two surfaces disagree on what an epic
  linkage is. Scenario 215 in `scenarios.md` exercises this bullet.
- `captured_at` — beads `created_at`. On live create the value is read
  back from the server; on import the supplied timestamp is preserved.
- `resolution` (typed enum) — beads label `resolution:<enum>`, one of:
  `completed`, `wontfix`, `duplicate`, `spec-revised`,
  `no-longer-applicable`, `resolved-out-of-band`. REQUIRED present when
  the logical `status == done` (stored as beads `closed`).
- `reason` — beads `close_reason` (set via `bd close --reason`).
  REQUIRED non-empty for closure records.
- `spec_commitment_hint` — beads native `spec_id` field. When non-null,
  carries the verbatim `id_hint` from a spec-side
  `spec_commitments.impl_followups[]` declaration (per
  `livespec/SPECIFICATION/contracts.md`). Absent for freeform items with
  no spec-side commitment.
- `audit` (the whole `AuditRecord`) — serialized losslessly into the
  beads issue's `metadata` JSON column. Present when `resolution` is one
  of `{completed, spec-revised, resolved-out-of-band}` (the resolutions
  that imply git activity landed on the canonical branch); absent
  otherwise. `AuditRecord` schema:
  - `verification_timestamp` (string, required). UTC ISO-8601 seconds of
    audit-record creation.
  - `commits` (array of strings, required, MAY be empty). SHAs of
    commits comprising the work. After squash-merge these SHAs may no
    longer exist locally; tooling MUST tolerate that case.
  - `files_changed` (array of strings, required, MAY be empty).
    Repo-root-relative paths touched by the work.
  - **`merge_sha`** (string, required, non-empty). SHA of the merge
    commit on the canonical branch that introduced this work. Tooling
    MUST verify it is reachable from `origin/<canonical_branch>` via
    `git merge-base --is-ancestor`.
  - **`pr_number`** (integer or null, optional). GitHub PR number for
    traceability; null when the merge did not originate from a PR.

  The audit MUST be present when `resolution` is one of `{completed,
  spec-revised, resolved-out-of-band}` — all three carry an implied
  canonical-branch merge that the audit attests. Resolutions in
  `{wontfix, duplicate, no-longer-applicable}` MUST carry no
  `AuditRecord` in `metadata`.

### Materialized view and close-in-place

Each work-item is exactly ONE beads issue row; there is no
latest-record-wins reduction (that is the plaintext sibling's concern).
A closure mutates the row IN PLACE: `bd close --reason` sets the
terminal status and `close_reason`, `bd update` sets the
`resolution:<enum>` label, and the `AuditRecord` (when required) is
written into `metadata`. A `done` (beads-native `closed`) issue is
terminal —
re-opening (`bd update --status open`) is ALLOWED but DISCOURAGED (the
right pattern is to file a new work-item with a fresh `id` that
references the closed one via `superseded_by` or `depends_on`). The
tenant DB's own version history is the immutable backing log behind the
in-place mutation; doctor's `no-orphan-blocker` invariant in `livespec`
reads materialized views, and readers of this plugin MUST do the same.

### `work_item_merge_evidence` static check

The check walks every materialized work-item from the configured store
descriptor (reading the `AuditRecord` from each closed issue's
`metadata` column) and applies the following rules. The check reads at
the SUBSTRATE layer: the beads-native rows, where the logical `done`
state appears as beads `closed`.

For each work-item with `status == "closed"`:

- If `resolution` is in `{completed, spec-revised, resolved-out-of-band}`:
  - REQUIRE an `AuditRecord` is present in `metadata`.
  - REQUIRE `audit.merge_sha` is non-empty.
  - REQUIRE `git cat-file -e <merge_sha>` exits 0 (the SHA exists in the
    local repo).
  - REQUIRE
    `git merge-base --is-ancestor <merge_sha> origin/<canonical_branch>`
    exits 0.
- If `resolution` is in `{wontfix, duplicate, no-longer-applicable}`:
  - REQUIRE no `AuditRecord` is present (the negative-evidence case — a
    record that says "this was closed administratively" must not carry
    merge-evidence).
- If `resolution` is null AND `status == "closed"`:
  - FAIL with message "closed work-item without resolution is
    malformed."

Work-items with `type == "epic"` are EXEMPT from the merge-evidence
requirement. Epics close when their child work-items (beads
epic-linkage members, `parent-child` or `tracks`, per §"Work-item
beads-issue mapping") are all closed; the check INSTEAD requires that
every child resolves to a closed work-item.

All operations are local `git` invocations (`cat-file`, `merge-base`);
the check is network-free per the existing no-network-I/O constraint
(the `bd` reads it depends on go through the same local `bd` client, not
a separate network surface owned by the check).

The check is plugin-private to `livespec-orchestrator-beads-fabro` (it depends on the
beads-issue mapping this plugin defines — specifically the `AuditRecord`
in `metadata` and the `resolution:` label). The plaintext sibling ships
its own JSONL-shaped equivalent; the two are not interchangeable.

### Closed-item-integrity check

The `closed_item_integrity` check is the mechanical guard for the
closed-item-integrity invariant in `constraints.md` §"Closed-item
integrity" — it makes "closed but unproven is forbidden" un-bypassable
rather than a remember-to-verify review.

The `closed_item_integrity` check MUST enumerate every closed gap-tied work-item in the beads store, derive each item's `gap-id` from its `gap-id:<id>` label, resolve that gap-id to its acceptance heading — a heading-derived gap-id (the live `detect-impl-gaps` derivation) names its heading's own `heading-coverage` entry directly, and a historical clause-derived gap-id, which a closed item keeps per §"`detect-impl-gaps`" → "Migration of clause-derived gap ids", resolves via the `clauses[]` gap-id→scenario map in `tests/heading-coverage.json` — and emit a `closed-item-integrity` finding for any such item whose resolved scenario's `heading-coverage` entry is still bound to the `TODO` sentinel (not a real integration-tier-or-above test node id) OR which lacks the `resolution:completed` label.

The `closed_item_integrity` check MUST be always-wired into the `just check` aggregate and always-running; it MUST NOT be silently skipped. Its severity is governed by a self-documenting per-check lever — the `LIVESPEC_CLOSED_ITEM_INTEGRITY` environment variable — whose only recognized values are `warn` and `fail`. In `warn` mode (the DEFAULT) the check MUST surface each offender as a warning and exit `0`; in `fail` mode it MUST surface each offender as an error and exit non-zero. An unset or unrecognized lever value MUST default to `warn`. The lever is the SEVERITY switch, not a wiring carve-out: the check always enumerates every closed gap-tied item and always runs regardless of the lever value.

The check REUSES existing primitives and introduces NO new gap-id logic:
it reads each item's gap-id from its label, resolves a
historical clause-derived id through the shared `livespec_spec_clauses`
extractor (single-source clause-id, no duplication) and a heading-derived
id through the same derivation `detect-impl-gaps` uses, reads the `clauses[]`
map already defined by livespec core's `constraints.md`, and reads
closed gap-tied items through the existing beads
reader (`bd` store). This check is enforced by
`just check-closed-item-integrity`.

Preconditions (recorded so the future revise/impl loop sees them, NOT as
separate invariants): the check requires (a) the `clauses[]`
gap-id→scenario map to be populated in `tests/heading-coverage.json` for
each gap-tied behavior clause (linking its gap-id to its acceptance
scenario's H2 section name) — this is the core `clauses[]` contract
(`constraints.md`, `non-functional-requirements.md`) that impl-beads
adopts; and
(b) for historical clause-derived gap-ids only, the shared
`livespec_spec_clauses` extractor available to impl-beads' dev-tooling.
Both are existing primitives; the impl
work-item adopts the `clauses[]` map into impl-beads' heading-coverage
and wires the check — it does not build new gap-id machinery.

Implementation-approach note (recorded so the future impl loop sees it,
NOT a second invariant): the `resolution:completed` half of the
invariant is best upheld by a "pit of success" `close-work-item`
wrapper that atomically closes a work-item AND applies the
`resolution:completed` label in one operation — so the
`constraints.md` §"Closed-item integrity" two-step close recipe (`bd
close --reason …` then `bd update --add-label resolution:completed`) can
never be half-done (closed without the label). This wrapper is an impl
work-item to be built alongside the `closed_item_integrity` check, not a
separate spec invariant; the invariant states WHAT must hold, the check
DETECTS violations, and the wrapper makes the compliant path the path of
least resistance.

## Spec Reader internal API

Per `livespec/SPECIFICATION/contracts.md`, every `livespec-impl-*` plugin MUST expose
four capabilities through an internal adapter. The shape is
implementation-dependent; this plugin's shape is a Python module with
these public functions:

```python
def read_current_specification(spec_root: Path) -> SpecSnapshot: ...
def read_specification_history(spec_root: Path, version: int) -> SpecSnapshot: ...
def current_specification_version(spec_root: Path) -> int: ...
def diff_specification_versions(
    spec_root: Path, version_a: int, version_b: int,
) -> SpecDiff: ...
```

`SpecSnapshot` and `SpecDiff` are dataclasses defined under
`.claude-plugin/scripts/<adapter>/spec_reader.py`. The Spec Reader is
substrate-agnostic — it reads the spec tree, never the beads tenant DB —
so its implementation is shared near-verbatim with the plaintext
sibling. The initial implementation is a thin file pass-through (no
caching, no indexing); cached or section-indexed implementations remain
valid future refinements without contract change.

The Spec Reader MUST:

- Consult the active template manifest's `spec_files` list rather than
  hardcoding the well-known file set (per the upstream Spec Reader
  required-capability surface, capability 1).
- Surface the `version-directories-complete` pruned-marker exemption
  when reading history (capability 2).
- Return `int` for the current version (capability 3).
- Compute diffs as a structured change list (capability 4); the initial
  implementation returns a `SpecDiff` carrying per-file
  added/removed-line counts plus a unified-diff body.

The Spec Reader MUST exclude content from
`<spec-root>/proposed_changes/`. Only ratified canonical content is
exposed; pending proposals are not yet intent.

The Spec Reader is consumed by `detect-impl-gaps`, `capture-spec-drift`,
and `implement`. It is NOT a slash command and NOT
exposed through the `/livespec-orchestrator-beads-fabro:` namespace.

## Persistent Agent Knowledge realization

Per `livespec/SPECIFICATION/contracts.md` §"Persistent Agent
Knowledge realization", the per-plugin form is
implementation-dependent. `livespec-orchestrator-beads-fabro` realizes the store as:

- A directory `.ai/` at the consumer project's root containing one
  markdown file per topic (`.ai/<topic-slug>.md`).
- Each topic file is referenced from the consumer project's `CLAUDE.md`
  and/or `AGENTS.md` via a one-line bullet pointing at the file path.
  Reference inclusion is REQUIRED — orphaned topic files MUST NOT exist.
- A topic file is authored by writing the durable knowledge to the
  chosen topic file (creating it if absent) and updating
  `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` references if needed in one atomic step.
- Topic files MAY accumulate; pruning is the user's call (this store
  does NOT auto-trim). Persistent-knowledge content is durable-pending,
  never transient, so no productivity-heuristic hygiene invariant
  applies to it (per upstream §"Persistent Agent Knowledge realization"
  bullet 3).

The harness loads `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` automatically into agent
context per Claude Code / Codex / other harness conventions; the linked
`.ai/<topic>.md` files are loaded on-demand by the agent following
bullet references when relevant. This realization is the same slot the
plaintext sibling implements — it is substrate-independent (the
Persistent Agent Knowledge store is markdown files, never beads issues).

## `compat` block

Per `livespec/SPECIFICATION/contracts.md`, every consuming project's
`.livespec.jsonc` declares a `compat` block for each active
impl-plugin. For
`livespec-orchestrator-beads-fabro`:

```jsonc
{
  "implementation": { "plugin": "livespec-orchestrator-beads-fabro" },
  "livespec-orchestrator-beads-fabro": {
    "format": "beads",
    "compat": {
      "livespec": ">=0.1.0,<1.0.0",
      "pinned": "master"
    },
    "connection": {
      "tenant": "livespec-orch-beads-fabro",
      "prefix": "bd-ib",
      "database": "livespec-orch-beads-fabro",
      "server_user": "livespec-orch-beads-fabro",
      "server_host": "127.0.0.1",
      "server_port": 3307,
      "fake": false
    }
  }
}
```

`format: beads` is fixed for this plugin (the substrate marker — the
plaintext sibling declares `jsonl`). `livespec` is a semver range
matching every `livespec` release this plugin's pinned version is known
to be compatible with. `pinned` is the SPECIFIC `livespec` release tag
the consumer currently runs against (`master` during bootstrap, which
fires doctor's `contract-version-compatibility` `warn` as expected).
Both are REQUIRED per upstream.

`pinned` is ALSO the ref the post-merge janitor provisions its
livespec-core clone at (§"Dispatch preflight and post-merge step
discipline" → "Janitor-core provisioning resolution"): the Dispatcher
MUST NOT silently substitute a moving branch tip for a missing `pinned`,
though a repository's explicitly-declared `pinned: "master"` bootstrap
value is honored as declared. `core_repo` (OPTIONAL) declares the
repository URL the janitor clones livespec-core from; when absent the
fleet livespec-core repository is used, and a present-but-unusable
`core_repo` refuses rather than sliding onto that fleet default.

The `connection` block is plugin-specific configuration. Its keys:

- `tenant` / `database` / `server_user` — all equal (the load-bearing
  ≤32-char tenant identity; one Dolt name serves all three).
- `prefix` — the beads issue-ID create-prefix (bd's server-stored
  prefix). It is DECOUPLED from the tenant DB name: a short, readable
  alias that MAY differ from it (here it is `bd-ib`). Skills read it from
  this value rather than assume it equals the tenant.
- `server_user` — the least-privilege tenant user scoped to this DB.
- `server_host` / `server_port` — the TCP connection to the shared
  `dolt sql-server`.
- `socket` — the Unix socket path; OVERRIDES host/port when reachable.
  TCP is the default for sandboxed callers that lack `0750`
  socket-directory access.
- `fake` — selects the hermetic in-memory backend; `false` in the
  committed config (which describes the real connection). CI and tests
  set `LIVESPEC_BEADS_FAKE=1` to force the fake.

The tenant PASSWORD is deliberately ABSENT from this block. It is
supplied only via the `BEADS_DOLT_PASSWORD` environment variable at
`bd`-call time and is NEVER committed. The `LIVESPEC_BD_PATH`
environment variable (the managed public entry point to the pinned `bd`
binary, resolving to the lifecycle guard when installed) and
`LIVESPEC_BEADS_FAKE` likewise overlay this block at runtime and are not
committed config keys.

There is no `work_items_path` key — that is the plaintext sibling's
JSONL-file location; this plugin's substrate is the tenant DB resolved
from the `connection` block.

**`canonical_branch`** (optional string). The canonical branch name
against which merge-evidence checks (see §"`work_item_merge_evidence`
static check") verify reachability. Default: the value of
`git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` (typically `master`
or `main`). Hard-coded fallback when symbolic-ref resolution fails:
`"master"`. The key is project-level (one value per repo), not
per-work-item — static checks resolve it once per invocation and apply
it uniformly.

The configuration block is read by every skill at invocation time. A
missing or malformed block MUST fire a `fail` finding from doctor's
`contract-version-compatibility` invariant (upstream cross-boundary
doctor invariants).

## Cross-boundary handoffs

Per `livespec/SPECIFICATION/contracts.md` §"Cross-boundary handoffs",
this plugin participates in these red-edge handoffs:

1. `/livespec-orchestrator-beads-fabro:capture-spec-drift` →
   `/livespec:propose-change` (drift findings).

The handoff mechanism is namespace invocation (per
`livespec/SPECIFICATION/contracts.md`) —
never direct CLI shelling-out to wrapper paths.

## Worker credential projection

The Dispatcher MAY authenticate a worker sandbox's coding-agent runtime from a
**projected provider-subscription credential** (for example a Claude subscription
or an OpenAI/ChatGPT subscription) as an alternative to a provider API key, so
workers MAY spend subscription quota rather than metered API billing.

The orchestrator host MAY hold provider-subscription credentials for more than one
provider at the same time, and the Dispatcher MAY project more than one of them
into a single worker sandbox — so one worker MAY authenticate more than one
coding-agent runtime (for example a Claude-subscription primary agent alongside an
OpenAI/ChatGPT-subscription runtime). Each projected credential MUST independently
satisfy the non-rotatability and host-ownership guarantees below.

The non-rotatability and host-ownership guarantees are provider-agnostic: they hold
for a Claude-subscription and an OpenAI/ChatGPT-subscription credential alike. The
projection **mechanism**, by contrast, MAY be provider-specific — the shape of each
projected credential MAY differ per provider — and is implementation-owned (see the
final paragraph).

Each projected worker credential MUST be **non-rotatable by the worker**: a worker
MUST NOT be able to mint or rotate any shared long-lived refresh credential. No
worker — including one whose run triggers a credential refresh — MAY invalidate a
credential for the orchestrator host or for any peer worker.

The Dispatcher MUST NOT dispatch a worker unless every projected credential covered
by the **freshness gate** has a usable lifetime that exceeds the worker's maximum
run budget. When the freshness gate cannot be satisfied, the Dispatcher MUST refuse
the dispatch and MUST surface that the host credential requires renewal, rather
than projecting a credential that MAY expire mid-run.

The worker's maximum run budget is the smaller of two figures. The first is the execution allowance the Dispatcher derives from the resolved workflow graph. The second is the bounded credential-use window, which is the resolved `dispatcher.credential_queue_allowance_seconds` plus the whole-run wall ceiling resolved for the same dispatch (§"ACP node timeouts", "Whole-run wall ceiling key"). The worker's credential-use deadline MUST be the projection instant plus that same figure, and the in-sandbox guard MUST stop coding-agent execution at that deadline, so the host gate and the in-sandbox guard use one figure. The freshness gate MUST require that figure plus the documented margin. The bound on credential use is the guard deadline, not the progress watchdog. Neither the whole-run wall budget nor its ceiling is itself a hard bound: queue time is excluded from it, a held or unmeasured budget lets a run continue past it, and it is enforced only while the watchdog polls. A run first launched within the credential queue allowance is never stopped by the deadline before the whole-run wall budget's worth of running time has elapsed. At the run's first coding-agent launch, the in-sandbox start check MUST refuse the launch when the time remaining before the credential-use deadline is less than the resolved whole-run wall budget, naming the deadline, the remaining time and the budget. This is the queue-exceeded refusal. It is a different measurement from the start check's comparison of the credential's remaining life against the freshness requirement, and both MUST be made. A run that queued past the credential queue allowance is therefore refused before any coding-agent turn starts, and is never stopped by the guard in the middle of a turn on its queue's account. `dispatcher.credential_queue_allowance_seconds` is a committed-only positive integer of seconds, default **86400**. A non-positive or non-integer value MUST be rejected before any run exists, naming the key. Its resolution and journaling follow the whole-run wall budget key. The status and manual-renewal surfaces MUST report the same figure and name which of the two figures governed. For a dispatch in flight they MUST also report the queue time consumed against the credential queue allowance. Scenario 228 in `scenarios.md` exercises this paragraph.

**A run ended by its credential-use deadline.** When the in-sandbox guard stops a coding agent at the credential-use deadline in the middle of a node, or refuses an agent launch because the deadline has passed, the Dispatcher MUST end the run under the export-then-terminate precondition of §"A factory run never awaits a human". It exports the run's record and writes and reads back the preserve-by-reference pointer, which names the run's published pull request and publish branch head when they exist, before the run is ended. It MUST journal exactly one `credential-use-deadline-reached` record carrying the run id, the factory, the node, the projection instant, the credential-use deadline, the queue time consumed, the governing figure, the preserve-by-reference pointer, and the cause. The cause is `queue-exceeded` for the start check's queue-exceeded refusal, `launch-refused` for a later agent launch refused because the deadline has passed, and `killed-mid-node` for an agent stopped at the deadline. The same disposition applies to all three. It MUST rest the item at `blocked` with `blocked_reason` `needs-human`, with a ledger comment naming the run, the node, the deadline, the cause and the pointer. The record anchors resume under §"Resume from a published pull request (`resume --item`)" exactly as a `run-wall-budget-exceeded` record does. The same published-head, stage and proof-record-precedence restrictions apply. A deadline record without those prerequisites preserves the recovery reference but does not itself authorize `resume --item`. Such an ending MUST NOT be reported as a plain failed run, MUST NOT be left without a journal record, and MUST NOT count toward any non-convergence or rework bound. Scenario 228 in `scenarios.md` exercises this paragraph.

The orchestrator **host** MUST be the sole owner and refresher of each long-lived
provider refresh credential; worker sandboxes MUST be read-only consumers of the
projected snapshots.

The projection mechanism — the per-provider projection shape, which projected
credentials the freshness gate covers, the credential file or field layout, and
the encoding that renders the snapshot non-rotatable — is implementation-owned
and MUST NOT be fixed by this contract. The maximum run budget, credential-use
deadline and freshness requirement follow the rules above; the documented
margin remains implementation-owned. The behavior is exercised by Scenario 18,
Scenario 19 and Scenario 228 in `scenarios.md`.

## Proof credential projection

A governed repository MAY declare `dispatcher.proof_credentials` as a list of
objects `{ "name": <environment variable name>, "purpose": <one sentence>,
"capability": <value> }` — the credentials its proof stages
(§"Definition-of-Done and Proof-of-Done stages") need to exercise the
deliverable's backing services from inside the sandbox. The key is
committed-configuration-only and does not trigger the console Settings
lockstep. `capability` MUST be a value of the closed enumeration whose only
member today is `read_only`, meaning the credential can observe the named
service and cannot create, modify, delete, or spend; the enumeration MAY gain
values by ratification and MUST use self-describing names, never tiers. The
declaration MUST carry names only; a declaration whose `name` or `purpose`
contains a credential-shaped value MUST be refused before any run exists by
the same scan that refuses credential-shaped adapter configuration (§"ACP node
adapter configuration").

**Projection.** The Dispatcher MUST project a declared proof credential into
the sandbox only when the value is present in the Dispatcher's own environment
as supplied by the target's configured `credential_wrapper`, MUST project it
through the same channel that projects the dispatch credential set
(§"Self-contained plugin dispatch") rather than a second channel, and MUST
refuse the dispatch — before any run exists, naming the declaration — when a
declared name is one of the withheld dispatch credentials (the store
credential, the durable App private key, any long-lived personal access token,
or any host provider refresh credential), when the value is absent (naming the
target's `credential_wrapper`), or when the declaration's capability would let
the sandbox execute code on the host substrate or modify a gate that validates
the factory's own output. Where the provider offers a management interface that
can mint a scoped, expiring credential, the Dispatcher SHOULD mint one per run
and revoke it afterwards rather than copy the host's credential, and the
dispatch journal MUST record per declaration whether the projected credential
was minted or copied. Journals and records MUST carry names, never values.

**Scope.** A proof that requires a capability outside the enumeration — any
write, or any production-scoped credential — is not a proof credential: the
item MUST carry `factory_safety: needs-host-secrets` and be host-routed, where
its proof is still captured mechanically. The rendering transport of a
projected proof credential is implementation-owned: an inline value in the
uncommitted run-configuration overlay on an engine with no secret reference
syntax, or a by-name vault reference on an engine that resolves one in the
worker; a change of transport MUST NOT change the declaration. Every rule of
`constraints.md` §"Factory sandbox credential constraints" applies to a proof
credential. The behaviour is exercised by Scenario 134 in `scenarios.md`.


## Bounded session waits and observable inventory

The plugin MUST expose a host-session CLI with `wait`, `inventory`, `ack`,
`retire` and `check` operations for detached gates and qualified Herdr panes. It MUST NOT
introduce another planning skill or an independent daemon.

### First-event waits and operational inventory

The wait subcommand MUST require a positive finite explicit deadline budget, bind immutable repository/session/target identities at arm time, and return on the first observed target outside its still-running predicate or on deadline expiry. Detached gate RUNNING and herdr working are the only still-running states. Other states MUST end the wait with the actual verdict or a distinct gone/unavailable/unknown outcome; diagnostic uncertainty MUST NOT become success. Gate identity includes the primary gate-store root and run id; pane identity includes backend, server/socket instance and process generation, and pane id. Retargeting via a rewritten pointer or reused identity MUST be refused. Cancelling a waiter MUST leave the target untouched.

All observations, subprocesses, transport operations and final return MUST share one monotonic deadline, including cancellation of a hung probe at expiry. Observation cadence MUST be no slower than one second while budget remains, and a slow target MUST NOT serialize observation of other targets. The result MUST identify the triggering target, each target's last observed state and freshness, and unfinished targets at expiry. Command outcome and a target's exit code MUST remain separate, both visible. A stale running observation MUST be labeled with its timestamp rather than asserted current.

Arming MUST atomically register a schema-versioned wait beneath the primary repository's ignored tmp/session-waits store before blocking. Records MUST hold session/wait identities, frozen targets, audit/deadline times, waiter process generation, observation sequence, return-ready state and acknowledgement. Concurrent writers MUST preserve each other's records. Inventory MUST re-observe targets and waiter generations, report ended-but-unacknowledged, running-without-waiter and overdue records, and expose corrupt, unsupported or unreadable records as unavailable. Unacknowledged records MUST survive session and waiter exit until explicit disposition; acknowledged retention and export queues MUST be bounded. The waiter's return-ready record proves only result production. An explicit ack by the receiving session MUST mark receipt acknowledgement only; execution consumption and target-result fulfillment MUST remain distinct under the shared obligation contract below. **A successor retires a terminal wait it does not own.** The `retire` operation MUST let a session other than the record's owning session dispose of a wait record, given the retiring session id and a non-empty reason. It MUST refuse, as `target-not-terminal` and without changing the record, while any target of the wait is in a still-running state. A retired record MUST keep its original session identity, frozen targets and observations unchanged, and MUST gain a retirement disposition carrying the retiring session id, the reason, the retirement time and the observed terminal state of every target. Retirement is a disposition, not a receipt acknowledgement: it MUST NOT mark the wait acknowledged by its owner, and MUST NOT establish execution consumption or target-result fulfillment. Inventory and the host turn-end check MUST NOT report a retired record as ended-but-unacknowledged. Retirement MUST publish a `session.wait.retired` event carrying the retiring and the original owning session ids, which joins the wait-family event catalog. Retired records count toward the bounded acknowledged retention. An exporter success or process exit MUST NOT establish any of those later states.

The check subcommand MUST expose those same mismatches before turn end. Existing host planning/drive guidance MUST use the shipped command rather than hand-written serial or single-status wait loops and MUST derive monitoring claims from inventory. Automatic stop integration MUST be claimed only for a runtime whose installed hook surface is exercised; where unavailable, guidance MUST explicitly invoke check and disclose that limit. Factory execution guidance MUST preserve the no-blocking-wait constraint.

The session producer MUST use OTLP/HTTP-JSON trace export to the configured host-local receiver and its /v1/traces surface, followed by host-owned enrichment and scrubbing before Honeycomb export. The receiver/exporter and its shared attribute allowlist are owned by this orchestrator; producers and consumers MUST co-evolve that allowlist and the vocabulary below. The host credential wrapper supplies the existing Honeycomb credential to the host exporter only; this contract MUST NOT introduce direct producer-to-Honeycomb credentials or a second collector. When this route is configured, arming, observation changes, return, acknowledgement and inventory snapshots MUST publish curated OTLP/HTTP-JSON trace events through the existing host-local enrichment/scrub and Honeycomb path. Resource service.name MUST be livespec-dispatcher and service.namespace MUST be livespec-family; scope MUST be livespec.orchestrator.session_wait with a version. The wait-family event catalog is session.wait.armed, session.wait.observed, session.wait.returned, session.wait.acknowledged, session.wait.retired and session.wait.inventory. Arming MUST enqueue its lifecycle observation before the waiter may terminate; remote delivery follows the bounded asynchronous failure rules below. Events MUST preserve allowlisted repository/session/wait identity, opaque target identity and kind, snapshot/observation identity and sequence, observed state, return reason, acknowledgement and waiter liveness. Existing work.item.id, dispatch.id and fabro.run_id MUST be populated only when known. Context MUST use an existing trace parent when present and otherwise a stable new wait trace.

Elapsed seconds, remaining budget, observation age, overdue seconds, target count, active/unacknowledged counts and export drop/rejection counts MUST be exported as typed numeric fields. An inventory invocation MUST publish its summary plus per-wait observations, including an explicit zero-count summary. Unchanged observation export MUST be rate-limited to at most once per minute; lifecycle changes MUST remain distinguishable immediately. Snapshot time and identity MUST keep repeated observations distinguishable from new waits. These trace measurements satisfy the initial metrics publication contract; a native OTLP metrics signal MAY be added only through a demonstrated ecosystem metrics route with bounded aggregate dimensions. Any unsupported publication MUST have a documented reason and equivalent trace representation where possible.

Only curated allowlisted fields MUST leave the host; raw commands, prompts, transcripts, environment values, secrets and credential-bearing paths/URLs MUST NOT be emitted. Producer, receiver allowlist and consumer MUST agree on the field vocabulary. Telemetry MUST use bounded asynchronous work and MUST NOT extend the wait deadline or suppress local results/alerts. Absent configuration MUST be visible as local-only; configured transport errors, partial rejection and queue overflow MUST be visible locally with bounded, non-recursive reporting. Honeycomb data MUST be labeled as timestamped observations, never as authoritative live control state.

The inventory contract MUST be consumable read-only by the existing overseer; daemon behavior is governed in that repository, and this repository owns the inventory interface and released integration proof. The sibling owns the daemon alert and its own specification; this repository MUST NOT add a second daemon or copy its supervision internals. The released cross-repository integration proof MUST observe the sibling consumer surfacing a completed unacknowledged wait for a monitored parked session within 60 seconds, including a live but ineffective waiter, with the alert remaining locally effective during telemetry outage. Untracked-session coverage MUST be disclosed. Released integration proof MUST exercise this sibling behavior before claiming the corresponding plan outcome.


### Dispatch trace correlation

This subsection extends the shared attribute vocabulary above to the Dispatcher's own launches. The vocabulary's `dispatch.id` field is carried on spans and run labels as `livespec.dispatch.id`, beside `work.item.id` and `livespec.dispatch.factory`; together these three are the correlation triple, and the receiver allowlist MUST admit all three.

Every `fabro run` the Dispatcher launches MUST pass the correlation triple as run labels: `--label work.item.id=<work-item id>`, `--label livespec.dispatch.id=<dispatch id>` and `--label livespec.dispatch.factory=<factory name>`, each carrying that dispatch's own value. A correlation value is identifier-shaped when, after surrounding whitespace is removed, it is 1 to 128 bytes long and every byte is an ASCII letter, an ASCII digit, `.`, `_`, `:` or `-`, so hyphenated work-item ids such as `bd-ib-5jvgfr` and factory names such as `hp-candidate` are identifier-shaped. A value that is not identifier-shaped MUST be left out of the argv, and leaving it out MUST NOT fail the dispatch.

The Dispatcher MUST emit one dispatch span per dispatch through its existing OTLP export path, carrying the correlation triple as span attributes. The span's trace id and span id MUST be derived from the dispatch id alone. Re-deriving the ids for the same dispatch id MUST yield the same trace id and span id. The derivation MUST use domain-separated SHA-256 outputs truncated to the required widths, with a deterministic non-zero fallback. Collisions in the resulting truncated identifiers are permitted. Emitting and exporting the dispatch span follows this section's bounded asynchronous telemetry and scrubbing rules, and an export failure MUST NOT fail the dispatch. The Dispatcher MUST set `TRACEPARENT` in the `fabro run` environment to `00-<trace id>-<span id>-01`, where the trace id is 32 and the span id 16 lowercase hexadecimal digits and neither is all zeros, using that dispatch span's ids, so that a factory which honours the run labels and the caller's trace parent places its run spans under the dispatch span. A factory that ignores either MUST NOT cause the dispatch to fail.

When a dispatch reaches a terminal state, the Dispatcher MUST emit exactly one terminal span named `livespec.dispatch.terminal` to service `livespec-dispatcher`. Its parent MUST be the dispatch span, and it MUST carry the correlation triple. It MUST carry `livespec.dispatch.outcome`, exactly one of:

- `succeeded`: the dispatch's work merged or was accepted;
- `failed`: the run ended in a terminal failure;
- `cancelled`: the run was cancelled;
- `rework`: acceptance returned the item for rework;
- `abandoned`: the dispatch ended without a terminal run outcome, for example a run that never started or was reaped as an orphan.

The outcome is the dispatch's final disposition: a dispatch whose run failed and whose item acceptance then returned for rework carries `rework`, and `failed` means the run failed with no acceptance verdict following it.

The terminal span MUST also carry `livespec.dispatch.attempt_count`. An attempt, in this paragraph, is one run of the dispatch's implementing turn on one candidate of its ACP fallback chain; it is not a rework attempt. For each attempt the dispatch made, the Dispatcher MUST emit one child span of the terminal span, named `livespec.dispatch.attempt`. Its start and end times MUST be the attempt's start and end. It MUST carry `livespec.dispatch.id`, `livespec.dispatch.attempt.index` (0-based), `acp.model` naming the model the attempt ran on, and `livespec.dispatch.attempt.fallback`, which is true exactly when the attempt ran on a candidate after the first in its fallback chain. A value the Dispatcher cannot observe MUST be omitted, never fabricated, and named in `livespec.dispatch.unavailable_fields` on the span that omits it. The receiver allowlist MUST admit every attribute this paragraph names. Emitting these spans follows this section's bounded asynchronous telemetry rules: an export failure MUST NOT fail, delay or alter the dispatch's recorded outcome.

**Terminal-span cost attributes.** The terminal span MUST also carry these four attributes, which the radar admission function of livespec-dev-tooling reads to place work by measured cost:

- `livespec.dispatch.run_class`, the name of the Fabro workflow the dispatch ran, such as `implement-work-item`;
- `livespec.dispatch.execution_target`, the host name of the machine whose capacity the run's sandbox consumed. For a Kubernetes pod sandbox this MUST be the host that the pod's `k8s.node.name` runs on;
- `livespec.sandbox.cpu_seconds`, the total CPU time the run's sandbox consumed over the dispatch, in seconds, as a non-negative number read from the sandbox's control group;
- `livespec.sandbox.memory_peak_bytes`, the peak memory of the run's sandbox over the dispatch, in bytes, as a non-negative integer read from the sandbox's control group.

These four follow the same omit-and-name rule as every other value of the terminal span: a value the Dispatcher cannot observe MUST be omitted, never fabricated or written as zero, and named in `livespec.dispatch.unavailable_fields`. The receiver allowlist MUST admit all four.

**Attributes a downstream scheduler requires.** livespec-dev-tooling publishes, in its package, one generated file `required_columns.json` naming every attribute and column its scheduler query specs read, each with the dataset it is read from. This repository MUST declare every span attribute key its emitters write in one committed emitted-attribute vocabulary module, and every emitter MUST take its keys from that module. A member of `just check` MUST read `required_columns.json` from the livespec-dev-tooling package this repository pins, and MUST fail, naming the attribute and its dataset, when an attribute the file requires from a dataset this repository's emitters write to (`livespec-dispatcher`, and the datasets the factory's step and turn spans reach) is absent from the emitted-attribute vocabulary or absent from `_otel_scrub.ATTRIBUTE_ALLOWLIST`. The check MUST read the required set only from that file and MUST NOT keep a second copy of it. It MUST perform no network I/O. A change to the required set MUST reach this check only through a bump of the livespec-dev-tooling pin.

### Host model-judgement caller labelling

This subsection extends the shared attribute vocabulary above to the model-judgement subprocesses the plugin launches on the host. A host model-judgement spawn is any subprocess the plugin starts on the host to obtain a model judgement, whichever agent runtime or model the resolved judge chain selects; a module that only wraps a caller-supplied model runner, or only reads verdict types, launches nothing and is not a spawn site.

Every host model-judgement spawn MUST carry a `livespec.caller=<caller>` entry in the `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` of the child's environment, naming the judgement that launched it. The caller value MUST be supplied by the launching judgement through the launch seam, and MUST NOT be inferred from the prompt, the model or the call stack, so that two judgements sharing one prompt and one launch seam are still told apart. The caller values are:

- `drift_run` for the drift run's spec-stated judgement;
- `dod_governing_heading` for the host governing-heading verdict, although it reaches the judge through the same launch seam as the drift run;
- `dod_judgement_pre_admission` and `dod_judgement_pre_dispatch` for the Definition-of-Done judgement taken before admission and before dispatch respectively;
- `ledger_intent_scan` for the ledger-intent scan's operator-supplied judge command.

A new spawn site MUST add its own caller value to this list in the same change that introduces it. Every caller value MUST be identifier-shaped as defined in §"Dispatch trace correlation".

When the launching environment already carries `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, the child MUST receive every existing entry unchanged, in its original order, with the `livespec.caller` entry appended as a further comma-separated entry. When it carries none, the child's `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` MUST consist of the `livespec.caller` entry alone. Labelling MUST NOT add, remove or rewrite any other environment variable of the child, and a failure to compose the label MUST NOT fail or alter the judgement.

The receiver allowlist MUST admit `livespec.caller` as a resource attribute, so that judge spend can be grouped by caller downstream. The attribute carries the caller identifier only; it MUST NOT carry the prompt, the subject under judgement or any environment value, per the curated-field rule above.

**A host Claude judgement journals its spend, ending with its final usage.** A host judgement runs its candidate without session persistence, so the agent writes no transcript that a spend reader could consume. Each host model-judgement spawn whose resolved candidate's agent identity is `claude-acp` (a Claude candidate) MUST therefore write a spend journal: one JSON-lines file under `$HOME/.claude/spend-journal/`, named by a session id generated for the launch. Its first line MUST be a header carrying `session_id`, `name`, `cwd`, `started_at`, the first 2,000 characters of the prompt as `first_prompt`, and `"final_usage_line": true`. `name` MUST be `purpose:<caller>@<working directory name>`, with `<caller>` the spawn's `livespec.caller` value, or `host_judgement` when the spawn names none.

The candidate's output is Claude's stream-json event stream: one JSON object per line, of which `assistant` events carry each response and a closing `result` event, when the process reaches it, carries the final usage. Each `assistant` event that carries a message id, a model and a `usage` object MUST be appended as one line, with a `ts` timestamp. When the candidate's stream emits a closing `result` event, the journal's last line MUST be a line of type `result`. It MUST carry that event's `usage` object unchanged, a `message_ids` array listing the message ids of the journal's `assistant` lines in order, and a `ts` timestamp, and it MUST NOT carry a `started_at` key. When the process ends without emitting a `result` event, including a candidate ended by the input bound of §"Dispatcher admission, WIP cap, and post-merge acceptance", the journal's last line MUST be its last `assistant` line. These rules MUST hold whether the launch reads the candidate's output as it streams or after the process exits. Writing the journal MUST NOT fail or alter the judgement.

Scenario 280 in `scenarios.md` exercises the caller labelling of this subsection, and Scenario 332 exercises its spend journal.

### Launch obligations and consumed recovery

Shared semantics MUST come from the canonical required-result, budget, progress-epoch and relay-delivery contracts in this specification: stable obligation identity, canonical required_result and reader, original budget/deadline, epoch, target-effect fulfillment and typed causal changed approach. This contract MUST NOT define a second result enum, independently reset an obligation deadline or equate wait completion with result fulfillment. Local runtime inventory is a projection of that authority. Consumer execution adds generation-fenced claim and execution evidence under the canonical recovery attempt identity, not new satisfaction semantics.

Dispatch/delegation MUST persist intent, session/repository/authorization scope, canonical result/epoch/original deadline and independently verifiable wake/consumer coverage BEFORE reporting a protected launch. It MUST attach the actual gate/run/delegation identity and reconcile crashes between intent and attachment by stable operation id without duplicating the external effect. A missing/unsupported independent recovery owner MUST produce an explicit unmonitored refusal/finding, never a claim of protected launch or completion. An actual owning session leaving its turn with unresolved authorized work MUST remain covered even if it never arms a wait. Supported completion gates MUST verify durable launch obligations and independent producer/consumer registration, preserving any existing stricter supervised Stop rules. Unsupported automatic-hook boundaries MUST be disclosed; independent launch-time registration and the consumer, not an invented hook, provide their coverage. Missing/unreadable authority MUST be unobservable, not no obligations. The inventory MUST cross-check unresolved launch obligations and actual gate/run evidence so missing wait records cannot hide outstanding work.

A protected-host coverage declaration MUST be visible through inventory/check and bind the runtime and version, terminal backend/version and instance, independent service identity and generation, authorized recovery route, maximum observation interval and takeover/launch budget, and installed proof artifact identity. Those measured timing budgets together MUST fit the 60-second bound. A declaration MUST be invalidated when its bound identities or prerequisite coverage change; a PID or self-declaration alone MUST NOT establish verified coverage. This declaration is runtime evidence, not a user-selectable exemption. The released Codex/Herdr positive proof MUST meet the bound; unsupported coverage may only satisfy the explicit refusal control, never that positive assertion.

The existing independently supervised consumer MUST read unresolved canonical result/relay obligations on startup and while the coordinator is idle or gone, regardless of waiter existence or pane notification delivery. Terminal target observation or original deadline expiry MUST schedule actual authorized diagnosis/recovery within 60 seconds on the declared supported host configuration while no valid safety barrier applies. Losing the original coordinator or recovery-owner process MUST be handled by the existing service recovery or authorized takeover path within that bound; a stale consumer is fenced by generation. No new daemon or blind killing/restarting of a non-ready coordinator is licensed. A host whose independent coverage cannot be verified MUST explicitly refuse/report unmonitored coverage, and MUST NOT count that result as autonomous prevention. The overseer repository owns and must ratify its consumer/service realization; this repository owns registration, interoperable consumer execution receipts, action reconciliation and released integration proof.

Notification production, receipt acknowledgement, consumer claim, execution start, execution evidence, resulting next-action reconciliation and target-effect fulfillment MUST be separate durable observations. Receipt or claim alone MUST NOT mark recovery consumed. Successful recovery execution MUST NOT discharge the original result unless the relay-owned authoritative reader establishes fulfillment. The consumer MUST re-read current authority, safety state, result epoch, ledger/forge and the recorded remote factory before selecting a typed sanctioned action. A stale pointer to a completed diagnostic MUST be reconciled; a failed local gate MUST NOT be treated as proof that its remote run or merged PR failed. An expired obligation MUST trigger authorized diagnosis rather than fabricate a human block. A genuine decision outside current authority may still route to a person.

Recovery MUST use the canonical stable attempt id with serialized generation-fenced ownership. Duplicate events, concurrent consumers and restart MUST converge on one observed effect for the supported idempotent recovery command. After an ambiguous execution crash the consumer MUST query durable command effects before retrying, retain unobservable state if it cannot decide, and MUST NOT claim exactly-once arbitrary shell execution. An execution receipt carries causal source evidence, command/action identity, build, attempt identity, start/end observation and resulting effect/next action. A self-declared changed-approach record without an executable attempt and execution evidence MUST NOT reset the original deadline.

A legitimate human HOLD MUST name authority, reason, owner and release condition while retaining the original obligation/deadline history. Running commits/hooks and open Red-Green pairs MUST be visible mutation barriers. The consumer MUST observe and queue recovery without interrupting or abandoning protected work and record the specific barrier kind, authority/release condition where applicable, and observed deferral time within 60 seconds of the failure/expiry trigger. When the actual safety barrier clears, the still-authorized recovery MUST execute within 60 seconds of clearance. Idle state, an ack, prose deadline or stale diagnostic alone MUST NOT count as a HOLD. No boundary may bypass spec/admission valves, interrupt a commit, close another session's pane or break a Red-Green pair to meet a timing bound.

Under the same versioned livespec.orchestrator.session_wait scope, the separate recovery-family event catalog MUST be session.obligation.registered, session.recovery.notification, session.recovery.receipt, session.recovery.claimed, session.recovery.started, session.recovery.executed, session.recovery.deferred, session.recovery.reconciled and session.recovery.coverage. These events MUST carry known opaque identities in session.obligation.id, session.obligation.epoch and session.recovery.attempt_id; UTC strings in session.obligation.deadline and session.observation.time; and curated state in session.recovery.state and session.coverage.state. The numeric fields session.recovery.latency_seconds and session.obligation.overdue_seconds MUST be finite nonnegative numbers, and session.recovery.duplicate_count and session.recovery.fenced_count MUST be nonnegative integers. Unavailable values MUST be omitted with an explicit observation diagnostic, never fabricated as zero. Telemetry MUST include obligation/epoch/original deadline, notification/receipt/claim/execution/next-action identities, coverage and safety state, actual recovery latency, overdue age, duplicate/fencing counts and export degradation as curated typed OTLP events/measurements through the approved existing path. An exporter outage MUST leave local registration, deadline and recovery behavior intact. Honeycomb observation MUST NOT substitute for the authoritative local recovery/result record.


### Released integration proof

Wait/target outcomes such as unknown, gone or unavailable MUST NOT directly satisfy the canonical result; the canonical reader decides satisfied, unsatisfied or unobservable using its own authoritative evidence.

Live Codex/Herdr and Honeycomb proof MUST use the host-captured Proof of Done procedure with a separately started independent replay session. A runnable normally installed released-host scenario MUST exercise real Codex/Herdr turn completion (including FINAL), detached failure and independently executed recovery command, including coordinator idle/gone, absent/dead waiter, dropped notification, owner loss, duplicate events, valid HOLD, active commit/open Red pair and unmonitored refusal controls. Capture MUST measure actual command effect and next action, not just an alert, submitted prompt, ack, claimed lease, changed-approach declaration or a replacement process being alive. Independent replay and Honeycomb identity/latency retrieval with local outage controls are required for plan closure. A filed sibling referral, a merged test alone or report-only attention MUST NOT be presented as autonomous stall prevention.

A Claude Stop hook or a simulated session MUST NOT satisfy the Codex/Herdr incident proof. Other supported runtime results MUST be independently labeled. Missing Codex automatic hooks MUST NOT waive launch-time registration and independent consumption on the Codex no-wait path; if that path is unsupported, the actual incident MUST be disclosed as uncovered and its proof assertion MUST remain unmet.

## Provisional fleet launch scripts

The top-level `fleet-launch/` directory is a PROVISIONAL and EXPERIMENTAL caller-side launch loop: it decides only WHEN a caller invokes `drive --action impl:<item>` or `resume --item <item>`, as §"Dispatcher admission, WIP cap, and post-merge acceptance" permits a caller to do ("A caller MAY add gates of its own for conditions the Dispatcher does not own"). Its shared fleet cap, per-factory FIFO tickets and mutex, hold file, board and in-flight readers are caller-side gates; per §"Host concurrency belongs to the Fabro scheduler" the Dispatcher MUST NOT read, enforce or depend on any of them, and `fleet-launch/` MUST NOT re-implement, pre-empt or stand in for any admission condition the Dispatcher owns.

Every script under `fleet-launch/` MUST open with a banner marking it PROVISIONAL and EXPERIMENTAL that names the livespec console application and the committed launch-loop tool (work-item bd-ib-jr6w7v) as its first-class replacement. Every host-specific value a `fleet-launch/` script reads MUST be assigned in `fleet-launch/config.sh` or in one constants block at the head of a Python script, and each such value MUST be overridable from an environment variable whose name begins with `FLEET_LAUNCH_`, so the scripts can be exercised against stubs. The launcher's bound on how long it waits for a factory slot, `FLEET_LAUNCH_MAX_WAIT_S`, MUST default to 86400 seconds (24 hours) and remains an overridable host value like any other, and a launcher that gives up waiting at that bound MUST log the work-item id it was launching and the queue ticket it held. That log line is the launcher's terminal line, defined below, with the cause `max-wait`.

A `fleet-launch/` launcher MAY gate its launches onto a factory whose node it shares with CI workloads on that node's CPU load. When it does, the gate MUST measure *factory-class pressure*, never whole-host idle. Factory-class pressure is the CPU used over the sample window by two things, as a percentage of the node's CPU capacity:

- pods in the factory namespaces that factory's sandboxes run in;
- the host's `system.slice`, which holds the k3s agent, the Fabro servers and any resident host service.

The measure is chosen by WHAT a workload is, never by its Kubernetes QoS class: CI workflow pods carry no CPU limits, so a burstable or best-effort CI pod can drive whole-host idle to zero without competing with factory pods for the CPU they request.

The threshold MUST be assigned in `fleet-launch/config.sh` and MUST be overridable by a `FLEET_LAUNCH_` environment variable, like every other host value. A launcher MUST treat the factory as green for this gate only when factory-class pressure is at or below the threshold. Above the threshold it MUST hold the launch. A reading that cannot be taken or parsed MUST hold the launch, and MUST NOT be read as green. Every gate decision MUST log the pressure value the launcher used, or `unknown`, together with the threshold.

A `fleet-launch/` impl launcher that holds a per-factory FIFO ticket MUST run its launch-time Definition-of-Done preflight while it is queued behind older tickets, and MUST NOT wait to reach the head of the FIFO before its preflight starts. A preflight pass is reusable for `FLEET_LAUNCH_PREFLIGHT_REUSE_S` seconds, a host value assigned in `fleet-launch/config.sh` and overridable like any other. A launcher that reaches the head of the FIFO holding a reusable pass MUST proceed to that factory's mutex without running the preflight again. A launcher that reaches the head with no pass, or with only a pass older than the reuse window, MUST run the preflight again before it takes the mutex. A failed preflight, whether it ran while queued or at the head, MUST end that launcher without a launch, and the launcher MUST drop its FIFO ticket without taking the mutex. Running the preflight while queued MUST NOT change the order in which queued launchers bind: tickets still bind in FIFO order, and a launcher MUST NOT add any ordering rule beside the FIFO ticket. The per-factory mutex MUST be held only from the binding count to its release, and that release MUST come before `drive --action impl:<item>` starts. A preflight pass is not a hold check: a reused pass MUST NOT stand in for, or let the launcher skip, any hold-file check the launcher makes before `drive --action impl:<item>` starts.

The launch-time preflight a `fleet-launch/` launcher runs is the committed `dev-tooling/dod-preflight.sh`. A launcher MUST NOT substitute a launcher-local copy of it, and that script MUST behave as follows wherever a launcher runs it:

- Run under a tenant credential wrapper that resets PATH, it MUST still resolve the `claude` and `codex` CLIs from the operator's user tool directory and complete its judgement, rather than failing with a command-not-found error.
- It MUST treat a legacy string-form adapter entry, consisting of environment assignments followed by a `claude-agent-acp` command line, as a claude-acp route, and MUST run its judgement rather than refuse the entry.
- It MUST run its Definition-of-Done and drift judges through the configured Codex-first judge chain, so that a Codex pass completes the preflight without a Claude judge call.
- It MUST take the models of its governing-heading, Definition-of-Done and reflector judges from the repository's committed judge configuration, including when the launcher that runs it exports no judge model.

A `fleet-launch/` launcher MAY also launch `resume --item <item>`. A resume launcher is a caller-side launch exactly as an impl launcher is, and it MUST pass through the same caller-side gates before it invokes `resume`:

- It MUST take a ticket on the target factory's FIFO and MUST start only when its ticket is the live head of that FIFO, so impl launchers and resume launchers queued on one factory bind in one ticket order.
- At the head of the FIFO it MUST take that factory's mutex and read the shared fleet count under it. It MUST start the resume only while that count is below the shared fleet cap. Otherwise it MUST release the mutex, keep its ticket, and wait. A count that cannot be read MUST be treated as at the cap.
- Before it releases the mutex to start a resume, it MUST write a fleet in-flight marker that every launcher's fleet count includes until the resumed run lists on its factory board, and it MUST remove that marker when the resume ends.
- It MUST hold while the hold file exists, as an impl launcher does.

A resume launcher MUST NOT run the launch-time Definition-of-Done preflight, because a resume re-enters a run whose item was already admitted. It MUST release the factory's mutex before `resume --item <item>` starts, as an impl launcher releases it before `drive --action impl:<item>` starts.

The committed `fleet-launch/` launchers MUST also enforce the following caller-side gates. Each is a gate on WHEN a launcher invokes `drive --action impl:<item>` or `resume --item <item>`; none of them is an admission decision, and none of them changes any admission condition the Dispatcher owns.

- **Tenant credential wrapper.** A launcher MUST run every launch-time command it runs against its target repository's ledger or Dispatcher under that repository's committed `credential_wrapper`, the argv the `credential_wrapper` key of the target repository's own `.livespec.jsonc` declares. Launch-time commands include the ready-set check, the host-only screen, the capacity projection read, the launch-time Definition-of-Done preflight, any read of the work item's record, every ledger comment the launcher appends, `drive --action impl:<item>` and `resume --item <item>`. A launch into a repository whose `credential_wrapper` names a tenant wrapper MUST therefore receive that tenant's password as its bare `BEADS_DOLT_PASSWORD`, and MUST NOT receive the family password in its place. A tenant wrapper MUST run nested inside the default family wrapper, with `BEADS_DOLT_PASSWORD` unset between the two, so that the tenant wrapper supplies the tenant password while every other variable the family wrapper projects, such as the credentials the launcher's own steps need, stays in the environment. A `credential_wrapper` whose argv names the default family wrapper itself MUST run as declared, without nesting. When the target repository's `.livespec.jsonc` declares no `credential_wrapper`, the launcher MUST use the default wrapper its host value in `fleet-launch/config.sh` names. When the key is present but cannot be read as a non-empty argv array, the launcher MUST NOT fall back to the default wrapper: it MUST make a non-run exit whose terminal line names the work item, its ticket number and the cause `credential-wrapper-unreadable`, and the non-run exit rules below apply. An explicit wrapper override the caller passes MUST still take precedence over both, as it does today.
- **Red-master repository hold.** A *repository hold file* is a file named `hold-repo-<repository>`, where `<repository>` is the basename of the target repository's checkout directory, in the directory a host value in `fleet-launch/config.sh` names. While the repository hold file of its target repository exists, an impl launcher or a resume launcher MUST keep its FIFO ticket, MUST yield the FIFO head to the next live ticket, so that launchers for other repositories bind as if its ticket were not there, and MUST launch nothing into that repository. When the file is removed, the launcher MUST take its FIFO place back, in the order of the ticket it kept.
- **Hold scope by launch kind.** A repository hold file MAY carry one line that begins with `kinds:` followed by a comma-separated list drawn from `dispatch` and `resume`. A launcher MUST apply the hold only to a launch of a listed kind: an impl launcher's launch is kind `dispatch`, and a resume launcher's launch is kind `resume`. A launch of an unlisted kind MUST proceed as if the hold file did not exist. A hold file with no `kinds:` line, or with an empty or unparseable one, MUST hold every launch kind, exactly as before. The kind `dispatch` covers both a fresh dispatch and one the Dispatcher's recovery routing seeds from preserved work, because only the Dispatcher decides between those, and a launcher MUST NOT attempt to tell them apart. A hold file MAY also carry one `reason:` line and one `until:` line, each with free text. Every log line in which a launcher yields to the hold MUST name the hold's `kinds`, and its `reason` and `until` text when present. A per-item exemption that a hold file carries under any rule of this section MUST apply whatever the file's `kinds:` line says.
- **Canary repository hold.** A *canary repository hold file* is a file named `canary-hold-repo-<repository>`, where `<repository>` is the basename of the target repository's checkout directory, in the directory a host value in `fleet-launch/config.sh` names. The *canary exemption list* is a file whose path is a host value in `fleet-launch/config.sh`, holding one work-item id per line. While the canary repository hold file of its target repository exists, an impl launcher or a resume launcher whose work item the canary exemption list does not name MUST keep its FIFO ticket, MUST yield the FIFO head exactly as the "Red-master repository hold" bullet requires, and MUST launch nothing into that repository. When the file is removed, the launcher MUST take its FIFO place back, in the order of the ticket it kept. A launcher whose work item the canary exemption list names MUST NOT be held by the canary repository hold. The launcher MUST read the canary exemption list at every check of the canary repository hold, so that removing a line holds that item again, and an exemption list that is absent or cannot be read MUST exempt no item. The canary repository hold applies to every launch kind; a `kinds:` line has no effect on it. Every log line in which a launcher yields to it MUST name the canary repository hold file and the first line of its contents. The exemption releases a launch only from the canary repository hold. It MUST NOT release a launch from a red-master repository hold, the repository WIP gate, the shared fleet cap, a per-factory cap, the gmktec factory hold or any other gate.
- **Holds re-read at the launch point.** A launcher MUST re-read every hold that applies to its launch (its repository hold file, with that file's `kinds:` scope; its target repository's canary repository hold file, with the canary exemption list; and the gmktec factory hold for a gmktec launch) while it holds the factory launch mutex, immediately before it invokes `drive` or `resume`. If any applicable hold is then set, it MUST release the mutex and its fleet in-flight marker, keep its FIFO ticket, yield, and launch nothing. A hold read only earlier in the launcher's loop, for example at its WIP gate or before its preflight, does NOT satisfy this rule.
- **Holds re-read until admission.** After an impl launcher invokes `drive --action impl:<item>`, and while that drive runs, the launcher MUST re-read every hold that applies to its launch, by the same rules as the launch-point re-read, on every poll it makes while it waits for the launched run to list on its factory board, until the first of these: the work item reads `active` in the ledger, the launched run lists on its factory board, or the drive exits. If an applicable hold is set while the work item still reads `ready`, the launcher MUST stop the drive by sending it TERM before the drive submits a run. It MUST then keep its FIFO ticket at the same ticket number, release any fleet in-flight marker it holds, yield as a held launcher does, and log one line naming the work item, its ticket number and the hold it read, with that hold's `kinds`, `reason` and `until` text when present. A drive stopped under this rule does not trigger the "Early-exit re-ticket" bullet, and the stop is not itself a non-run exit, because the launcher does not exit. Once the work item reads `active`, or the run lists, the launcher MUST NOT stop the drive for any hold, whenever that hold appears; the Dispatcher's own dispositions govern the dispatch from admission onward. After it stops a drive, the launcher MUST re-read the work item's status. If the item then reads `active`, because the drive admitted it before the signal took effect, the launcher MUST make a non-run exit with the cause `stopped-after-admission`, MUST NOT re-take its ticket, and MUST append one ledger comment to the item naming its ticket number and the operator `move` valve as the remedy for its claim, which carries a pending stamp. A status that cannot be read after the stop MUST be treated as `active`. This gate relies on the Dispatcher running every pre-dispatch step of §"Dispatch preflight and post-merge step discipline", including the master-CI preflight's bounded wait, before the admission write that moves the item to `active`; the Dispatcher MUST keep that order. The Dispatcher MUST NOT read any hold for this purpose: stopping the drive is the launcher's caller-side act. A resume launcher is not subject to this bullet, because a resume re-enters a run whose item was already admitted.
- **Repository WIP gate.** Before an impl launcher runs its launch-time Definition-of-Done preflight, it MUST read its target repository's counted-claims count, through the authoritative capacity projection of §"Orchestrator-owned attention facts" → "Capacity single authority", and that repository's configured `wip_cap`. The launcher MUST NOT derive that count from a count of its own of the rows at status `active`. While the counted-claims count is at or above the cap, the launcher MUST keep its FIFO ticket, MUST yield the FIFO head as a held launcher does, and MUST NOT run its launch-time preflight; the obligation above to run the preflight while queued applies only while the count is below the cap. Once the count drops below the cap, the launcher MUST take its FIFO place back, in the order of the ticket it kept. This gate is an early yield, not an admission decision: the Dispatcher still applies its own WIP cap to every `drive --action impl:<item>` the launcher starts, and a launcher whose count cannot be read MUST NOT hold on that unreadable count, because the Dispatcher's own cap still applies.
- **Yielding ticket marked and skipped.** A *yielding ticket* is a live FIFO ticket whose launcher yields the FIFO head under any rule of this section. A launcher that yields the FIFO head MUST mark its own ticket file as yielding by appending one line of the form `held=<cause>`, where `<cause>` names the rule it yields under, while it yields, and MUST remove that line when it takes its FIFO place back. A launcher MUST NOT write a second `held=` line into a ticket that already carries one. A queue reader computing any launcher's place in a FIFO MUST skip over another launcher's live ticket whose file carries a line beginning `held=`, and MUST equally skip one whose file carries a line reading exactly `wip-wait=1`, the marker the dispatcher seat's transitional launcher writes, so that a yielding ticket never blocks a launchable ticket behind it, whichever launcher marked it. A conforming launcher MUST NOT write the `wip-wait=1` form. A skipped ticket MUST keep its ticket number. A launcher MUST NOT skip its own ticket. The marker governs only FIFO order: it MUST NOT change a ticket's number, a dead-pid stall report, or any gate that decides whether the marked launcher itself may launch.
- **Breakage exception.** The repository includes a committed breakage-exception list, the file `fleet-launch/breakage-exception`, holding one work-item id per line; its path is a host value assigned in `fleet-launch/config.sh` and overridable like any other. For a work item that list names, the repository WIP gate MUST treat the cap as one above that repository's `wip_cap`, so the gate does not hold that item while the counted-claims count is below `wip_cap` + 1. The gate MUST hold, at or above `wip_cap`, every work item the list does not name, and the exception MUST NOT raise the shared fleet cap or any per-factory cap. The exception changes only when the launcher stops yielding; it does not change the Dispatcher's own WIP cap, which still applies to the drive the launcher starts.
- **Shared WIP claim-count cache.** The *in-flight addition* of a target repository is the number of that repository's launches already past the FIFO, each marked by a fleet in-flight marker whose launcher process is still running, whose work item is not yet at status `active`; a launcher MUST NOT count its own marker in it.
