The in-flight addition refines the comparison of the repository WIP gate and the breakage exception: where those bullets compare the counted-claims count against the cap, the launcher MUST compare the counted-claims count plus the in-flight addition, so that it holds while that sum is at or above the cap and takes its FIFO place back once the sum drops below it. The in-flight addition is a launcher-side early-yield margin only. The counted-claims count stays the value the capacity projection reports, the launcher is not a capacity authority, and the Dispatcher's own WIP cap, applied to the projection, remains the sole admission authority. The projection read MUST be shared across launchers through a per-repository claim-count cache file, in the directory a host value in `fleet-launch/config.sh` names, holding the projection's count, each counted work item's status, and the time the read was taken. A launcher MUST read that cache file before it spawns any process to compute the count. A cached read younger than the cache time-to-live, a host value assigned in `fleet-launch/config.sh` and overridable like any other, MUST be reused rather than recomputed. A cached read that is older than the time-to-live, absent or unparseable MUST be recomputed through the capacity projection, and that recomputation MUST be serialized per repository, so that when many launchers poll within one time-to-live window the projection read runs once and every other launcher reuses its result. If the recomputation fails, or the per-repository serialization cannot be obtained, the counted-claims count is unreadable and the repository WIP gate's rule for an unreadable count applies: the launcher MUST NOT hold on it, and MUST NOT write a cache file for the failed read. The in-flight addition MUST be recomputed on every gate pass from the cached statuses, never cached. For the same ledger state and the same in-flight markers, the gate MUST compare the same sum with the cache as an uncached computation does; a time-to-live of 0 MUST disable the cache.
- **Host-only screen.** Before it takes a factory launch mutex or runs its launch-time Definition-of-Done preflight, a launcher MUST evaluate the shared factory-safety routing predicate for its work item, the same predicate the Dispatcher's admission valve and the plan child audit's `HOST-ONLY` classification consume (a non-null `factory_safety`, or a declared edit under `.github/workflows/` that no `workflow-scope-override:citation-only` label overrides). The launcher MUST obtain that verdict from the Dispatcher, through `dispatcher.py host-only --repo <path> --item <work-item-id> --json`, and MUST NOT re-implement the predicate in shell. The Dispatcher MUST provide that command, and it MUST print one JSON object carrying `work_item_id`, `host_only` (boolean) and, when `host_only` is true, `reason`. When the verdict is host-only, the launcher MUST make a non-run exit whose terminal line names the work item, its ticket number and the cause `host-only`, MUST NOT re-take its ticket, and MUST append the one ledger comment that "Ready item never silently dropped" prescribes, naming the dropped ticket number and the host-only reason. A command that cannot answer MUST NOT be read as `host_only: false`: the launcher MUST then proceed to its next gate, where the Dispatcher's own refusal still applies. This screen is a caller-side gate under this section's first paragraph; it MUST NOT stand in for the Dispatcher's own host-only refusal, which remains authoritative.
- **Checkout at the origin tip.** Before an impl launcher runs its launch-time Definition-of-Done preflight, and again immediately before any launcher invokes `drive --action impl:<item>` or `resume --item <item>`, the launcher MUST fetch `origin` in its target repository's checkout and bring that checkout to the fetched tip of origin's default branch, the branch the remote's `HEAD` names, which the launcher MUST read with `git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD` and which MUST NOT be assumed to be `master`. A read that names no branch MUST fail the refresh, and the launcher MUST NOT fall back to a literal branch name. It MAY do so by a fast-forward merge. The refresh MUST be serialized per checkout, so that two launchers for one repository never fetch or merge in that checkout at once. A launcher MUST NOT run its preflight and MUST NOT launch when the fetch or the default-branch read fails, when the checkout cannot be fast-forwarded because it is dirty or has diverged, or when its `HEAD` is not then the fetched tip; in each of those cases it MUST make a non-run exit whose terminal line names the work item, its ticket number and the cause `checkout-not-at-origin-tip` with the failing step, and the non-run exit rules below apply. This is a caller-side freshness gate on the checkout the launcher reads; it is not an admission decision.
- **Early-exit re-ticket.** A launcher whose `drive --action impl:<item>` or `resume --item <item>` exits non-zero before the launched run lists on its factory board MUST re-take a FIFO ticket for the same work item, at the same ticket number, and pass every gate again, rather than dropping the item from the queue. A launcher MAY bound how many times it re-takes a ticket for one work item. Before it re-takes the ticket, a launcher MUST wait a delay set by how many consecutive early exits that work item has had with no run listing between them: 0 seconds after the first, 300 seconds after the second, and 600 seconds after the third and each later one. Each of the three delays is a host value assigned in `fleet-launch/config.sh` with those defaults. The launcher MUST persist that count in a per-item state file, under a directory whose path is a host value in `fleet-launch/config.sh`, so that the count survives the launcher's restart, and MUST reset the count to zero when a launched run for that work item lists on its factory board. While it waits, the launcher MUST NOT hold the factory mutex or a fleet in-flight marker, and it MUST yield the FIFO head as a held launcher does. A launcher whose drive reports, in its JSON output, the dispatch stage `goal-minijinja-preflight` with status `failed` MUST NOT re-take its ticket for that exit, because that stage fails identically on every retry until the work item's record is repaired. Unless the drive exited with code `5`, in which case the `refused` rule below applies, the launcher MUST make a non-run exit whose terminal line names the work item, its ticket number and the cause `goal-minijinja-preflight`, and MUST append the one ledger comment that "Ready item never silently dropped" prescribes, naming the dropped ticket number and that cause. That terminal line and that comment MUST NOT carry a goal-template opening delimiter (a left brace followed by a second left brace, a percent sign or a hash sign), so that the launcher's own record of the refusal does not re-poison the work item. When it stops re-taking, it exits without a run, and the rules for a non-run exit below apply, with a cause that names the drive's exit code. A drive or resume that exits with code `5` (§"Dispatcher exit codes": a permanent pre-dispatch refusal) is NOT an early exit for this rule. The launcher MUST NOT re-take its ticket for it, MUST make a non-run exit whose terminal line names the work item, its ticket number and the cause `refused`, and MUST append the one ledger comment that "Ready item never silently dropped" prescribes, naming the dropped ticket number and the refusal line the Dispatcher wrote. Every other non-zero exit before listing, other than one whose drive reports a failed `goal-minijinja-preflight` stage, remains an early exit and MUST still re-take the ticket at the same ticket number, after the delay above.
- **Configured ACP overrides and judge-model environment.** The ACP overrides file is a file whose path is a host value in `fleet-launch/config.sh`. A launcher MUST read it before every `drive --action impl:<item>` it starts and MUST pass each of its lines that is neither empty nor begins with `#` to that drive as one `--acp-node` argument, unchanged and in file order. An absent or empty overrides file MUST add no `--acp-node` argument, so the repository's committed routing governs that dispatch, and the launcher MUST log how many override arguments it passed. The launcher MUST NOT write or edit any repository's committed routing configuration to apply an override. The judge-model environment is three host values in `fleet-launch/config.sh`, one each for `LIVESPEC_DOD_JUDGEMENT_MODEL`, `LIVESPEC_DRIFT_JUDGE_MODEL` and `LIVESPEC_REFLECTOR_MODEL`. A launcher MUST export each of those variables whose host value is non-empty into the environment of every drive it starts, and MUST NOT export one whose host value is empty or unset. That export is a pass-through and carries no model-selection authority: the contracts.md paragraph that begins "Host judgements take the resolved `dod_gate` chain" continues to govern the model of every host judgement, and no consumer that paragraph forbids to take a model from the host's environment MAY read these variables.
- **gmktec factory hold.** While the gmktec factory hold file exists, a launcher MUST hold every launch onto a gmktec factory instance, except a launch this bullet releases. The launcher MUST itself read that hold file's path from its host value in `fleet-launch/config.sh`, overridable like any other, into a variable of its own, and MUST check that path before every gmktec launch; a path assigned only in `fleet-launch/config.sh` that no launcher reads does not satisfy this rule. The *freeze allowlist* is a file whose path is a host value in `fleet-launch/config.sh`, holding one work-item id per line. While the hold file exists:
  - **One-shot allowlist release.** A launcher whose work item the freeze allowlist names MUST NOT be held by the gmktec hold. The launcher MUST read the allowlist at every hold check, so that removing a line holds that item again. When it invokes `drive --action impl:<item>` or `resume --item <item>` for an allowlisted item while the hold file exists, the launcher MUST remove that item's line from the allowlist at that LAUNCH, under the freeze-allowlist lock, a lock file whose path is a host value in `fleet-launch/config.sh`, taken with `flock` by every launcher and by the seat that edits the allowlist, and MUST log the grant with the work item and the time. One allowlist line therefore releases its item exactly once: a later launch of the same item, a re-take after an early exit included, MUST be held as any unlisted item is, unless the allowlist names it again.
  - **Priority-1 release.** A launcher whose work item has priority 1 in the ledger MUST NOT be held by the gmktec hold, and consumes no allowlist line. The launcher MAY read the priority once per launcher. A priority that cannot be read MUST be treated as not priority 1, so the hold applies.
  - **Held queue head skipped.** A launcher computing its place in a gmktec FIFO MUST skip over another launcher's live ticket whose work item the hold holds, exactly as it skips a yielding ticket, so that a held ticket at the head does not block a released ticket behind it. A skipped ticket MUST keep its ticket number and MUST take its FIFO place back when the hold file is removed. A launcher MUST NOT skip its own ticket, and under this rule MUST NOT skip a ticket whose work item the freeze allowlist names; that exception covers only the skip this rule adds, so an allowlisted item's ticket that carries a `held=` or `wip-wait=1` marker for any other rule is still skipped as "Yielding ticket marked and skipped" requires. A queue reader MAY treat another launcher's ticket whose item the allowlist does not name as held without reading that item's priority; a priority-1 ticket so skipped still binds, because its own launcher never skips its own ticket and the factory mutex still serializes every bind.
  The releases above MUST also apply where the "Holds re-read at the launch point" bullet re-reads the gmktec hold under the mutex. They release a launch only from the gmktec factory hold. They MUST NOT release it from a repository hold, the shared fleet cap, a per-factory cap or any other gate, and they change no admission condition the Dispatcher owns.
- **gmktec target and candidate cap.** The *gmktec target setting* selects which gmktec factory instance a gmktec launch goes to: the default instance, or the candidate instance. The launcher MUST read the setting on every gate pass from the location a host value in `fleet-launch/config.sh` names, and MUST select the default instance when the setting is absent or names anything other than the candidate. A launcher whose setting selects the candidate instance MUST launch onto it only while that instance's live run count, read from its factory board, is below the configured candidate cap, a host value read the same way; an absent candidate cap MUST be read as 0, and a live run count that cannot be read MUST hold the launch.

Every committed `fleet-launch/` launcher, impl or resume, MUST account for every exit it makes before its launched run lists on its factory board (a *non-run exit*). A launcher's *ticket number* is the ordering key in its FIFO ticket's file name, the part that fixes its FIFO order. A launcher's *sequence log* is its own standard output, which the caller that starts it captures to a per-launch log file.

- **Terminal line.** On every non-run exit for a trappable cause, a launcher MUST write exactly one terminal line to its sequence log. The line MUST name the work-item id, the ticket number it held (or `none` when it never took one) and the exit cause. The trappable causes include a TERM or INT signal, a hold or WIP yield wait that ends, a ready-set refusal (including a give-up after the bounded retries below), a failed launch-time preflight, a drive or resume that exits before its run lists, and the `max-wait` give-up. The launcher MUST write the terminal line before its exit removes its FIFO ticket file. It MUST also write it before any ledger read or write it makes on that exit, so that an exit cut short after the line still leaves the line. A launcher that is killed by a signal it cannot trap writes no terminal line; that case is covered by the stall report below.
- **Ready item never silently dropped.** A launcher that makes a non-run exit while its work item still reads `ready` in the ledger MUST do one of two things. It either re-takes its FIFO ticket at the same ticket number, or it appends one ledger comment to the work item naming the dropped ticket number and the exit cause. A launcher exiting on a TERM or INT signal MUST NOT re-take its own ticket, because it is ending. It MUST append the comment unless it can establish that a successor launcher already holds a ticket at the same ticket number for that work item; this applies to every signal exit, including a launcher stopped deliberately by the seat that runs the launchers. That comment MUST describe the drop as a dropped or lost ticket. It MUST NOT state or imply that the work item is held by its owner, though it MAY name a repository hold file as the exit cause; a screen that reads ledger comments for owner holds before it issues a ticket would otherwise refuse the item's next ticket. For a signal exit, the comment's cause MUST name the signal and MUST state that the exit was not a run ending. If the comment cannot be appended, the launcher MUST write a second line to its sequence log saying the comment failed and why. The launcher MUST NOT change the work item's status on such an exit.
- **Bounded ready-set retry.** A launcher whose ready-set check refuses its work item MUST NOT exit at once. It MUST re-run that check on each of its next polls, up to `FLEET_LAUNCH_READY_RETRY_POLLS` polls, a host value assigned in `fleet-launch/config.sh` and overridable like any other. While it retries, it MUST keep any FIFO ticket it holds, and MUST NOT hold the factory mutex or a fleet in-flight marker. It MUST yield the FIFO head as a held launcher does. A refusal that clears within those polls MUST let the launcher take its FIFO place back, in the order of the ticket it kept. A launcher that gives up after those polls MUST name the work-item id, the last refusal reason and the number of polls it tried. It MUST do so both in its terminal line and in the ledger comment of the previous bullet, when that comment is owed. The retry asks the Dispatcher's own ready set again; it is not an admission decision, and it does not change any admission condition the Dispatcher owns. When a ready-set check refuses a work item and lists that item's open blockers, it MUST list only those of the item's dependencies whose status is neither `closed` nor `done`, because the beads projection reports a closed item as `done`, and the admit decision MUST NOT change.
- **Dead-pid ticket is a stall.** Any launcher code that reads a per-factory FIFO directory (a *queue reader*) and finds a ticket file whose launcher pid is no longer alive MUST report that ticket as a stall. It MUST write a stall line to its own output naming the work-item id, the ticket number and the dead pid. It MUST do so the first time it finds that ticket, and MUST NOT skip the ticket silently. A queue reader MAY remove the dead ticket after it has reported it, and MUST NOT remove it before.

`just check` MUST run a `check-fleet-launch` target, declared in the justfile's `check:` targets array, that runs shellcheck over every shell script under `fleet-launch/` and runs a hermetic harness. The harness MUST exercise the launcher against stub factory boards and throwaway queue, lock, in-flight and state directories, and its cases MUST cover at least: reading a factory board; refusing a launch when the shared fleet cap is reached; launching two queued tickets in FIFO order; holding a launch while the hold file exists; counting a retired factory's board as zero rather than as unknown; treating a shared factory node as green when CI pods drive whole-host idle down while factory-class pressure is at or below the threshold; holding a launch when factory-class pressure is above the threshold; holding a launch when the node reading cannot be taken or parsed; starting a queued launcher's preflight before an older ticket binds while the older still binds first; reusing a preflight pass younger than `FLEET_LAUNCH_PREFLIGHT_REUSE_S` at the head of the FIFO; holding a launch at the head of the FIFO while the hold file exists even though the launcher's preflight pass is reusable; re-running a stale preflight pass at the head before the mutex; and dropping the FIFO ticket of a launcher whose preflight fails while it is queued, without taking the mutex. A change to a `fleet-launch/` launcher that breaks any of those cases MUST make `just check` exit non-zero. A syntax check alone MUST NOT be treated as satisfying this obligation.

The `check-fleet-launch` harness cases MUST also cover a resume launcher that waits while the fleet count is at the cap and starts once it drops below the cap, and a resume launcher queued behind an impl launcher on the same factory that binds after it.

The `check-fleet-launch` harness cases MUST also cover each of the gates above: an impl launcher and a resume launcher that hold their tickets, yield the FIFO head and launch nothing while their repository's hold file exists, and take their place back once it is removed; an impl launcher that yields the FIFO head without running its preflight while its repository's counted-claims count is at its `wip_cap`, and takes its place back once the count drops below the cap; an item on the breakage-exception list not held at a counted-claims count equal to `wip_cap`, and an unlisted item at the same count held; a launcher whose drive exits before its run lists re-taking a FIFO ticket for the same item; a gmktec launch of an item that is neither allowlisted nor priority 1 held while the gmktec factory hold file exists, with the hold file path the launcher assigns; an allowlisted item that launches once while the hold file exists, its allowlist line removed at that launch, and a second launch of the same item then held; a priority-1 item that launches while the hold file exists without an allowlist line, and an item whose priority cannot be read held; and a held ticket at the head of a gmktec FIFO skipped so that an allowlisted ticket behind it launches, the held ticket keeping its ticket number and taking its place back once the hold file is removed; an impl launcher and a resume launcher that hold their tickets, yield the FIFO head and launch nothing into their repository while its canary repository hold file exists, while a launcher for an item the canary exemption list names launches into that repository, and an unlisted launcher takes its place back once the canary repository hold file is removed; a canary repository hold file created while a launcher holds the factory launch mutex, under which it releases the mutex and launches nothing; a launcher that yields under a repository hold appending exactly one `held=` line to its ticket and removing it when it takes its place back; and a waiting launcher behind another launcher's live ticket marked `held=` and behind one marked `wip-wait=1`, which skips both, binds and launches, while the two marked tickets keep their ticket numbers; and a gmktec launch sent to the instance the gmktec target setting names, launching onto the candidate only while its live run count is below the candidate cap.

The `check-fleet-launch` harness cases MUST also cover the shared WIP claim-count cache: many launchers for one repository polling within one time-to-live window run the projection read once; a cached read older than the time-to-live is recomputed; a launcher's own in-flight marker is excluded from the in-flight addition; a failed recomputation does not hold the launch and writes no cache file; and the cached sum equals the uncached sum for the same ledger state and in-flight markers.

The `check-fleet-launch` harness cases MUST also cover non-run exits. An impl launcher and a resume launcher that each receive TERM while yielding on a repository hold MUST write a terminal line naming the item, the ticket number and the signal before their ticket file is removed. A launcher whose item still reads `ready` at a non-run exit either re-takes its ticket at the same ticket number or appends a ledger comment naming the dropped ticket number and the cause; that comment does not state that the item is held by its owner, and for a signal exit it names the signal and states that the exit was not a run ending. A ready-set refusal that clears within `FLEET_LAUNCH_READY_RETRY_POLLS` polls keeps the launcher's ticket and launches. A refusal that persists past those polls ends with a terminal line and a ledger comment, each naming the last refusal reason and the number of polls tried. A stub dependency the ledger reports as `done` is not listed as an open blocker in the ready-set refusal line. A queue reader that meets a ticket whose launcher pid is dead writes a stall line naming the item, the ticket number and the dead pid before it removes or skips that ticket. Scenario 312 in `scenarios.md` exercises these cases.

The `check-fleet-launch` harness cases MUST also cover the host-only screen and permanent refusals: a launcher whose stub `host-only` verdict is true exits before any mutex or preflight with a `host-only` terminal line and one ledger comment, and re-takes no ticket; a launcher whose stub drive exits `5` re-takes no ticket and leaves a `refused` terminal line and one ledger comment; and a launcher whose stub drive exits `1` before listing still re-takes its ticket at the same ticket number. Scenario 314 in `scenarios.md` exercises these cases.

The `check-fleet-launch` harness cases MUST also cover hold scope by launch kind: a hold file carrying `kinds: dispatch` under which an impl launcher yields and a resume launcher for the same repository launches; a hold file carrying `kinds: resume` under which the reverse holds; and a hold file carrying no `kinds:` line, which holds both, as before. They MUST also cover that a yield line names the `kinds`, `reason` and `until` text, and a repository hold file created after a launcher has passed its WIP gate and while it waits for the mutex: that launcher MUST release the mutex and its in-flight marker without launching, and keep its ticket. Scenario 316 in `scenarios.md` exercises these cases.

The `check-fleet-launch` harness cases MUST also cover the tenant credential wrapper, the origin-tip checkout gate, re-ticket pacing and the configured routing: a stub target repository whose `.livespec.jsonc` names a stub tenant wrapper, under which every launch-time command, `drive` included, runs under that tenant wrapper nested inside the default wrapper, with the family `BEADS_DOLT_PASSWORD` absent from the tenant wrapper's environment; a stub target declaring no `credential_wrapper`, which runs under the default wrapper; a stub target whose `credential_wrapper` is unreadable, which launches nothing and leaves a `credential-wrapper-unreadable` terminal line; a checkout behind a stub origin's default branch, which is fast-forwarded and then launches; a dirty or diverged checkout, and a failing fetch, each of which launches nothing and leaves a `checkout-not-at-origin-tip` terminal line; consecutive early exits of one item that re-take the ticket after the first, second and third configured delays, read through `FLEET_LAUNCH_` overrides; a stub drive whose JSON output reports `goal-minijinja-preflight` failed with exit code `1`, which re-takes no ticket and leaves a `goal-minijinja-preflight` terminal line and one ledger comment that carries no goal-template opening delimiter; an overrides file whose lines each reach the stub drive as one `--acp-node` argument, and an absent overrides file under which the stub drive receives none; and non-empty judge-model host values that reach the stub drive's environment while an empty one is not exported. Scenario 338 in `scenarios.md` exercises these cases.

The `check-fleet-launch` harness cases MUST also cover holds re-read until admission: a hold file created while a stub drive waits before admission, with the item still reading `ready`, under which the launcher stops the drive, no run is submitted, the launcher keeps its ticket at the same ticket number and logs the hold it read; a hold file created after the stub item reads `active`, under which the drive is not stopped and its run lists; no hold file, under which the drive proceeds from launch to listing exactly as before; and a stub item that reads `active` after the stop, under which the launcher makes a `stopped-after-admission` non-run exit, re-takes no ticket and appends one ledger comment naming the `move` valve. Scenario 330 in `scenarios.md` exercises these cases.

Until the deletion the next paragraph requires, every seat that launches factory work through a `fleet-launch/` launcher, the dispatcher seat included, MUST launch every work item through a committed `fleet-launch/` launcher (impl through `dispatch-dual.sh`, resume through `resume-capped.sh`), run from a checkout of this repository in which that launcher is tracked and carries no uncommitted modification. This rule takes effect at the launcher cutover recorded under bd-ib-4xqmqh, once the committed launchers carry every gate the seat's interim launcher runs, the `homelab-worker-arm64` instance's route and fleet count included. Until that cutover the seat's interim launcher runs, and the cutover's canary judges the committed launchers' parity with it. The cutover MUST drain every live interim launcher before the first committed launch, because the interim launcher's queue reader honours only `wip-wait=1` markers and would not skip a ticket a committed launcher marks `held=`. From the cutover on, a seat MUST NOT run, on the dispatching host, a launcher copy kept outside `fleet-launch/`, or a locally modified copy, for any launch. A gate the seat needs that the committed launchers lack MUST land in them through this repository's change path before the seat relies on it.

The directory MUST be deleted once every factory launch on the operator host is made by the livespec console application or by the committed launch-loop tool, and no seat runs a `fleet-launch/` script.

## Expedited incident lifecycle

For an authorized recorded incident only, this section MUST take precedence over conflicting ordinary admission, factory provenance, WIP, reconciliation and completion clauses. It MUST preserve the ordinary policy for every other item and for normal repayment. The incident phase is context on the canonical ledger item, not a second work-item store or lifecycle authority.

The plugin MUST preserve one canonical incident work-item id through repair, revert, corrected attempts, normal factory repayment and later reopening. Each attempt MUST bind its repository, immutable operation id, attempt id, phase/generation, exact base/head, carrier identity (including its real PR once the carrier is `pr-bound`, per §"Carrier identity before and after PR creation"), complete landed commit/tree identities and cumulative original scope. Claim stamps, branch recovery, merged-PR resolution, proof publication, acceptance and closure MUST select that explicit current identity; the first merged branch match, latest title mention, or marker-removal diff alone MUST NOT select it. Existing explicit multi-PR selection work remains a prerequisite; this contract does not replace its general ambiguity refusals.


The sanctioned incident transition MUST publish the following phase and canonical lifecycle-state pair. Host-owned active phases MUST carry the incident owner rather than a factory claim and MUST NOT consume a factory slot. Unknown phase/state combinations MUST produce a named configuration refusal. Only the incident transition may establish these exceptional host phases; flags alone MUST NOT mutate lifecycle state. Ordinary factory admission and acceptance govern the repayment phases.

| Incident phase | Canonical lifecycle state | Transition condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| repair | active | Authorized canonical entry or corrected repair with fresh evidence. |
| master-observation | active | The exact expedited repair carrier merged. |
| reverting | active | A current incident failure requires the recorded inverse recovery. |
| rollback-conflict | blocked | The controller records an owned inverse-patch conflict with its release condition. |
| collecting-failures | active | Revert receipt exists and original failed CI evidence remains incomplete. |
| repayment-admission | pending-approval | Complete normal master CI succeeded and ordinary repayment admission remains owed. |
| repayment-ready | ready | Ordinary admission approved the unchanged incident behavioral Definition of Done. |
| repayment-active | active | One fresh normal factory claim is admitted. |
| repayment-acceptance | acceptance | The current normal repayment carrier merged and awaits final proof. |
| closed | done | All incident completion requirements below are satisfied. |
| drill-closed | done | The `drill-close` action closed a recorded drill. |

Canonical entry MUST preserve the item's original behavioral Definition of Done, or its initially recorded incident behavioral intent until normal grooming authors that section, across all phases. A current attributable regression after closure MUST reopen the same item into reverting, fenced against the closed generation; a completed revert and collected failure evidence permit a new repair phase only with the fresh evidence required below.

Incident entry MUST reuse an existing item or canonically file a minimal identified incident with impact, owner, scope and behavioral intent, recording ordinary model-backed admission and spec debt as deferred to normal repayment. Slow Definition-of-Done/governing-heading judgement, factory capacity, provider probes and green-master preconditions MUST NOT delay that authorized host repair or recorded emergency revert. This is not permission for ordinary implementation to evade admission. A missing tenant MUST use a previously recorded canonical incident id and trusted receipt; it MUST NOT invent a second work-item identity or treat a failed read as absence.

Before local ownership begins, the sanctioned transition MUST record immutable intent, cancel or fence the item's live factory attempt, disarm queued duplicate dispatch and preserve the prior run/claim history. One current generation and operation identity MUST govern writes. Lifecycle mutation exclusion MUST be enforced by a server-side conditional operation available to all tenant writers, never a host-local lock or client read-modify-write. The transition MUST refuse with a named capability error rather than pretend it fenced writers when no such conditional operation is available. Every proof, completion, claim recovery and dispatch effect MUST revalidate current generation immediately before its side effect; a late old run MUST NOT publish proof, consume a claim, merge cleanup or close the item. Recovery intent and receipt reconciliation across tenant failure MUST interoperate with the independently available trusted controller receipt/fence owned by dev-tooling; the plugin MUST reconcile exact receipts back idempotently without creating a second lifecycle truth or requiring the failed tenant to authorize emergency rollback.

A valid incident repair receipt MUST admit only the exact authorized local repair carrier through factory provenance and the retrospective bypass audit; a valid emergency-revert receipt MUST admit only the recorded complete inverse carrier. The receipt MUST record deferred verification honestly and remain distinct from normal factory/TDD proof. Historical validation MUST bind exact PR/head/landed identities after environment and labels disappear. An arbitrary label, caller environment, Factory-Override trailer or code marker alone MUST NOT confer an exception. Workflow-edit authorization remains separately scoped; factory workers MUST retain their existing credential boundary. Normal factory repayment MUST require normal provenance and complete validation.

After the expedited merge's complete normal master CI succeeds, the incident MUST remain unfinished and enter one same-item normal factory repayment. Its eligibility MUST derive from the recorded successful attempt and outstanding repayment, even though an earlier PR already merged. Before dispatch, normal Definition-of-Done and governing-heading admission MUST be completed and deferred spec obligations resolved through their normal owners. No incident execution flag MAY be set before provider selection and before sandbox/hooks/PR execution, including malformed inherited values. The fresh factory run and carrier PR MUST remove the original code/test marker and exercise cumulative original incident paths, relevant tests, deferred validation and spec debt. Acceptance MUST receive that original change/evidence corpus plus follow-up changes, not only marker removal. Cancellation, restart or duplicate delivery MUST resume the same recorded operation rather than create a second repayment run.

A defect found only by deferred factory verification while deployed master remains healthy MUST be repaired in that normal repayment PR without reverting the successful expedited merge solely for the deferred finding. A demonstrated incident-attributable regression on master, another PR or an adopted consumer MUST instead request recovery through the trusted controller and fence stale repayment before a corrected expedited attempt. First-failure recovery semantics belong to the controller contract and MUST NOT be delayed by acceptance classification or ordinary rework budgets. Failed original master runs MUST remain attributable and retained to terminal evidence; a corrected attempt MUST carry fresh repair or measured resolution evidence on the same item, rather than an unchanged reland to retry a broken base.

No accept, reconcile-merged, close/no-change-needed, proof-only resume or automatic completion path MAY discharge an incident from its expedited merge alone. Closure MUST require the current normal factory repayment PR merged, its normal master CI successful, original behavioral proof and manual outcome satisfied, marker removal, repaid spec/verification debt and disposition of related consumer/PR failures. Missing, cancelled or unreadable CI and absent proof MUST remain named outstanding obligations. Incident recovery attempts MUST be accounted separately from ordinary acceptance rework/nonconvergence budgets. Durable incident-to-change attribution MUST survive closure; a later demonstrated related regression MUST reopen the same item, increment/fence the generation and restore recovery plus normal repayment obligations.

A recorded drill MUST be able to end, and it MUST end only through the `drill-close` action of the incident authority writer. `drill-close` is a sanctioned incident transition and the only writer of incident phase `drill-closed`: the `commit-transition` action MUST refuse a `drill-closed` successor with the named reason `incident-drill-close-requires-action`. Before any `drill-close` write, every incident reader, including standing, provenance, closure and inspection readers, MUST be released and verified to accept `drill-closed`, as this section already requires of readers before enablement. The action MUST take the same server-side conditional generation fence and immutable operation identity as every incident transition, MUST revalidate the current generation immediately before it writes, and a same-operation retry after a committed write MUST recover the `drill-closed` result rather than refuse. Before it writes, it MUST establish that the item is a recorded drill from an authenticated forge read of each bound pull request number. Four conditions MUST all hold: the item's incident authority history binds at least one carrier pull request; every distinct carrier in that history, identified by its `target_ref`, is `pr-bound` in its latest snapshot, so a carrier never bound to a pull request, or an attempt with no recorded carrier, fails the test; every bound pull request's base branch, as the forge reports it, matches `incident-scratch/**`; and no attempt landed commit and no recorded revert commit in that history is reachable from `master`. A label such as `incident:drill`, a title, a description or a caller's assertion alone MUST NOT make an item a recorded drill. For a recorded drill at incident phase `repair`, `master-observation`, `reverting`, `rollback-conflict` or `collecting-failures`, the action MUST move the item to `drill-closed`, MUST publish canonical lifecycle state `done` on the item, MUST release the incident owner's claim, and MUST drop any rollback-conflict release condition. Standing, provenance and closure readers MUST then report a `drill-closed` head as a terminal drill closure with no repayment outstanding and no incident completion, and no incident receipt MAY admit a new carrier for it; its historical receipts MUST report no repayment outstanding. For any other item, the action MUST refuse with the named reason `incident-not-a-recorded-drill`, naming the first attempt, carrier or commit that failed the test. When a forge read fails or is incomplete, it MUST refuse with the named reason `incident-drill-evidence-unavailable`. In both refusal cases it MUST write nothing, leaving the item's phase, generation, claim and authority history unchanged. The closure requirements of the preceding paragraph govern incident phase `closed` and do not apply to `drill-closed`. A `drill-closed` item MUST NOT be reported as incident phase `closed`, as a completed repayment or as a completed incident. Neither the reopen requirement of the paragraph after the phase table nor the reopen requirement of the preceding paragraph applies to `drill-closed`: a recovery request or regression reopen against a `drill-closed` item MUST refuse with `incident-reopen-not-eligible`, and a regression attributed to its scratch branch is drill evidence only. Inspection MUST report a `drill-closed` item as a drill closure with its full incident authority history.

Inspection MUST report the item's attempts, owner/generation, current carrier, merge/revert SHAs, CI run identities, skipped work, focused evidence, retained failures, deferred debt, recovery receipts and final normal proof. Readers and installed consumers MUST be released and verified to preserve this context before enablement; developing and adopting this feature MUST use normal gates.

These incident-specific first-authority and pre-PR carrier requirements do not replace the ordinary claim-token protocol under `### Stranded claim release`, admit a duplicate generic ownership project, or claim that its currently accepted residual races satisfy a stronger incident capability. Incident entry delivery belongs to `bd-ib-dzbwaq`; the generic all-writer prerequisite remains `bd-ib-jjws2`, whose claim-token design was ratified in v254 and Scenario 263. These ids explain delivery ownership; runtime behavior MUST NOT depend on their literal values.

### First incident authority publication

A first incident authority is the canonical item's initial immutable incident snapshot together with its one named transition root. Before authorizing an incident hook, host repair or publication, the public canonical writer MUST atomically establish that root, generation, owner and initial phase against the exact expected item/lifecycle/dispatch-claim state. An existing item with no root MUST NOT be initialized by observing absence followed by `bd update --metadata`, an insert-only comment, a fixed-id `bd create`, or a host-scoped lock. A fixed-id create is an upsert and can reopen a closed token; metadata updates are client read-modify-write. Neither is a server-side exclusion. A fresh random root record alone MUST NOT authorize effects before its canonical publication is confirmed.

The writer MUST expose a named `incident-genesis-capability-unavailable` refusal when its installed PUBLIC store capability cannot condition first publication on absent incident authority AND the exact expected claim state in the same server-enforced operation. It MUST write no activation projection or incident effect in that case. A fully migrated existing current-token protocol MAY provide the exclusion only when all applicable writers participate and the provider establishes the required atomic publication semantics; merely calling `bd close` on an unrelated new record or accepting the ordinary protocol's delayed-write residual MUST NOT advertise that capability. The implementation MUST use the public guarded ledger/provider boundary, never a private Beads delegate, direct ungoverned SQL or a host-local authority file. A genuinely new canonical incident may be filed minimally under existing intake policy, but its identity MUST remain the same through initialization and repayment; failure to initialize an existing item MUST NOT cause another incident item to be created.

The immutable initialization request MUST bind schema version, tenant/repository, canonical item id, authorizing principal, immutable operation id, expected absent incident root, expected lifecycle/claim identity, and the complete proposed initial snapshot. A successful reply MUST bind that exact request digest and committed root/generation. The caller MUST read authoritative current state before treating activation as usable. Two hosts racing different operations for one item MUST observe at most one committed initial root; a loser MUST perform no incident effects. Same-operation retry with identical bytes MUST recover the original root and result. Reuse with a different request MUST refuse `incident-operation-conflict`. Timeout, unreadable outcome or an unavailable provider MUST remain unknown until exact operation-receipt lookup establishes committed, confirmed-absent or still-unknown status; an unknown outcome MUST NOT cause another root or blind initialization attempt. Immutable predecessor and operation receipts MUST survive any projection refresh.

### Carrier identity before and after PR creation

Canonical attempt identity MUST represent the carrier as a discriminated state: `branch-reserved`, `head-published`, or `pr-bound`. `branch-reserved` binds the exact repository, fully qualified `refs/heads/...` target ref, authorized base/input parent commit, and current staged tree. It has no PR number. A first local commit MUST validate that current input boundary before its effects; the resulting actual commit id, parent and tree MUST be verified and recorded under the same attempt before push. An autofix or other source/index change MUST obtain a fresh current boundary receipt rather than reusing one for different bytes. This permits a real pre-commit entrance without inventing the future commit SHA or requiring a PR that can only be created after publication.

The first push MUST revalidate current owner/generation and bind the exact authorized commit/tree and target repository/ref. Publication MUST use a compare-and-swap against the recorded remote-ref precondition: confirmed absent for a new branch, or the exact expected prior SHA for a recorded retry/update. It MUST NOT overwrite unrelated branch contents, infer ownership from a matching branch basename, or use an unconstrained force push. Lost publication replies MUST be reconciled by exact repository/ref/head and operation receipt before another effect. `head-published` MUST retain the confirmed remote head and the complete earlier branch reservation; it still has no PR number.

Only an authenticated forge observation of a real PR with that repository, target ref, exact published head and intended base MUST advance the carrier to `pr-bound` with a positive PR number. Zero, a placeholder PR, a guessed next PR number, first branch match or title mention MUST NOT stand in for the observation. A conflicting PR/head/base MUST refuse the binding without replacing the original branch authority. Initial hooks and push may consume only the permissions granted by the current pre-PR state; PR CI, observer arming, merge and post-merge readers MUST require their real `pr-bound` identity and existing independent observer contract. Later states MUST append retained observations rather than rewriting earlier identity/history. Unsupported carrier schema/state MUST produce a named capability/configuration refusal, never normal-mode fallback or an improvised second parser.

A `repair` attempt whose `pr-bound` expedited pull request failed a retained fast check before merge MAY be followed by a corrected `repair` attempt on the same canonical item. The successor MUST be the next generation under a new attempt id and a new operation id, with a fresh `branch-reserved` carrier on a fully qualified `refs/heads/...` target ref different from the failed carrier's, no PR number, no landed identities, and normal repayment still owed. The failed attempt and its `pr-bound` carrier MUST remain in the authority history exactly as recorded: the correction is an appended successor, never a rewrite of the bound carrier, and a `branch-reserved` successor on the failed carrier's own target ref MUST still be refused. Before committing that successor, the writer MUST observe through an authenticated forge read that the attempt's bound pull request is closed and not merged at the carrier's exact head and target ref, and that the operator-named workflow run completed with conclusion failure on that exact bound head. When the forge does not show the pull request closed unmerged at that head, or the named run is unreadable, incomplete, not a failure, or ran on another head, the writer MUST refuse by name and record nothing. The failed run, its head and the closed pull request MUST be retained in the item's recovery record as the corrected attempt's failure evidence and MUST join the item's retained failures. The unchanged-reland rule of §"Expedited incident lifecycle" applies: the correction MUST carry fresh repair or measured-resolution evidence, a repair's head MUST NOT equal any retained failed head, and its evidence MUST NOT reuse a retained failed run.

### Factory transfer and recovery of the initial operation

The initial host takeover of an item that has queued or live factory work MUST win the same server-enforced current-claim transition used by every factory admission, valve, proof, terminal and recovery writer. It MUST durably record the expected prior claim/run and invalidating generation before host effects, prevent queued old admission, and retain cancel/fence intent plus exact receipts. An unobserved cancellation MUST NOT be reported as a canceled run. No stale completion, proof, branch recovery or cleanup publisher may proceed after losing that current generation, even if a delayed ordinary metadata write arrives. Where the installed all-writer capability cannot provide that exclusion, incident entry MUST refuse rather than claiming the factory is fenced. Returning ownership for normal repayment MUST use the same canonical conditional boundary, restore ordinary admission/provenance and retain the host attempt; it MUST NOT manufacture factory proof or reuse a stale factory run.

All these requirements MUST be demonstrated against the installed public provider with independent concurrent clients that share only the server before incident enablement. An in-process mock or same-host lock race alone is insufficient. The proof MUST include first-root races, operation retry after a lost reply, an unobservable outcome, queued/live factory transfer and a late old terminal write; pre-PR commit and first push with no PR record; stale source/tree/ref refusal; forged PR binding refusal; and successful exact PR binding followed by ordinary normal factory repayment. Missing provider capability remains an explicit rollout obligation, not authority granted by the flag.
